Electric Charges and Fields102 questions

Q1CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q1 (NTA Q.No. 391)NTA final key
An electric dipole is placed in an external uniform electric field. The net electric force on the dipole
  1. is always zero
  2. depends on the orientation of the dipole
  3. can never be zero
  4. depends on the dipole moment of the dipole
Concept to recallIn a uniform field the forces qE and −qE cancel: net force zero, torque p × E in general non-zero.
  1. F = qE + (−q)E = 0 for every orientation.
  2. Orientation and p decide only the torque pE sin θ.

Answer: option (1) — is always zero

TrapA non-uniform field is needed for a net force on a dipole.
Q2CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q2 (NTA Q.No. 392)NTA final key
Identify the correct statements from the following :
A. The charge on a body can have any value greater than the charge on an electron or proton.
B. Gauss’s theorem is valid for a closed surface of any shape and for any general charge distribution.
C. The net flux through a closed surface due to a charge lying outside the closed surface is zero.
D. Gauss’s theorem is applicable to any field which obeys the inverse square law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B and C only
  2. A, B and D only
  3. A, B, C and D
  4. B, C and D only
Concept to recallCharge is quantised (q = ne); Gauss’s law holds for any closed surface and any field falling as 1/r2.
  1. A false: charge comes only in whole multiples of e, not “any value”.
  2. B true; C true (field lines from an outside charge enter and leave); D true (gravity has a Gauss law too).

Answer: option (4) — B, C and D only

Q3CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q3 (NTA Q.No. 393)NTA final key
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-ILIST-II
A. E is independent of rI. For a point charge
B. E is inversely proportional to rII. For a short dipole
C. E is inversely proportional to r2III. For a uniform line charge
D. E is inversely proportional to r3IV. For a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
  2. A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
  3. A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
  4. A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
Concept to recallSheet E ∝ r0; line ∝ 1/r; point charge ∝ 1/r2; dipole ∝ 1/r3.
  1. A → IV (sheet), B → III (line), C → I (point), D → II (dipole).

Answer: option (2) — A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

Q4CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q4 (NTA Q.No. 394)NTA final key
A charge q is placed at the center of a line joining two equal positive charges Q. The system of the three charges will be in equilibrium, if q is equal to
  1. −Q2
  2. −Q4
  3. +Q4
  4. +Q2
Concept to recallEvery charge must feel zero net force. The middle charge is balanced by symmetry; an end charge sets q.
  1. Separation 2r; force on one end Q: kQ2/(2r)2 + kQq/r2 = 0.
  2. Q/4 + q = 0 ⇒ q = −Q/4.

Answer: option (2) — −Q4

TrapA positive q would push both end charges outwards; it must attract them.
Q5CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
For an electric dipole in a non-uniform electric field with dipole moment parallel to direction of the field, the force F and torque τ on the dipole respectively are __________.
  1. F = 0, τ = 0
  2. F ≠ 0, τ = 0
  3. F = 0, τ ≠ 0
  4. F ≠ 0, τ ≠ 0
Concept to recallτ = p × E depends only on the angle; a net force needs the field to differ at the two charges (non-uniform).
  1. p parallel to E: τ = pE sin 0° = 0.
  2. Non-uniform field: qE at +q and qE at −q differ, so F ≠ 0 (the dipole is pulled towards the stronger field).

Answer: option (2) — F ≠ 0, τ = 0

Trap“F = 0” holds only in a uniform field.
Q6CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
A negatively charged object A is repelled by another charged object B. However, an object C is attracted to object B. Which of the following is the most probable for the charge of object C?
  1. neutral or negatively charged
  2. negatively charged only
  3. neutral or positively charged
  4. positively charged only
Concept to recallLike charges repel; a charged body attracts both an unlike charge and a neutral body (by induction). Only repulsion proves a charge.
  1. A (negative) is repelled by B, so B is negative.
  2. C is attracted by B: C is positive, or neutral (B induces a positive near side on it).

Answer: option (3) — neutral or positively charged

Trap“Positively charged only” forgets attraction by induction.
Q7CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
Two point charges, q1 = 36 μC and q2 = −9 μC are placed at a distance of 30 cm. What distance from q1, where the net electric field is zero, will be:
  1. 10 cm
  2. 20 cm
  3. 60 cm
  4. 30 cm
Concept to recallFor unlike charges the null point lies outside the pair, on the side of the smaller magnitude: |q1|/(r + x)2 = |q2|/x2.
  1. Let the null point be x beyond q2: 36/(30 + x)2 = 9/x2.
  2. Square roots: 6/(30 + x) = 3/x ⇒ 6x = 90 + 3x ⇒ x = 30 cm.
  3. Distance from q1 = 30 + 30 = 60 cm.

Answer: option (3) — 60 cm

Trap30 cm is the distance from q2, not from q1.
Q8CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived
An infinitely long line charge distribution produces a field of 9 × 104 N C−1 at a distance of 2 cm. The linear charge density of the distribution is:
  1. 0.01 μC m−1
  2. 0.1 μC m−1
  3. 1 μC m−1
  4. 2 μC m−1
Concept to recallGauss’s law for a line charge: E = λ/(2πε0r) = 2kλ/r.
  1. λ = Er/(2k) = (9 × 104)(0.02)/(2 × 9 × 109).
  2. λ = 10−7 C m−1 = 0.1 μC m−1.

Answer: option (2) — 0.1 μC m−1

TrapLeaving r in cm gives 100 times too much.
Q9CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived
A body of 20 g and +50 μC charge is suspended from the ceiling by a string. If a horizontal electric field of 10 kV/m is applied, the angle between the string and vertical direction is: (Take g = 10 N/kg)
  1. tan−1(2.50)
  2. tan−1(3.00)
  3. tan−1(3.50)
  4. sin−1(2.50)
Concept to recallEquilibrium of the bob: T sin θ = qE, T cos θ = mg, so tan θ = qE/mg.
  1. qE = (50 × 10−6)(104) = 0.5 N; mg = (0.02)(10) = 0.2 N.
  2. tan θ = 0.5/0.2 = 2.5, so θ = tan−1(2.50).

Answer: option (1) — tan−1(2.50)

Trapsin−1(2.50) does not exist: a sine cannot exceed 1.
Q10CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
The transfer of integral number of ________ is one of the evidence of quantisation of electric charge. Fill in the blank with the correct answer from the options given below.
  1. photons
  2. nuclei
  3. electrons
  4. neutron
Concept to recallQuantisation: q = ne. Bodies are charged by gaining or losing whole electrons.
  1. Charging by friction or contact moves electrons, and only whole electrons: q = ±ne.

Answer: option (3) — electrons

TrapPhotons and neutrons carry no charge.
Q11CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
A copper ball of density 8.0 g/cc and 1 cm in diameter is immersed in oil of density 0.8 g/cc. The charge on the ball if it remains just suspended in oil in an electric field of intensity 600π V/m acting in the upward direction is __________. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
  1. 2 × 10−6 C
  2. 2 × 10−5 C
  3. 1 × 10−5 C
  4. 1 × 10−6 C
Concept to recallBalance of forces: qE + buoyancy = weight, i.e. qE = V(ρ − σ)g.
  1. V = (4/3)πr3 with r = 0.5 cm = 5 × 10−3 m: V = (π/6) × 10−6 m3.
  2. ρ − σ = 7.2 g/cc = 7200 kg m−3.
  3. q = V(ρ − σ)g/E = (π/6)(10−6)(7200)(10)/(600π) = 2 × 10−5 C.

Answer: option (2) — 2 × 10−5 C

TrapForgetting the buoyant force gives 2.2 × 10−5 C; using the diameter as the radius gives 8 times too much.
Q12CUET 2026 · 15 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
An electric dipole of moment P is placed along the direction of electric field E. The work done in deflecting the dipole through 180° is equal to
  1. PE
  2. +2PE
  3. −2PE
  4. Zero
Concept to recallU(θ) = −pE cos θ; work by an external agent W = Uf − Ui = pE(cos θ1 − cos θ2).
  1. W = pE(cos 0° − cos 180°) = pE(1 + 1) = 2PE.

Answer: option (2) — +2PE

Trap−2PE is the work done by the field, not the work needed to turn the dipole.
Q13CUET 2026 · 15 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
What is the unit of electric flux in terms of the base units of SI?
  1. kg−1 m3 s−3 A−1
  2. kg m3 s3 A−1
  3. kg m3 s−3 A1
  4. kg m3 s−3 A−1
Concept to recallΦE = EA; E = F/q in N/C, and C = A s.
  1. [E] = (kg m s−2)/(A s) = kg m s−3 A−1.
  2. [Φ] = [E] × m2 = kg m3 s−3 A−1 (= V m).

Answer: option (4) — kg m3 s−3 A−1

Q14CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
Two infinite plane parallel sheets, separated by a distance d have equal and opposite uniform charge densities σ. Electric field at a point between the sheets is
  1. σ/2ε0
  2. σ/ε0
  3. zero
  4. depends on the location of the point
Concept to recallOne sheet: E = σ/(2ε0), independent of distance.
  1. Between oppositely charged sheets the two fields point the same way: σ/2ε0 + σ/2ε0 = σ/ε0.
  2. Outside they cancel.

Answer: option (2) — σ/ε0

Q15CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6 also 2026 18 May S2 Q7 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
The nucleus of helium atom contains two protons that are separated by a distance 3.0 × 10−15 m. The magnitude of the electrostatic force that each proton exerts on the other is
  1. 20.6 N
  2. 25.6 N
  3. 15.6 N
  4. 12.6 N
Concept to recallCoulomb: F = kq1q2/r2.
  1. F = (9 × 109)(1.6 × 10−19)2/(3 × 10−15)2
  2. = (9 × 109)(2.56 × 10−38)/(9 × 10−30) = 25.6 N.

Answer: option (2) — 25.6 N

Q16CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7 also 2026 18 May S2 Q8 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
Under the action of a given coulombic force the acceleration of an electron is 2.5 × 1022 m s−2. Then the magnitude of the acceleration of a proton under the action of same force is nearly
  1. 1.6 × 10−19 m s−2
  2. 9.1 × 1031 m s−2
  3. 1.5 × 1019 m s−2
  4. 1.6 × 1027 m s−2
Concept to recallSame force: a ∝ 1/m, so ap = ae(me/mp) = ae/1836.
  1. ap = (2.5 × 1022)(9.1 × 10−31)/(1.67 × 10−27) = 1.36 × 1019 m s−2.
  2. The only option of that order is 1.5 × 1019 m s−2.

Answer: option (3) — 1.5 × 1019 m s−2

NoteThe exact value is 1.36 × 1019 m s−2; the remembered option rounds it to 1.5. Pick the option of the right order of magnitude.
Q17CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8 also 2026 18 May S2 Q9 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
If the charge on an object is doubled then electric field becomes
  1. half
  2. double
  3. unchanged
  4. thrice
Concept to recallField of a point charge E = kq/r2 ∝ q.
  1. At the same point, doubling q doubles E.

Answer: option (2) — double

TrapThe field at a point does not depend on the test charge, but it does depend on the source charge.
Q18CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9 also 2026 18 May S2 Q10 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
Which of the following statements is not true about electric field lines?
  1. Electric field lines start from positive charge and end at negative charge.
  2. Two electric field lines can never cross each other.
  3. Electrostatic field lines do not form any closed loops.
  4. Electric field lines cannot be taken as continuous curve
Concept to recallField lines are continuous curves (in a charge-free region), start on + and end on −, never cross, and form no closed loops (the field is conservative).
  1. The first three are standard properties; field lines are continuous curves, so the last is false.

Answer: option (4) — Electric field lines cannot be taken as continuous curve

Q19CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
Two point charges 8 μC and −2 μC are located at x = 2 cm and x = 4 cm, respectively on the x-axis. The ratio of electric flux due to these charges through two spheres of radii 3 cm and 5 cm with their centers at the origin is ________.
  1. 4 : 1
  2. 3 : 4
  3. 4 : 3
  4. 4 : 5
Concept to recallGauss: Φ = qenclosed/ε0.
  1. Sphere of radius 3 cm encloses only 8 μC; sphere of 5 cm encloses 8 − 2 = 6 μC.
  2. Φ1 : Φ2 = 8 : 6 = 4 : 3.

Answer: option (3) — 4 : 3

Q20CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1worked here
A circular plane sheet of radius 10 cm is placed in a uniform electric field of 5 × 105 N C−1, making an angle of 60° with the field. The electric flux through the sheet is:
  1. 1.36 × 102 N m2 C−1
  2. 1.36 × 104 N m2 C−1
  3. 0.515 × 102 N m2 C−1
  4. 0.515 × 104 N m2 C−1
Concept to recallΦ = EA cos θ, with θ between E and the normal to the sheet. A plane at 60° to E has its normal at 30°.
  1. A = π(0.1)2 = 0.0314 m2; θ = 90° − 60° = 30°.
  2. Φ = (5 × 105)(0.0314)(0.866) = 1.36 × 104 N m2 C−1.

Answer: option (2) — 1.36 × 104 N m2 C−1

TrapUsing cos 60° (angle with the plane) gives 7.85 × 103.
NoteThe site works the flux to 1.36 × 104 and then marks 0.515 × 104, which follows from no reading of the data.
Q21CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Two parallel infinite line charges +λ and −λ are placed with a separation distance R in free space. The net electric field exactly mid-way between the two charges is:
  1. zero
  2. 2λ/(πε0R)
  3. λ/(πε0R)
  4. λ/(2πε0R)
Concept to recallLine charge: E = λ/(2πε0r), away from + and towards −.
  1. At r = R/2 each gives λ/(2πε0(R/2)) = λ/(πε0R).
  2. Between opposite charges both point from + to −: they add to 2λ/(πε0R).

Answer: option (2) — 2λ/(πε0R)

Trapλ/(πε0R) is one line’s field only; “zero” would be for like charges.
Q22CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
An electric dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E. Then
(i) the torque on the dipole is p × E.
(ii) the potential energy of the system is p · E.
(iii) the resultant force on the dipole is zero.
Choose the correct option.
  1. (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct
  2. (i) and (iii) are correct and (ii) is wrong
  3. Only (i) is correct
  4. (i) and (ii) are correct and (iii) is wrong
Concept to recallτ = p × E; U = −p · E; in a uniform field the forces on ±q cancel.
  1. (i) true. (ii) false: U = −p · E (the sign matters). (iii) true.

Answer: option (2) — (i) and (iii) are correct and (ii) is wrong

TrapMissing the minus sign in U = −p · E.
Q23CUET 2026 · 31 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived
Two charges +4 μC and +9 μC are separated by a distance of 3 m in vacuum. The electrostatic force between them is (k = 9 × 109 N m2 C−2)
  1. 0.018 N
  2. 0.036 N
  3. 0.054 N
  4. 0.072 N
Concept to recallCoulomb: F = kq1q2/r2.
  1. F = (9 × 109)(4 × 10−6)(9 × 10−6)/9 = 0.036 N.

Answer: option (2) — 0.036 N

Q24CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q1NTA final key
If the protons and electrons are the only basic charges in the universe, all the observable charges have to be integral multiples of e. Thus, if an object contains x electrons and y protons, the net charge on the object will be
  1. − (x + y) e
  2. (x + y) e
  3. (x − y) e
  4. (y − x) e
Concept to recallCharge is additive and quantised: q = (number of protons − number of electrons) e.
  1. x electrons carry −xe; y protons carry +ye.
  2. Net charge = ye − xe = (y − x) e.

Answer: option (4) — (y − x) e

Trap(x − y) e has the sign reversed: it treats electrons as positive.
Q25CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q5NTA final key
If the net flux through a cube is 1.05 N m2 C−1, what will be the total charge inside the cube? (Given : The permittivity of free space is 8.85 × 10−12 C2 N−1 m−2).
  1. 9.29 × 10−11 C
  2. 9.27 × 10−10 C
  3. 9.22 × 10−6 C
  4. 9.29 × 10−12 C
Concept to recallGauss’s law: Φ = qenc/ε0, whatever the shape of the closed surface.
  1. q = ε0Φ = 8.85 × 10−12 × 1.05 = 9.29 × 10−12 C.

Answer: option (4) — 9.29 × 10−12 C

Q26CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q8NTA final key
Two point charges placed a distance d apart in vacuum exert a force of magnitude F on each other. One of the two charges is doubled. To keep the magnitude of force same the separation between the charges should be changed to
  1. 2d
  2. d/2
  3. √2 d
  4. d/√2
Concept to recallCoulomb’s law: F ∝ q1q2/r2.
  1. F = kq1q2/d2 = k(2q1)q2/d′2.
  2. d′2 = 2d2 ⇒ d′ = √2 d.

Answer: option (3) — √2 d

Trap2d over-corrects: the force goes as 1/r2, not 1/r.
Q27CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q1 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
For a short electric dipole, identify the incorrect statement(s).
  1. (A) The electric field intensity varies inversely with the cube of the distance from the center of the dipole.
  2. (B) The electric field is directed from negative to positive charge.
  3. (C) The electric potential at mid-point of the dipole is zero.
  4. (D) The electric field intensity at mid-point of the dipole is zero.
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
  1. (A) and (C) only
  2. (B) and (D) only
  3. (A) only
  4. (B) only
Concept to recallDipole: E ∝ 1/r3 far away; field lines run from +q to −q; at the mid-point the potentials cancel (V = 0) but the fields add (E ≠ 0).
  1. (A) correct: Eaxial = 2kp/r3, Eeq = kp/r3.
  2. (B) incorrect: electric field lines start on the positive and end on the negative charge.
  3. (C) correct: kq/a + k(−q)/a = 0.
  4. (D) incorrect: at the mid-point both fields point from + towards − and add to 2kq/a2.

Answer: option (2) — (B) and (D) only

TrapV = 0 at the mid-point does not mean E = 0 there.
Q28CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q38 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A point charge of 17.7 μC is placed at a perpendicular distance of 5 cm from the centre of a square. The amount of electric flux going through the square will be: (Given ε0 = 8.85 × 10−12 C2N−1m−2)
  1. 3.33 × 105 N·m2/C
  2. 2.0 × 106 N·m2/C
  3. 4.08 × 106 N·m2/C
  4. 6.4 × 107 N·m2/C
Concept to recallGauss + symmetry: a charge at the centre of a cube sends q/(6ε0) through each face.
  1. Take the square as one face of a cube of side 10 cm with the charge at its centre (5 cm from each face).
  2. Φ = q/(6ε0) = 17.7 × 10−6/(6 × 8.85 × 10−12) = 3.33 × 105 N m2/C.

Answer: option (1) — 3.33 × 105 N·m2/C

NoteAs printed, the side of the square is not stated. The intended problem (NCERT Exercise 1.17) has a square of side 10 cm, i.e. twice the 5 cm distance, which is what makes it a cube face; the answer above assumes that.
Q29CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q5 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
There are two electric charges, Q1 and Q2, placed in vacuum. Identify the correct statements from the following
  1. (A) There will be an electrostatic force between them.

  3. (D) true: 2 × 2 = 4 times.

Q30CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q11worked here

List-I: Physical quantityList-II: Unit
(A) Electric flux(I) V m−1
(B) Polarisation(II) kg m−1s−2
(C) Electric field(III) V m
(D) Energy density(IV) C m−2

Concept to recallFlux = E × area; polarisation = dipole moment per volume; energy density = J m−3.

Q31CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q33worked here
A system has two charges, qA = 5 × 10−7 C and qB = −5 × 10−7 C, located at points A: (0, 0, −10 cm) and B: (0, 0, +10 cm), respectively. Which of the following are true?

  2. (B) Electric field intensity is zero at origin (0, 0, 0)
  3. (C) dipole moment (p) = 5 × 10−8 C m
  4. (D) direction of the dipole moment is along the negative z-axis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (D) only
  2. (A) and (B) only
  3. (A) and (C) only
  4. (A), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallE = kq/r2 for each charge, added as vectors; p = q(2a), directed from −q to +q.
  1. At z = −15 cm: from +q (5 cm) E = 9 × 109 × 5 × 10−7/0.052 = 1.8 × 106 N/C along −z;
  2. from −q (25 cm) E = 7.2 × 104 N/C along +z. Net = 1.73 × 106 N/C. (A) true.
  3. At the origin both fields point towards −q (+z): they add, not cancel. (B) false.
  4. p = 5 × 10−7 × 0.20 = 1 × 10−7 C m. (C) false.
  5. p points from −q (z = +10) to +q (z = −10): along −z. (D) true.

Q33CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q40worked here
A semicircular arc of radius R is charged uniformly and its linear charge density is λ. What will the electric field be at its centre?
  1. λ2πε0R
  2. λ4πε0R
  3. λ2π2ε0R
  4. λ2πRε0
Concept to recallIntegrate dE = kλR dθ/R2; the components along the diameter cancel.

Q34CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q5worked here
A point charge Q is kept at the midpoint of a face of cube of side L. The electric flux emerging from the cube is
  1. zero

  3. 6Qε0−1L2
  4. Q(2ε0)−1
Concept to recallGauss: total flux Q/ε0. Use symmetry to find the share through the cube.

  2. By symmetry each cube gets half: Φ = Q/(2ε0).

Answer: option (4) — Q(2ε0)−1

Q35CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q38worked here

Q41CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q46worked here
Which of the following statements is correct about the effect of the presence of a third charge on Coulomb force between the two charges?

Concept to recallSuperposition: each pairwise force is unaffected by other charges.

Q44CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q22 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q48CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q1NTA final key
Two charged particles, placed at a distance d apart in vacuum, exert a force F on each other. Now, each of the charges is doubled. To keep the force unchanged, the distance between the charges should be changed to __________.
  1. 4d
  2. 2d
  3. d
  4. d/2

Q49CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q3NTA final key
Two large plane parallel sheets shown in the figure have equal but opposite surface charge densities +σ and −σ. A point charge q placed at points P1, P2 and P3 experiences forces F1, F2 and F3 respectively. Then
  1. F1 = 0, F2 = 0, F3 = 0
  2. F1 = 0, F2 ≠ 0, F3 = 0
  3. F1 ≠ 0, F2 ≠ 0, F3 ≠ 0
  4. F1 = 0, F3 ≠ 0, F2 = 0
Concept to recallEach infinite sheet gives a uniform field σ/2ε0 pointing away from (+) or towards (−) it.
  1. Outside the pair the two fields σ/2ε0 are opposite and cancel: F1 = F3 = 0.
  2. Between the sheets they add: E = σ/ε0, so F2 = qσ/ε0 ≠ 0.

Answer: option (2) — F1 = 0, F2 ≠ 0, F3 = 0

Q50CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q33NTA final key
The transfer of integral number of ____________ is one of the evidence of quantization of electric charge.
  1. photons
  2. nuclei
  3. electrons
  4. neutrons
Concept to recallq = ne: charging by friction or contact moves whole electrons.
  1. Bodies are charged by gaining or losing a whole number of electrons, so q = ±ne.

Answer: option (3) — electrons

Q51CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q35NTA final key
A copper ball of density 8.0 g/cc and 1 cm in diameter is immersed in oil of density 0.8 g/cc. The charge on the ball if it remains just suspended in oil in an electric field of intensity 600π V/m acting in the upward direction is ____________. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
  1. 2 × 10−6 C
  2. 2 × 10−5 C
  3. 1 × 10−5 C
  4. 1 × 10−6 C
Concept to recallEquilibrium: qE + buoyancy = weight, i.e. qE = V(ρ − σ)g.
  1. V = (4/3)π(0.5 × 10−2)3 = (π/6) × 10−6 m3.
  2. Net weight = V(8000 − 800)(10) = 72000V = 0.012π N.
  3. q = 0.012π/(600π) = 2 × 10−5 C (positive, since E is upward).

Answer: option (2) — 2 × 10−5 C

TrapIgnoring the buoyancy of the oil gives 2.2 × 10−5 C.
Q52CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q50NTA final key
For an electric dipole in a non-uniform electric field with dipole moment parallel to direction of the field, the force F and torque τ on the dipole respectively are ____________.
  1. F = 0, τ = 0
  2. F ≠ 0, τ = 0
  3. F = 0, τ ≠ 0
  4. F ≠ 0, τ ≠ 0
Concept to recallτ = p × E (zero when p ∥ E); a net force needs a field that differs at the two charges.
  1. p ∥ E ⇒ τ = pE sin 0° = 0.
  2. Non-uniform field: the forces on +q and −q differ, so F ≠ 0.

Answer: option (2) — F ≠ 0, τ = 0

Q56CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q10 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
An electric dipole of dipole moment P is rotated in an electric field of magnitude E from the most stable orientation to most unstable orientation. The work done in the process is:
  1. pE
  2. 2pE
  3. −2pE

Concept to recallU(θ) = −pE cosθ; work done by an external agent = Ufinal − Uinitial.

Q59CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q9 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A molecule of a substance has a permanent electric dipole moment of magnitude 10−31 Cm. A mole of this substance is 100% polarised by applying a strong electrostatic field of magnitude 108 Vm−1. The direction of field is suddenly changed by an angle of 60°. Find the heat released by substance in aligning its dipoles along the new direction of the field.
[Take 1 mole = 6 × 1023 molecules]
  1. −9 J
  2. −3 J
  3. 9 J
  4. 3 J
Concept to recallDipole energy U = −pE cosθ. The energy released when dipoles swing from θ to 0 is pE(1 − cosθ) each.
  1. Total moment P = N p = 6 × 1023 × 10−31 = 6 × 10−8 C m.
  2. Just after the field turns, the dipoles are at 60°: Ui = −PE cos 60°. When realigned: Uf = −PE.
  3. Heat released = Ui − Uf = PE(1 − cos 60°) = 6 × 10−8 × 108 × 0.5 = 3 J.

Answer: option (4) — 3 J

Trap−3 J is the change in potential energy; the heat released is positive.
NoteThe paper prints “changed by all angle of 60°”, read as “an angle”.
Q60CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q23 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q65CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q3 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A thin metallic spherical shell contains a charge +10 μC on it. A point charge +2 μC is placed at the centre of the shell and another charge +5 μC is placed outside it as shown. The force on the charge +2 μC at the centre is:

Concept to recallElectrostatic shielding: the cavity of a conductor is screened from charges outside it; a uniform shell gives no field inside.

  2. The +2 μC at the centre is acted on by no net field: F = 0.

Q67CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q39 · Prepp reconstructionworked here

(C) In a uniform electric field E, an electric dipole experiences a torque and a net force F.

(E) If the uniform surface charge density of an infinite plane sheet is positive, the electric field is directed away from the plate.

  2. (A), (C) and (D) only

  4. (A), (B) and (C) only
Concept to recallA dipole in a uniform field: forces +qE and −qE cancel (net force 0) but form a couple (torque pE sinθ).

NotePrepp's unofficial key gives option (2); the working above shows why that cannot be right. That choice includes C, which is false, and omits B and E, which are true.

Q83CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q21key re-derived

  1. on the surface of the sphere

  4. 1.8 × 10−12 m s−2
Concept to recallBetween plates E = V/d; acceleration a = eE/m.
  1. E = 6000/0.06 = 1 × 105 V m−1.
  2. a = (1.6 × 10−19 × 105)/(9.1 × 10−31) = 1.76 × 1016 m s−2.

Answer: option (2) — 1.76 × 1016 m s−2

TrapUsing d = 6 instead of 0.06 m gives 1014.
Q94CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q1NTA final key
Choose the correct statements from the following:
A. The total charge in any isolated system remains constant.
B. When some charge is transferred to a conductor, its stays at the same place without getting distributed over the entire surface.
C. One Coulomb of negative charge is the total charge of 6.25 × 1018 electrons.
D. Electric field is a scalar field.
E. Permanent dipole means that the dipole moment p exists irrespective of external electric field E
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B, C, D and E only
  2. A, D and E only
  3. B and D only
  4. A, C and E only
Concept to recallCharge is conserved and quantised (q = ne); on a conductor charge spreads over the surface; E is a vector field.
  1. A true (conservation). B false (charge spreads over a conductor’s surface).
  2. C true: 1/(1.6 × 10−19) = 6.25 × 1018. D false (vector field). E true. So A, C, E.

Answer: option (4) — A, C and E only

Q95CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q2NTA final key
Choose the correct alternative from the following:
  1. Gauss law is true for any open surface.
  2. Gauss law includes the sum of all charges enclosed by the surface for calculation of electric flux through the surface.
  3. Gauss law can be used to calculate the magnetic field due to steady current.
  4. Gauss law is not based on the inverse square dependence on distance contained in the Coloumb’s law.
Concept to recall∮E·dA = qenc/ε0 over a closed surface; it follows from the 1/r2 law.
  1. Gauss’s law needs a closed surface and uses the net enclosed charge: option 2.
  2. Magnetic field of currents comes from Ampere’s/Biot–Savart law; Gauss’s law relies on the inverse-square law.

Answer: option (2) — Gauss law includes the sum of all charges enclosed by the surface for calculation of electric flux through the surface.

Q96CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q3NTA final key
Choose the correct answer from the following:
If three charged particles are collinear and are in equilibrium, then:
  1. all the charged particles have equal charge.
  2. all the charged particles have the same sign and the distances between two consecutive charged particles are same.
  3. all the charged particles have the same sign
  4. all the charged particles cannot have the same sign
Concept to recallFor every charge to be in equilibrium, each must feel equal and opposite pushes and pulls.
  1. If all three had the same sign, each end charge would be repelled by both others in the same direction: no equilibrium.
  2. So the middle charge must be of opposite sign: they cannot all have the same sign.

Answer: option (4) — all the charged particles cannot have the same sign

Q97CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q5NTA final key
The electric field intensity due to an infinite thin plane sheet of surface charge density σ is:
  1. +σε0
  2. σ2ε0
  3. −σε0
  4. −2σε0
Concept to recallGauss’s law with a pill-box through the sheet: 2EA = σA/ε0.
  1. Flux leaves through both faces: 2EA = σA/ε0, so E = σ/2ε0.

Answer: option (2) — σ2ε0

Trapσ/ε0 is the field just outside a conductor (or between two oppositely charged sheets).
Q98CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q1NTA final key
An infinitely long wire is charged uniformly with charge density λ and placed in air, the electric field at distance r from wire will be :
  1. 14πε0 λr
  2. 14πε0 λr2
  3. λ2ε0
  4. λ2πε0r
Concept to recallGauss’s law with a coaxial cylinder: only the curved surface carries flux.
  1. Flux through the curved surface: E(2πrL).
  2. Charge enclosed: λL, so E(2πrL) = λL/ε0.
  3. E = λ/(2πε0r), falling as 1/r.

Answer: option (4) — λ2πε0r

Trapλ/2ε0 is the field of an infinite sheet (with σ), not a line.
Q99CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q2NTA final key
Two point charges (−q) and (+4q) are placed at separation ‘r’. Where should a third charge be placed so that entire system of charges becomes in equilibrium ?
  1. at separation ‘r’ from (−q) on the extreme side of −q.
  2. at separation ‘r’ from (4q) on the extreme side of 4q.
  3. at separation r2 from (−q) in between the two charges.
  4. at separation r4 from (4q) in between the two charges.
Concept to recallFor unlike charges the null point lies outside, on the side of the smaller charge; balance k q1/x12 = k q2/x22.
  1. Between unlike charges both forces on a test charge point the same way, so it must be outside, nearer the smaller charge (−q).
  2. At distance x beyond −q: q/x2 = 4q/(x + r)2 ⇒ x + r = 2x ⇒ x = r.
  3. Choosing the third charge as +4q makes the forces on the other two balance as well, so the whole system can be in equilibrium.

Answer: option (1) — at separation ‘r’ from (−q) on the extreme side of −q.

TrapPlacing it between the charges works only for like charges.
Q100CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q3NTA final key
The variation of electric field with respect to distance from centre of a charged conducting spherical shell of radius R is given by :
Concept to recallCharged conducting shell: E = 0 inside (r < R); E = kQ/r2 for r ≥ R.
  1. Inside, the Gaussian sphere encloses no charge, so E = 0 for r < R.
  2. At r = R the field jumps to kQ/R2, then falls as 1/r2.
  3. Only graph (2) is zero inside and decays from R onwards.

Answer: option (2) —

TrapGraph (3), rising linearly inside, is a uniformly charged solid (non-conducting) sphere.
Q101CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q4NTA final key
A conducting sphere is charged. If the electric field at a distance 20 cm from the centre of the sphere is 1.2 × 103 NC−1 and points radially inwards, the net charge on the sphere is :
  1. 4.5 × 109 C
  2. −4.5 × 10−9 C
  3. 1.7 × 109 C
  4. −5.3 × 10−9 C
Concept to recallOutside a sphere E = kq/r2; a field pointing inwards means negative charge.
  1. |q| = E r2/k = (1.2 × 103)(0.2)2/(9 × 109).
  2. |q| = 48/(9 × 109) = 5.3 × 10−9 C.
  3. Inward field ⇒ q = −5.3 × 10−9 C.

Answer: option (4) — −5.3 × 10−9 C

TrapUsing r = 20 instead of 0.20 m, or forgetting the sign.
Q102CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q6NTA final key
The expression for torque ‘τ’ experienced by an electric dipole of dipole moment ‘P’ in an external uniform electric field ‘E’ is given by :
  1. τ = P·E
  2. τ = PE
  3. τ = EP
  4. τ = P × E
Concept to recallTorque on a dipole: τ = pE sinθ, a vector perpendicular to both p and E.
  1. The two forces ±qE form a couple of arm 2a sinθ: τ = pE sinθ.
  2. As a vector: τ = p × E.

Answer: option (4) — τ = P × E

TrapThe dot product p·E appears in the potential energy U = −p·E, not in the torque.

Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance94 questions

Q103CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q5 (NTA Q.No. 395)NTA final key
A metal wire is bent in the shape of a circle of 10 cm radius. It is given a charge of 200 μC which spreads on it uniformly. The electric potential at its center is
  1. 3 × 106 V
  2. 6 × 106 V
  3. 9 × 106 V
  4. 18 × 106 V
Concept to recallEvery element of a ring is at the same distance R from the centre: V = kQ/R (potential is a scalar, no cancellation).
  1. V = 9 × 109 × 200 × 10−6/0.1 = 1.8 × 107 V = 18 × 106 V.

Answer: option (4) — 18 × 106 V

TrapThe field at the centre is zero; the potential is not.
Q104CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q6 (NTA Q.No. 396)NTA final key
Three capacitors of equal capacitance, when connected in series have net capacitance C1 and when connected in parallel have net capacitance C2. The ratio of C1 and C2 is
  1. 13
  2. 3
  3. 19
  4. 9
Concept to recalln equal capacitors: series C/n, parallel nC.
  1. C1 = C/3, C2 = 3C.
  2. C1/C2 = 1/9.

Answer: option (3) — 19

Q105CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q7 (NTA Q.No. 397)NTA final key
A 800 pF capacitor is charged by a 100 V battery. After some time, the battery is disconnected. The capacitor is then connected across another 800 pF capacitor. The electrostatic energy stored in the combination will be
  1. 2 × 10−6 J
  2. 3.8 × 10−6 J
  3. 4.2 × 10−6 J
  4. 6 × 106 J
Concept to recallCharge is conserved when an isolated capacitor shares charge; energy Q2/2C.
  1. Q = 800 × 10−12 × 100 = 8 × 10−8 C; initial U = ½CV2 = 4 × 10−6 J.
  2. Combined C = 1600 pF, same Q: U = Q2/2(1600 pF) = 2 × 10−6 J.
  3. Half the energy is lost as heat and radiation while charge flows.

Answer: option (1) — 2 × 10−6 J

Q106CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1 also 2026 29 May S1 Q5 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
A network of five capacitors is shown in the figure. The total charge stored in the network connected between A and B is:
  1. 8 μC
  2. 10 μC
  3. 9 mC
  4. 10 mC
Concept to recallA capacitor bridge is balanced when C1/C2 = C3/C4; the middle capacitor then holds no charge and can be removed.
  1. Upper arms 4 and 2, lower arms 6 and 3: 4/2 = 6/3 = 2, so the bridge is balanced and the 5 μF drops out.
  2. Upper branch: 4 and 2 in series = 4×2/6 = 4/3 μF. Lower branch: 6 and 3 in series = 2 μF.
  3. Parallel: C = 4/3 + 2 = 10/3 μF.
  4. Q = CV = (10/3)(3) = 10 μC.

Answer: option (2) — 10 μC

TrapThe options mix μC and mC: 10 mC is the right digits in the wrong unit.
Q107CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
In a certain region, a uniform electric field exists in the positive x-direction. Let VA = potential at (0, 0, 0) cm, VB = potential at (5, 0, 0) cm and VC = potential at (0, 5, 0) cm. The correct relationship between them is:
  1. VA < VC and VA = VB
  2. VA = VC and VA > VB
  3. VA > VC and VA = VB
  4. VA = VC and VA < VB
Concept to recallPotential falls along the field (dV = −E dx); planes perpendicular to a uniform field are equipotentials.
  1. B is 5 cm further along +x, the field direction: VB = VA − E(0.05) < VA.
  2. C differs from A only in y, perpendicular to E: same equipotential plane, VC = VA.

Answer: option (2) — VA = VC and VA > VB

TrapMoving along E lowers the potential; moving across E changes nothing.
Q108CUET 2026 · 12 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
When a slab of insulating material 4 mm thick is introduced between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of separation 4 mm, it is found that the distance between the plates has to be increased by 3.2 mm to restore the capacity to its original value. The dielectric constant of the material is __________.
  1. 2
  2. 5
  3. 3
  4. 7
Concept to recallA slab of thickness t behaves like air of thickness t/K, so it “removes” t(1 − 1/K) of gap.
  1. Extra separation needed = t(1 − 1/K): 3.2 = 4(1 − 1/K).
  2. 1 − 1/K = 0.8 ⇒ 1/K = 0.2 ⇒ K = 5.

Answer: option (2) — 5

Q109CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Consider a parallel plate capacitor of area A of each plate and separation d between the plates. If E is the electric field and ε0 is the permittivity of free space between the plates, then potential energy stored in the capacitor is:
  1. ½ε0E2Ad
  2. ¾ε0E2Ad
  3. ¼ε0E2Ad
  4. ε0E2Ad
Concept to recallEnergy density u = ½ε0E2; the field fills volume Ad.
  1. U = u × volume = ½ε0E2 × Ad.
  2. Check: ½CV2 = ½(ε0A/d)(Ed)2 = ½ε0E2Ad.

Answer: option (1) — ½ε0E2Ad

Q110CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 1 μF is charged to a potential difference of 20 V. The distance between plates is 1 μm. The energy density between plates of capacitor is:
  1. 1.8 × 103 J/m3
  2. 2 × 103 J/m3
  3. 2 × 102 J/m3
  4. 1.8 × 105 J/m3
Concept to recallu = ½ε0E2 with E = V/d. (The capacitance is not needed.)
  1. E = V/d = 20/10−6 = 2 × 107 V/m.
  2. u = ½(8.85 × 10−12)(4 × 1014) = 1.77 × 103 ≈ 1.8 × 103 J/m3.

Answer: option (1) — 1.8 × 103 J/m3

TrapThe 1 μF is a distractor: energy density depends only on E.
Q111CUET 2026 · 15 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
A parallel plate capacitor with air between the plates has a capacitance of 6 pF. What will be the capacitance if the distance between the plates is reduced to half and the space between them is filled with a substance of dielectric constant 5?
  1. 30 pF
  2. 60 pF
  3. 15 pF
  4. 120 pF
Concept to recallC = Kε0A/d.
  1. Halving d doubles C; K = 5 multiplies by 5: C = 6 × 2 × 5 = 60 pF.

Answer: option (2) — 60 pF

Q112CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
The dimensional formula of capacitance is:
  1. [M−1L−2T4A2]
  2. [ML2T−2A−2]
  3. [M−1L−1T3A]
  4. [MLT−3A−1]
Concept to recallC = Q/V; [Q] = AT, [V] = W/Q = ML2T−3A−1.
  1. [C] = AT/(ML2T−3A−1) = M−1L−2T4A2.

Answer: option (1) — [M−1L−2T4A2]

Q113CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: In electrostatics, a conductor does not store any net charge inside.
Reason R: Inside the capacitor (with no dielectric medium), the free charge carriers, if placed between the plates of capacitor, experience force and drift.
  1. Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
  2. Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
  3. A is true but R is false
  4. A is false but R is true
Concept to recallIn electrostatic equilibrium E = 0 inside a conductor, so by Gauss’s law no net charge resides inside: it sits on the surface.
  1. A is true (E = 0 inside ⇒ ρ = 0 inside).
  2. R is true: between capacitor plates E ≠ 0, so free charges feel qE and drift.
  3. But R is about the gap of a capacitor, not the interior of a conductor, so it does not explain A.

Answer: option (2) — Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

Q114CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
A parallel plate capacitor having area A and separated by distance d is filled by a copper plate of thickness b. The new capacity is:
  1. ε0A/(d + b/2)
  2. ε0A/2d
  3. ε0A/(d − b)
  4. 2ε0A/(d + b/2)
Concept to recallA metal slab has E = 0 inside (K → ∞), so it simply removes thickness b from the gap.
  1. C = ε0A/(d − b + b/K) with K → ∞: C = ε0A/(d − b).

Answer: option (3) — ε0A/(d − b)

Q115CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived
A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 5 μF and plate separation 6 cm is connected to a 1 V battery and charged. A dielectric of dielectric constant 4 and thickness 4 cm is introduced between the plates of the capacitor. The additional charge that flows into the capacitor from the battery is:
  1. 2 μC
  2. 3 μC
  3. 5 μC
  4. 10 μC
Concept to recallC = ε0A/(d − t + t/K); with the battery connected V stays fixed and ΔQ = VΔC.
  1. Effective gap = 6 − 4 + 4/4 = 3 cm, half the original 6 cm, so C doubles to 10 μF.
  2. Q rises from 5 μC to 10 μC: extra 5 μC flows in.

Answer: option (3) — 5 μC

Trap10 μC is the final charge, not the extra charge.
Q116CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived
A slab of material of dielectric constant K has the same area A as the plates of a parallel plate capacitor, and has thickness (3/4)d, where d is the separation of the plates. The capacitance when the slab is inserted between the plates is:
  1. (ε0A/d)(K + 3)/(4K)
  2. (ε0A/d)(2K/(K + 3))
  3. (ε0A/d)(K/(K + 3))
  4. (ε0A/d)(4K/(K + 3))
Concept to recallC = ε0A/(d − t + t/K).
  1. d − 3d/4 + 3d/(4K) = (d/4)(1 + 3/K) = d(K + 3)/(4K).
  2. C = (ε0A/d) · 4K/(K + 3).

Answer: option (4) — (ε0A/d)(4K/(K + 3))

Q117CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived
Four capacitors are connected as shown in the figure. If C1 = 2 μF, C2 = 3 μF, C3 = 5 μF and C4 = 10 μF, then the equivalent capacitance between points A and B is:
  1. 20 μF
  2. 5 μF
  3. 10 μF
  4. 0 μF
Concept to recallParallel capacitors add; series combine as reciprocals.
  1. C1, C2, C3 in parallel: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 μF.
  2. In series with C4 = 10 μF: 10 × 10/20 = 5 μF.

Answer: option (2) — 5 μF

Q118CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Four capacitors are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. The effective capacitance between P and Q is:
  1. 10 μF
  2. 5 μF
  3. 2 μF
  4. 7.5 μF
Concept to recallReduce from the inside out: parallel pairs first, then series, then the outer parallel branch.
  1. 2 + 2 = 4 μF; in series with 12 μF: 4 × 12/16 = 3 μF.
  2. In parallel with the lower 2 μF: 3 + 2 = 5 μF.

Answer: option (2) — 5 μF

Q119CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
In the figure given below, the resultant capacitance between points A and B is:
  1. 20 μF
  2. 20/3 μF
  3. 40/3 μF
  4. 10 μF
Concept to recallLabel the junctions and look for a Wheatstone bridge: balanced when CAX/CXB = CAY/CYB.
  1. Junctions: A–X 10, X–B 20, A–Y 20, Y–B 40, with the 5 μF across X–Y.
  2. 10/20 = 20/40: balanced, so the 5 μF carries no charge.
  3. Branches: 10 and 20 in series = 20/3; 20 and 40 in series = 40/3; total 60/3 = 20 μF.

Answer: option (1) — 20 μF

Q120CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
Three capacitors have capacitances 2 μF, 4 μF and 8 μF. When they are connected in a way to give minimum capacitance, their effective capacitance is:
  1. 8 μF

Concept to recallSeries gives the minimum (less than the smallest); parallel gives the maximum.

Q121CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived

Q122CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived

Q123CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
Two capacitors of capacitances 6 μF and 3 μF are connected in series across a battery. The equivalent capacitance of the combination is

Q124CUET 2026 · labelled 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain; no answers printed) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8worked here

Q125CUET 2026 · file dated 6 June, headed 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived

Q126CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q2NTA final key
A charge of magnitude 3 × 10−7 C is located at a distance of 0.09 m from a point P. Obtain the work done in bringing a charge of 2 × 10−9 C from infinity to the point P.
  1. 6 × 104 J
  2. 6 × 10−2 J
  3. 6 × 10−5 J
  4. 6 × 105 J
Concept to recallW∞→P = qVP, with VP = kQ/r and V(∞) = 0.
  1. VP = 9 × 109 × 3 × 10−7 / 0.09 = 3 × 104 V.
  2. W = qVP = 2 × 10−9 × 3 × 104 = 6 × 10−5 J.

Answer: option (3) — 6 × 10−5 J

Q127CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q3NTA final key
In a series combination of capacitors connected across a battery
  1. each capacitor has an equal charge for certain values of capacitances only
  2. each capacitor has different charge for a certain value of its capacitance
  3. each capacitor has equal charge for any value of its capacitance
  4. each capacitor has different charge for any value of its capacitance
Concept to recallSeries capacitors: the same charge Q on every capacitor (charge on the isolated inner plates is conserved); the voltages divide as Vi = Q/Ci.
  1. The battery puts +Q on the first plate; induction puts −Q, +Q, −Q … on the following plates.
  2. Each inner plate pair is an isolated conductor with zero net charge, so every capacitor holds the same Q, whatever its capacitance.

Answer: option (3) — each capacitor has equal charge for any value of its capacitance

Q128CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q4NTA final key
Two point charges, 4 μC and −3 μC (with no external field) are placed at (−6 cm, 0, 0) and (6 cm, 0, 0), respectively. The amount of work required to separate the two charges infinitely away from each other will be
  1. 0.9 J
  2. 0.18 J
  3. −0.9 J
  4. −0.018 J
Concept to recallU = kq1q2/r; work needed to separate to infinity = Uf − Ui = −Ui.
  1. r = 6 − (−6) = 12 cm = 0.12 m.
  2. Ui = 9 × 109 × (4 × 10−6)(−3 × 10−6)/0.12 = −0.9 J.
  3. W = 0 − (−0.9) = +0.9 J (positive: the charges attract, so work must be supplied).

Answer: option (1) — 0.9 J

Trap−0.9 J is the potential energy itself, not the work needed to pull the charges apart.
Q129CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q6NTA final key
A parallel plate capacitor having plate area 200 cm2 and separation 2.0 mm holds a charge of 0.06 μC on applying a potential difference of 60 V. The dielectric constant of the material filled in between the plates is.
  1. 0.113
  2. 1.13
  3. 11.3
  4. 113
Concept to recallC = Q/V and C = Kε0A/d, so K = Cd/(ε0A).
  1. C = 0.06 × 10−6/60 = 1.0 × 10−9 F.
  2. K = (10−9 × 2 × 10−3)/(8.85 × 10−12 × 200 × 10−4) = 11.3.

Q130CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q7NTA final key
The electric potential due to an electric dipole
  1. (A) depends on r, where r is the magnitude of position vector r
  2. (B) depends on the angle between the position vector r and the dipole moment vector p
  3. (C) falls off at long distances, as 1/r2
  4. (D) does not depend upon the distance separating the charges
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

  3. V ∝ p = q(2a), so it does depend on the separation 2a of the charges: (D) false.

Trap(D) would be true only if p were held fixed; as stated (separation of the charges) it is false.

Q166CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q44 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following statement is NOT true, when two capacitors charged to different potential are connected in parallel by a conducting wire?

  2. The charge lost by one is equal to the charge gained by the other
  3. Both the capacitors acquire a common potential

Concept to recallSharing charge: total charge conserved, common potential V = (C1V1 + C2V2)/(C1 + C2), energy lost as heat.
  1. Charge, not potential, is conserved: C1ΔV1 = C2ΔV2.
  2. The potential changes are equal only if C1 = C2; statement (4) is not true in general.

Answer: option (4) — The potential lost by one is equal to the potential gained by the other

Q167CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key
A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacity ‘C’, distance of separation between its plates is ‘x’ and potential difference applied across the plates is V. What is the force of attraction between the plates of the parallel plate air capacitor?
  1. C2V22x2
  2. CV2x
  3. C2V22x
  4. CV22x
Concept to recallEach plate sits in the field of the other, σ/2ε0: F = Q2/(2ε0A).
  1. F = Q2/(2ε0A) with Q = CV and ε0A = Cx.
  2. F = C2V2/(2Cx) = CV2/(2x).

Answer: option (4) — CV22x

TrapCV2/x uses the full field σ/ε0 instead of the field of one plate.
Q168CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q42NTA final key
When a number of capacitors are connected in parallel between two points increases, the equivalent capacitance
  1. Decreases
  2. Increases
  3. Remains the same
  4. Zero
Concept to recallParallel: C = C1 + C2 + …
  1. Each added capacitor adds its capacitance, so the total increases.

Answer: option (2) — Increases

Q169CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q50NTA final key

Q170CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q14 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. 5 A
  3. 5 × 106 A
  4. Zero
Concept to recallIn steady DC a capacitor is an open circuit (XC = 1/ωC → ∞ as ω → 0).

  2. Steady current = 0.

Q171CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q20 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A slab of material of dielectric constant k has the same area as the plates of a parallel plate capacitor, but has a thickness 3d/4, where d is the distance between plates of capacitor. The ratio of the capacitance with dielectric inside it to its capacitance without the dielectric is:
  1. 3k/(k + 4)
  2. 4k/(k + 3)
  3. 5k/(k + 2)
  4. k/(k + 3)
Concept to recallSlab of thickness t: C = ε0A/[d − t + t/k].
  1. d − 3d/4 + 3d/4k = (d/4)(1 + 3/k) = d(k + 3)/4k.
  2. C/C0 = d ÷ [d(k + 3)/4k] = 4k/(k + 3).

Answer: option (2) — 4k/(k + 3)

Q172CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q23 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Two identical thin metal plates are given charges q1 and q2 (q2 < q1) respectively. If they are now brought close together to form a parallel plate capacitor with a capacitance C then the potential difference between the plates is:
  1. (q1 + q2)/2C
  2. q1/(2Cq2)
  3. (q1 − q2)/2C
  4. q2/[C(q1 + q2)]
Concept to recallFor plates with charges q1, q2, the facing (inner) surfaces carry ±(q1 − q2)/2; V = Qinner/C.
  1. Outer surfaces each carry (q1 + q2)/2; they produce no field between the plates.
  2. Inner surfaces: +(q1 − q2)/2 and −(q1 − q2)/2.
  3. V = (q1 − q2)/2C.

Answer: option (3) — (q1 − q2)/2C

Q173CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q33 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q174CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q37 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A dielectric material placed in uniform electric field, which of the following option is NOT CORRECT:

  4. The external field induces dipole moment by re-orienting molecules of dielectrics
Concept to recallDielectrics have no free charges; a field polarises them by stretching non-polar molecules and aligning polar ones.

  2. Charges in a dielectric are bound: (2) is not correct.

Answer: option (2) — The free movement of charges in a dielectric is possible

Q175CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q34worked here

D. During charging by rubbing, the insulating material with higher work function becomes positively charged
E. Dielectric polarisation means formation of electric dipole inside the dielectric
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B and D only
  2. A, D and E only
  3. C, D and E only
  4. A, B, C and E

Q176CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q48worked here
Two identical capacitors are joined in parallel, charged to a potential V and then separated and connected in series, i.e., negative plate of first is connected to positive plate of second:
  1. the charges on the plates connected together are destroyed
  2. the charges on the free plates are decreased
  3. the potential difference between the free plates becomes 2V
  4. the potential differences between the free plates becomes 4V
Concept to recallIsolated capacitors keep their charges; in series the voltages add.

  2. In series (+ to −) the voltages add: 2V between the free plates.

Q177CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q15 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A cube of side a has a charge Q at each of its vertices, what is the potential due to this charge array at the centre of the cube?

  3. Q/(2√3 πε0a)
  4. 8Q/(√3 πε0a2)

Q178CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q27 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q179CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q35 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q180CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q37 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A point charge q moves from point A to D along the path ABCD (as shown) in a uniform electric field E pointing parallel to negative direction of X-axis. The co-ordinates of A, B, C, D are (0, 0, 0), (a, b, 0), (3a, 0, 0) and (2a, −b, 0) respectively. The work done by the field in the above process is given by expression:
  1. qEa
  2. √2 qEa
  3. −qEa
  4. −2aqE
Concept to recallThe electrostatic force is conservative: work depends only on the end points, W = F·d = qE·(rD − rA).
  1. E = −Eî; displacement A → D = 2aî − bĵ.
  2. W = q(−E)(2a) + 0 = −2qEa.

Answer: option (4) — −2aqE

Q181CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q4 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. Of the options only (3) is a derivative of V with respect to distance; it is the form that equals the field.

Answer: option (3) — −dV/dr

Q182CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q18key re-derived

Q183CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q38key re-derived

  2. C1C2(V1 − V2)2(C1 + C2)
  3. C1C2(V1 − V2)22(C1 + C2)
  4. (C1 + C2)(V1 − V2)C1C2
Concept to recallSharing charge: common potential V = (C1V1 + C2V2)/(C1 + C2); energy lost = ½[C1C2/(C1 + C2)](V1 − V2)2.
  1. Ui − Uf = ½C1V12 + ½C2V22 − ½(C1 + C2)V2.
  2. Simplifies to C1C2(V1 − V2)2/[2(C1 + C2)].
  3. Dimension check: only this option is (capacitance)(voltage)2, an energy.

Q184CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q5key re-derived
Two spheres of silver of same radii, one solid and the other hollow, are charged to the same potential, then:

  2. hollow sphere will have more charge

Concept to recallCharge on a conductor resides on its outer surface; an isolated sphere has C = 4πε0R whether solid or hollow.

  2. Same R, same V ⇒ same charge, all on the outer surface.

Q185CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q1NTA final key
The potential of a uniformly charged spherical shell at a point r/2 from its centre is 5 V. The potential at its surface is :
(Given radius of shell = r)
  1. zero
  2. 2.5 V
  3. 5 V
  4. 10 V
Concept to recallInside a charged shell E = 0, so V is the same everywhere inside and equal to its surface value kQ/R.
  1. E = 0 inside ⇒ no work needed to move a charge inside ⇒ V constant.
  2. V(surface) = V(r/2) = 5 V.

Q186CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q10NTA final key

  2. Rows in parallel: 1/3 + 1/2 = 5/6 μF.

Q187CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q2NTA final key

Q188CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q5NTA final key
Two charges 5 μC and −2 μC (with no external field) are placed at (−9 cm, 0, 0) and (9 cm, 0, 0) respectively. The work required to separate the two charges infinitely away from each other is :

Q189CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q1NTA final key
Choose the correct statement:
Three charges 2q, −q, −q are located at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. At the centroid:
  1. the field is zero but the potential is non-zero
  2. potential is zero but the field is non-zero
  3. both field and potential are zero
  4. both field and potential are non-zero
Concept to recallPotential is a scalar (add algebraically); field is a vector (add with directions).
  1. All three charges are the same distance r from the centroid, so V = k(2q − q − q)/r = 0.
  2. Fields: 2q pushes away from its vertex; each −q pulls towards its own vertex. The two pulls (each kq/r2, 120° apart) add to kq/r2 directed away from the 2q vertex, and 2q’s push of 2kq/r2 is in the same direction.
  3. Net field = 3kq/r2 ≠ 0.

Answer: option (2) — potential is zero but the field is non-zero

Q190CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q3NTA final key
A conducting sphere of radius R is given a charge Q. What is the electric field and the electric potential at the centre of the sphere?

  3. zero and Q4πε0R

  1. Charge sits on the surface; E = 0 everywhere inside.
  2. V inside = V on surface = Q/(4πε0R).

Q191CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q4NTA final key

Concept to recallParallel: C = C1 + C2; series: 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2.

  2. In series with C3: (2C·C)/(3C) = 2C/3.
  3. This branch is in parallel with C4: 2C/3 + C = 5C/3.

Q195CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q6NTA final key

Q196CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q5NTA final key
A parallel plate capacitor having cross - sectional area ‘A’ and separated by distance ‘d’ is filled by copper plate of thickness b. It’s capacitance is :

Q199CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q12 (NTA Q.No. 402)NTA final key

Q202CUET 2026 · 15 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived

Q203CUET 2026 · 15 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived

  3. Req = 30 × 60/90 = 20 Ω; I = 40/20 = 2 A.

Answer: option (1) — 2 A

Q204CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Two resistors of 200 Ω and 400 Ω are connected in series with a battery of 100 V. A bulb rated at 200 V, 100 W is connected across the 400 Ω resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is _________ V.
  1. 25
  2. 50
  3. 66.6
  4. 100
Concept to recallBulb resistance R = Vrated2/P; then series-parallel and the potential divider.
  1. Rbulb = 2002/100 = 400 Ω; in parallel with 400 Ω gives 200 Ω.
  2. Now 200 Ω and 200 Ω in series share 100 V equally: 50 V across the bulb.

Answer: option (2) — 50

Q205CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
The drift velocity of electrons in a conductor increases when:
  1. Temperature increases only
  2. Electric field increases
  3. Length of conductor increases
  4. Area of cross-section increases
Concept to recallvd = eEτ/m.
  1. vd ∝ E. Raising temperature shortens τ and lowers vd; for a fixed voltage a longer wire means a smaller E.

Answer: option (2) — Electric field increases

Q206CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10worked here
Two cells ε1 and ε2 are connected in opposition to each other as shown in the figure. The cell ε1 is of emf 9 V and internal resistance 3 Ω. The cell ε2 is of emf 7 V and internal resistance 7 Ω. The potential difference between the points A and B is:
  1. 8.4 V
  2. 5.6 V
  3. 7.8 V
  4. 6.6 V
Concept to recallA cell driving current has V = ε − Ir; a cell being charged (current forced in at its + terminal) has V = ε + Ir.
  1. Net emf 9 − 7 = 2 V round a loop of 3 + 7 = 10 Ω: I = 0.2 A.
  2. Across the 9 V cell (discharging): VAB = 9 − 0.2 × 3 = 8.4 V.
  3. Check with the 7 V cell (being charged): 7 + 0.2 × 7 = 8.4 V.

Answer: option (1) — 8.4 V

Trap5.6 V uses ε − Ir for the cell that is being charged.
NoteThe site prints 5.6 V, from 7 − Ir for the 7 V cell. But the stronger 9 V cell drives current into the 7 V cell, which is being charged, so its terminal voltage is 7 + Ir = 8.4 V, as the 9 V cell confirms. The set gives no figure; the slide redraws the usual arrangement (the two cells side by side between A and B).
Q207CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
A wire has a resistance of 2.5 Ω at 28°C and a resistance of 2.9 Ω at 100°C. The temperature coefficient of resistivity of the material of the wire is:
  1. 1.06 × 10−3 °C−1
  2. 3.5 × 10−2 °C−1
  3. 2.22 × 10−3 °C−1
  4. 3.95 × 10−2 °C−1
Concept to recallR2 = R1[1 + α(T2 − T1)].

Q208CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
Choose the correct combination of three resistances 1 Ω, 2 Ω and 3 Ω to get equivalent resistance 11/5 Ω.
  1. All three are combined in parallel
  2. All three are combined in series
  3. 1 Ω and 2 Ω are in parallel and 3 Ω is in series with both
  4. 2 Ω and 3 Ω are combined in parallel and 1 Ω is in series with both
Concept to recallSeries adds; parallel gives R1R2/(R1 + R2).
  1. Parallel 6/11, series 6, (1||2) + 3 = 2/3 + 3 = 11/3.
  2. (2||3) + 1 = 6/5 + 1 = 11/5 Ω.

Answer: option (4) — 2 Ω and 3 Ω are combined in parallel and 1 Ω is in series with both

Q209CUET 2026 · 25 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
A battery of emf 15 V and internal resistance of 4 Ω is connected to a resistor. If the current in the circuit is 2 A, the resistance of the resistor and terminal voltage of the battery will be:

  2. 3.5 Ω, 6 V
  3. 2.5 Ω, 7 V
  4. 3.5 Ω, 7 V
Concept to recallI = ε/(R + r); terminal voltage V = ε − Ir = IR.
  1. R + 4 = 15/2 = 7.5 ⇒ R = 3.5 Ω.
  2. V = 15 − 2 × 4 = 7 V (check: IR = 2 × 3.5 = 7 V).

Q210CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
Four resistors of 8 Ω each are connected in parallel. Then five such equivalent combinations are connected in series. What will be the total resistance?

  2. 2 Ω
  3. 12 Ω
  4. 2.5 Ω
Concept to recalln equal resistors in parallel: R/n; m equal in series: mR.

Q211CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
A wire of uniform cross-section A, length l and resistance R is bent into a complete circle. The equivalent resistance between any two diametrically opposite points will be:

  2. R/8
  3. 4R

Concept to recallTwo arcs between the same points are in parallel; each arc has resistance in proportion to its length.

Q212CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
A uniform wire of resistance R is cut into four equal parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination is:

  3. R/16

Concept to recallR ∝ l; n equal resistors r in parallel give r/n.

Q213CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived
Five resistors, each of resistance R, are connected between points A and B as shown in the figure. The equivalent resistance between A and B is:
  1. 3R/8
  2. 5R
  3. 8R/3
  4. 2R
Concept to recallReduce each branch, then combine branches in parallel.
  1. Upper branch: R + (R || R) = R + R/2 = 3R/2. Lower branch: R || R = R/2.
  2. Parallel: (3R/2)(R/2)/(3R/2 + R/2) = (3R2/4)/(2R) = 3R/8.

Answer: option (1) — 3R/8

Q214CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
In the figure shown, three resistors of 4 Ω are connected. If point D divides the resistor between B and C into two equal parts, then the equivalent resistance between points A and D is:
  1. 12 Ω
  2. 6 Ω
  3. 3 Ω
  4. 1/3 Ω
Concept to recallSplit the divided resistor at D, then trace the paths from A to D.
  1. Path A–B–D: 4 + 2 = 6 Ω. Path A–C–D: 4 + 2 = 6 Ω.
  2. Two 6 Ω paths in parallel: 3 Ω.

Answer: option (3) — 3 Ω

Q215CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
For the given mixed combination of resistors, calculate the total resistance between points A and B.
  1. 9 Ω
  2. 18 Ω
  3. 4 Ω
  4. 14 Ω
Concept to recallLadder networks collapse from the far end towards the terminals.
  1. Top: 4 + 4 = 8 Ω in parallel with 8 Ω = 4 Ω.
  2. Next rung: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 Ω in parallel with 12 Ω = 6 Ω.
  3. Add the two 6 Ω legs: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 Ω.

Answer: option (2) — 18 Ω

Q216CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
A wire of uniform cross-sectional area and resistivity has total resistance 36 Ω and is bent into a circle as shown in the figure. The equivalent resistance between points A and B is:

Concept to recallArc resistance ∝ angle; the two arcs between A and B are in parallel.

Q217CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived

Concept to recallList every path between the two terminals; paths that share only the terminals are in parallel.

  2. Three 3 Ω paths in parallel: 1 Ω.

Q218CUET 2026 · 31 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived

Q219CUET 2026 · labelled 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain; no answers printed) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1worked here

Q221CUET 2026 · file dated 6 June, headed 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived

Q222CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q10NTA final key
Resistivity of a conductor depends on
  1. its material and the dimensions of the conductor
  2. its material and temperature of the conductor
  3. the dimensions of the conductor only
  4. the temperature of the conductor only
Concept to recallρ = m/(ne2τ): fixed by the material (n) and its temperature (τ); resistance R = ρl/A depends on dimensions, resistivity does not.
  1. n is a property of the material; the relaxation time τ falls as temperature rises.
  2. Length and area enter R, not ρ.

Answer: option (2) — its material and temperature of the conductor

TrapConfusing resistance (depends on dimensions) with resistivity.
Q223CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q11NTA final key
In the (i) absence of electric field, and in the (ii) presence of electric field, the paths of electrons between successive collisions with the positive ions of the metal, are
  1. (i) Straight line, (ii) straight line
  2. (i) Curved, (ii) straight line
  3. (i) Curved, (ii) curved
  4. (i) Straight line, (ii) Curved in general
Concept to recallBetween collisions an electron moves under whatever force acts on it: none ⇒ uniform velocity; constant force eE ⇒ parabola-like (projectile) path.
  1. No field: no force between collisions, so motion is in a straight line.
  2. With E: a constant force −eE acts, and unless the velocity happens to be along E, the path bends (like a projectile): curved in general.

Answer: option (4) — (i) Straight line, (ii) Curved in general

Q224CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q12NTA final key
A resistor develops 800 J of thermal energy in 20 s on applying a potential difference of 20 V. Its resistance is
  1. 20 Ω
  2. 10 Ω
  3. 40 Ω
  4. 0.5 Ω
Concept to recallJoule heating: H = (V2/R) t.
  1. P = 800/20 = 40 W.
  2. R = V2/P = 400/40 = 10 Ω.

Answer: option (2) — 10 Ω

Q225CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q13NTA final key
A wire of resistance 4 Ω is used to make a coil of radius 7 cm. The wire has a diameter of 1.4 mm and the resistivity of its material is 2 × 10−7 Ω m. The number of turns in the coil will be
  1. 70
  2. 40
  3. 140
  4. 20
Concept to recallR = ρl/A gives the wire length; turns = l/(2πr).
  1. A = π(0.7 × 10−3)2 = 1.54 × 10−6 m2.
  2. l = RA/ρ = 4 × 1.54 × 10−6/(2 × 10−7) = 30.8 m.
  3. N = 30.8/(2π × 0.07) = 30.8/0.44 = 70.

Answer: option (1) — 70

TrapUsing the diameter 1.4 mm as the radius gives 4× the area and 280 turns; using the coil diameter halves N.
Q226CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q14NTA final key
A battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 3 Ω is connected to an external resistor. If the current in the circuit is 0.6 A, the voltage across the external resistor will be
  1. 10.2 V
  2. 17.0 V
  3. 12.0 V
  4. 13.8 V

  1. V = 12 − 0.6 × 3 = 10.2 V.

Answer: option (1) — 10.2 V

Q227CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q15NTA final key
A uniform wire of resistance 12 Ω is cut into three pieces in the ratio of length 1: 2: 3. Now the three pieces are connected to form a triangle. A cell of emf 8 V and internal resistance 5 Ω is connected across the highest of the three resistors. The current through the circuit is:
  1. 4 A
  2. 2 A
  3. 0.5 A
  4. 1 A
Concept to recallR ∝ l for a uniform wire; across one side of a triangle, that side is in parallel with the other two in series.
  1. Pieces: 2 Ω, 4 Ω, 6 Ω.
  2. Across the 6 Ω side: 6 ∥ (2 + 4) = 3 Ω.
  3. I = 8/(3 + 5) = 1 A.

Answer: option (4) — 1 A

Trap4 A divides 8 V by the 2 Ω piece alone; about 0.5 A puts all three pieces in series with the cell.
Q228CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q9NTA final key
Conductors develop electric currents in them
  1. on applying electric field
  2. on placing the conductor in the magnetic field
  3. on applying gravitational field only
  4. on applying the magnetic field and gravitational field
Concept to recallA steady current needs a force that drives free electrons along the conductor: an electric field (vd = eEτ/m).
  1. An applied electric field gives the free electrons a drift velocity, i.e. a current.
  2. A static magnetic field exerts no force on charges at rest, and gravity on electrons is negligible.

Answer: option (1) — on applying electric field

Q229CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q12 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only

Q230CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q14 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The following statements are given related to Wheatstone Bridge:
  1. (A) when Wheatstone Bridge is balanced, no current flows through the galvanometer arm.
  2. (B) Wheatstone Bridge works on the principle of Kirchhoff’s law.
  3. (C) Being a null method based experiment, the result is free from the effect of extra resistances (cell resistance) of the circuit
  4. (D) Wheatstone Bridge is most sensitive when all the four resistances are nearly of the same magnitude.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only

Q231CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q16 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A cell supplies a current of 0.6 A through a 3 Ω resistor and a current of 0.2 A through a 10 Ω resistor. The internal resistance of the cell is:

  2. 1.0 Ω

Q232CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q30 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q233CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q31 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q234CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q40 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q235CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q12worked here
A Wheatstone bridge has four resistors: R1 = R2 = R3 = 1 Ω and R4 = 2 Ω. In order to balance the bridge, resistor R4 has to be shunted by resistance of
  1. 0.5 Ω

  3. 2.0 Ω

Q236CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q14worked here

Q241CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q49worked here

Q242CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q17worked here
The external diameter of a 5 m long hollow copper tube is 10 cm and the thickness of its wall is 5 mm. If the specific resistance of copper be 1.7 × 10−8 Ω-m, then its resistance would be approximately
  1. 4.5 × 10−5 Ω

  4. 8.0 × 10−5 Ω
Concept to recallR = ρl/A, with A the annulus π(r22 − r12).
  1. r2 = 5 cm, r1 = 4.5 cm: A = π(0.0025 − 0.002025) = 1.49 × 10−3 m2.
  2. R = 1.7 × 10−8 × 5/1.49 × 10−3 = 5.7 × 10−5 Ω ≈ 6.0 × 10−5 Ω.

Answer: option (2) — 6.0 × 10−5 Ω

TrapUsing the full disc area πr22 gives 1.1 × 10−5 Ω.
NoteThe exact value is 5.7 × 10−5 Ω; the nearest option is 6.0 × 10−5 Ω (“approximately”).
Q243CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q2worked here
A cell of emf 2.2 V gives a current of 0.2 A through a resistance of 9 Ω. The internal resistance of the cell will be:

  2. 2 Ω
  3. 4 Ω
  4. 1.1 Ω

Q244CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q33worked here
For a metre Bridge, Choose the incorrect option from the following
  1. The wire of one meter length fixed on the wooden plank is a uniform conducting wire having constant resistance per unit length.
  2. Metre Bridge is not suitable to measure very low resistances.
  3. Interchanging the position of the galvanometer and the cell will not change the balance point on the wire X/Y = l1/l2
  4. The internal resistance of the cell affects the balancing position of null point.
Concept to recallAt balance no current flows in the galvanometer; the null point depends only on the four arm resistances.
  1. The cell’s internal resistance changes the total current but not the ratio of the arms, so it does not move the null point.
  2. The other three statements are true (end resistances spoil low-resistance measurements; G and cell are interchangeable).

Answer: option (4) — The internal resistance of the cell affects the balancing position of null point.

Q245CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q37worked here

  1. 12 A
  2. 8 A
  3. 6 A

Q246CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q41worked here
Choose the correct option from the following
  1. (A) The internal resistance of a cell depends on its distance between electrodes and on the area of the electrodes.
  2. (B) The emf of a cell is measured when it is used in series in an electrical circuit carrying current I.
  3. (C) If a cell of emf E and of internal resistance r is providing current I through a resistance R then the potential difference across the cell is V = I(R + r).
  4. (D) The emf of a cell is 1 V, if 1 J of work is done by the cell to drive 1 C of charge in the whole circuit.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (B) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (C) and (D) only
  4. (A) and (D) only
Concept to recallTerminal voltage V = E − Ir = IR; emf = work done per unit charge round the whole circuit.
  1. (A) true: r grows with electrode separation and falls with electrode area.
  2. (B) false: emf is the p.d. on open circuit (no current).
  3. (C) false: V = IR = E − Ir; I(R + r) is E itself.
  4. (D) true: definition of emf.

Answer: option (4) — (A) and (D) only

NoteThe re-typeset numbers the first three statements 1–3 and the last (D); relabelled (A)–(D) as the options require.
Q247CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q49worked here
The resistivity of the material of a wire of length 15 m, area of cross-section 6 × 10−7 m2 and resistance 10 Ω will be

  3. 3 × 10−7 Ω m
  4. 5 × 10−7 Ω m

Answer: option (1) — 4 × 10−7 Ω m

Q248CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q8worked here
Which of the following statements is true about electromotive force (emf) of a cell?
  1. It depends on external resistance.
  2. emf is the potential difference between positive and negative terminals of a cell in a closed circuit.
  3. It has electrostatic origin.
  4. emf is the potential difference between positive and negative terminals of a cell in a open circuit.
Concept to recallTerminal voltage V = ε − Ir equals ε only when I = 0.
  1. On open circuit I = 0, so the terminal p.d. equals the emf.
  2. Emf is chemical (non-electrostatic) in origin and does not depend on the external R.

Answer: option (4) — emf is the potential difference between positive and negative terminals of a cell in a open circuit.

Q249CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q25worked here
Which of the following statements are true?
  1. (A) Rheostat can be used both as a variable resistance and a potential divider.
  2. (B) An electrical circuit is functional only if all the components of the circuit are connected in proper order, assuming that all circuit components/ devices are in working condition and key is closed.
  3. (C) An open circuit means a break in some part of a circuit which could be deliberate such as a key in open position or a fault such as broken wire or burnt out component(s) or loose connection.
  4. (D) Rheostat as a potential divider gives variable resistance.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B) and (D) only
Concept to recallA rheostat used with all three terminals is a potential divider: it gives a variable voltage.
  1. (A), (B), (C) true.
  2. (D) false: as a potential divider it supplies a variable voltage, not a variable resistance.

Answer: option (2) — (A), (B) and (C) only

Q250CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q32worked here
Identify the correct statements among the following.
  1. (A) Electrical appliances in a household are always connected in series.
  2. (B) Electrical appliances in a household are always connected in parallel.
  3. (C) The potential difference across different electrical appliances in households is not equal.
  4. (D) The potential difference across different electrical appliances in households is equal.

  1. (A) and (D) only
  2. (A) and (C) only
  3. (B) and (D) only
  4. (B) and (C) only

Q251CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q4worked here

Q252CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q41worked here
The current in a wire varies with time according to the relationship; I = (2 + 2t) A, where t is time in seconds. The charge passing through a cross-section of the wire in the time interval between t = 0 s to t = 4 s is
  1. 24 C
  2. 32 C
  3. 20 C
  4. 22 C

Q253CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q44worked here
What will be the internal resistance of a cell of emf 2.2 V which gives a current of 0.2 A through a resistance of 10 Ω?
