Q254CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q45worked here
The Wheatstone bridge is an arrangement of four resistances R1, R2, R3, R4 as shown in the figure given below. The null-point condition is not given by
  1. R2/R1 = R4/R3
  2. R1/R2 = R3/R4
  3. R1R4 = R2R3
  4. R1R2 = R3R4
Concept to recallBalance: ratio of the two arms on one side equals the ratio on the other, R2/R4 = R1/R3.
  1. VB = VD gives R2/R4 = R1/R3, i.e. R1R4 = R2R3.
  2. Options 1, 2, 3 are rearrangements of this; R1R2 = R3R4 is not.

Answer: option (4) — R1R2 = R3R4

Q255CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q6worked here
Each resistor shown in figure has a resistance of 20 Ω and the battery has an emf of 12 V. The current supplied by the battery is
  1. 0.3 A
  2. 0.6 A
  3. 1.2 A
  4. 2.4 A
Concept to recallSymmetric (balanced) bridge: the middle resistor carries no current.
  1. f–e–d and a–b–c are identical, so e and b are at the same potential; drop e–b.
  2. Two 40 Ω branches in parallel = 20 Ω.
  3. i = 12/20 = 0.6 A.

Answer: option (2) — 0.6 A

Q256CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q12 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The electric field in a copper wire of cross-sectional area 2.0 mm2 carrying a current of 1 A is: (Given: Resistivity of copper ρ = 2 × 10−8 Ω·m)
  1. 10−2 V/m
  2. 5 × 10−2 V/m
  3. 10−3 V/m
  4. 2.5 × 10−2 V/m
Concept to recallMicroscopic Ohm’s law: E = ρj = ρI/A.
  1. j = 1/(2 × 10−6) = 5 × 105 A/m2.
  2. E = 2 × 10−8 × 5 × 105 = 10−2 V/m.

Answer: option (1) — 10−2 V/m

Trap2.0 mm2 = 2 × 10−6 m2, not 2 × 10−3.
Q257CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q16 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A 10 V battery of negligible internal resistance is connected with a 200 V battery and a set of parallel resistances as shown in the figure. The value of current in the circuit.
  1. 5 A
  2. 15 A
  3. 10 A
  4. 2 A
Concept to recallCells in one loop: net emf = sum with signs (opposing cells subtract); three equal R in parallel give R/3.
  1. Going round the loop, the two cells push in opposite senses: net emf = 200 − 10 = 190 V.
  2. Req = 38/3 Ω.
  3. I = 190 × 3/38 = 15 A.

Answer: option (2) — 15 A

TrapAdding the cells (210 V) gives 16.6 A, which is not offered; reading one 38 Ω gives 5 A.
Q258CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q20 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The variation of resistivity of a metallic conductor with temperature is given correctly by which of the following relations? (Where ρT is the resistivity at a temperature T and ρ0 is the resistivity at a reference temperature T0, α is the temperature coefficient of resistivity, T > T0)
  1. ρT = ρ0[1 + α(T − T0)]
  2. ρ0 = ρT[1 + α(T0 − T)]
  3. ρT = ρ0[1 + α(1 − T0)]
  4. ρT = [ρ0 + α(T − T0)]
Concept to recallFor a metal, resistivity rises linearly over a moderate range: ρT = ρ0[1 + α(T − T0)].
  1. α is defined relative to ρ0 at T0, so the factor multiplies ρ0.
  2. The last option is dimensionally wrong (adds αΔT to a resistivity).

Answer: option (1) — ρT = ρ0[1 + α(T − T0)]

Q259CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q32 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In the circuit diagram shown in the figure, the resistance R1 = 10 Ω, R2 = 15 Ω and E = 20 V. When the switch S is closed, the ratio of i1 to i3 will be
  1. 6:5
  2. 20:3
  3. 4:3
  4. 5:3
Concept to recallParallel branches across an ideal cell each carry E/R; the main current is their sum.
  1. i3 = 20/10 = 2 A (through R1), i2 = 20/15 = 4/3 A.
  2. i1 = 2 + 4/3 = 10/3 A.
  3. i1 : i3 = (10/3) : 2 = 5 : 3.

Answer: option (4) — 5:3

Q260CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q36 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A hot electric iron has resistance of 88 Ω and is used with a 220 V source. The electrical energy consumed in 4 h is:
  1. 7.92 × 106 J
  2. 7.92 × 107 J
  3. 2.2 × 103 J
  4. 1.32 × 105 J
Concept to recallP = V2/R; energy = Pt with t in seconds.
  1. P = 2202/88 = 550 W.
  2. W = 550 × 4 × 3600 = 7.92 × 106 J (2.2 kWh).

Answer: option (1) — 7.92 × 106 J

Q261CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q44 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Two wires with resistances R1 and R2 are stretched n times their original length. After stretching, the two wires are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination will be:
  1. n2R1R2R1 + R2
  2. nR1R2R1 + nR2
  3. R1R2n2(R1 + R2)
  4. nR1R2nR1 + R2
Concept to recallStretching at constant volume: l → nl, A → A/n, so R → n2R.
  1. New resistances n2R1 and n2R2.
  2. Parallel: n4R1R2/n2(R1 + R2) = n2R1R2/(R1 + R2).

Answer: option (1) — n2R1R2R1 + R2

TrapStretching changes the area too, so R grows as n2, not n.
Q262CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q45 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Match List-I with List-II
List-I (Physical Quantity)List-II (Formula)
A. j (current density)I. eτ/m
B. vd (drift velocity)II. (ne2/m)τ
C. σ (conductivity)III. (e/m)τE
D. μ (mobility)IV. (ne2/m)τE

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)
  2. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)
  3. (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)
  4. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)
Concept to recallvd = eτE/m, μ = vd/E, j = nevd = σE.
  1. vd = (e/m)τE → III; μ = eτ/m → I.
  2. j = nevd = (ne2/m)τE → IV; σ = j/E = (ne2/m)τ → II.

Answer: option (1) — (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

Q263CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q36NTA final key
A metal wire is subjected to a constant potential difference. When the temperature of the metal wire increases, the drift velocity of the electron in it ____________.
  1. increases, thermal velocity of the electrons decreases
  2. decreases, thermal velocity of the electrons decreases
  3. increases, thermal velocity of the electrons increases
  4. decreases, thermal velocity of the electrons increases
Concept to recallvd = eEτ/m; a hotter lattice means more collisions, so a shorter relaxation time τ.
  1. T up ⇒ τ down ⇒ vd decreases (resistance rises).
  2. Thermal speed ∝ √T increases.

Answer: option (4) — decreases, thermal velocity of the electrons increases

Q264CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q37NTA final key
For the given mixed combination of resistors calculate the total resistance between points A and B.
  1. 9 Ω
  2. 18 Ω
  3. 4 Ω
  4. 14 Ω
Concept to recallReduce from the end farthest from the terminals: series then parallel, repeatedly.
  1. Top: 4 + 4 = 8 Ω, in parallel with 8 Ω ⇒ 4 Ω.
  2. Add the two 4 Ω sides: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 Ω, in parallel with 12 Ω ⇒ 6 Ω.
  3. RAB = 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 Ω.

Answer: option (2) — 18 Ω

Q265CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q38NTA final key
A cell of emf 1.1 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a wire of resistance 0.5 Ω. Another cell of the same emf is now connected in series with the intention of increasing the current but the current in the wire remains the same. The internal resistance of the second cell is ____________.
  1. 1 Ω
  2. 2.5 Ω
  3. 1.5 Ω
  4. 2 Ω
Concept to recallI = (total emf)/(external + all internal resistances).
  1. Before: I = 1.1/(0.5 + 0.5) = 1.1 A.
  2. After: 2.2/(1 + r) = 1.1 ⇒ r = 1 Ω.

Answer: option (1) — 1 Ω

Q266CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q39NTA final key
P, Q, R and S are four wires of resistances 3, 3, 3 and 4 Ω respectively. They are connected to form the four arms of a wheatstone bridge circuit. The resistance with which S must be shunted in order that the bridge may be balanced is ____________.
  1. 14 Ω
  2. 12 Ω
  3. 15 Ω
  4. 7 Ω
Concept to recallBalanced bridge: P/Q = R/S; a shunt is a resistor in parallel.
  1. Need S′ = RQ/P = 3 Ω.
  2. 4x/(4 + x) = 3 ⇒ 4x = 12 + 3x ⇒ x = 12 Ω.

Answer: option (2) — 12 Ω

Q267CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q5NTA final key
Two resistances of 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in series across a 20 V battery as shown in figure below. The reading in a 200 Ω voltmeter connected across the 200 Ω resistance is ___________.
  1. 4 V
  2. 203 V
  3. 10 V
  4. 16 V
Concept to recallA real voltmeter is a resistor in parallel with what it measures, so it loads the circuit.
  1. 200 Ω ∥ 200 Ω (voltmeter) = 100 Ω.
  2. Circuit: 100 Ω + 100 Ω = 200 Ω, I = 20/200 = 0.1 A.
  3. Reading = 0.1 × 100 = 10 V.

Answer: option (3) — 10 V

TrapIgnoring the voltmeter’s resistance gives 40/3 V across the 200 Ω (not offered); 20/3 V is the 100 Ω share without the meter.
Q268CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q6NTA final key
The current through a 4/3 Ω external resistance connected to a parallel combination of two cells of 2 V and 1 V emf and internal resistances of 1 Ω and 2 Ω respectively is ___________.
  1. 1 A
  2. 2/3 A
  3. 3/4 A
  4. 5/6 A
Concept to recallCells in parallel (like terminals together): Eeq = (E1r2 + E2r1)/(r1 + r2), req = r1r2/(r1 + r2).
  1. Eeq = (2×2 + 1×1)/3 = 5/3 V; req = 2/3 Ω.
  2. I = (5/3)/(2/3 + 4/3) = (5/3)/2 = 5/6 A.

Answer: option (4) — 5/6 A

Q269CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q7NTA final key
A metallic wire of uniform area of cross section has a resistance R, resistivity ρ and power rating P at V volts. The wire is uniformly stretched to reduce the radius to half the original radius. The values of resistance, resistivity and power rating at V volts are now denoted by R′, ρ′ and P′ respectively. The corresponding values are correctly related as ________.
  1. ρ′ = 2ρ, R′ = 2R, P′ = 2P
  2. ρ′ = (1/2)ρ, R′ = (1/2)R, P′ = (1/2)P
  3. ρ′ = ρ, R′ = 16R, P′ = (1/16)P
  4. ρ′ = ρ, R′ = (1/16)R, P′ = 16P
Concept to recallStretching keeps the volume: if r → r/n then A → A/n2, l → n2l, so R → n4R. Resistivity is a material property.
  1. n = 2: R′ = 24R = 16R; ρ′ = ρ.
  2. At fixed V, P = V2/R, so P′ = P/16.

Answer: option (3) — ρ′ = ρ, R′ = 16R, P′ = (1/16)P

Q270CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q637NTA final key
An electric bulb rated 200 V - 100 W is connected to a 160 V power supply. The power consumed by it would be :
  1. 64 W
  2. 80 W
  3. 100 W
  4. 125 W

  1. R = 2002/100 = 400 Ω.
  2. P = 1602/400 = 64 W (= 100 × (0.8)2).

Q271CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q646NTA final key
A conducting wire of length L, uniform area of cross-section A of a material having n free electrons per unit volume offers a resistance R to flow of current through itself. (m and e respectively denote the mass and charge of electron). If τ is mean free time of free electrons in the conductor, the correct formula for resistance R is :
  1. R = mLe2nAτ
  2. R = mAe2nLτ
  3. R = mτe2nAL
  4. R = e2nAτmL
Concept to recallDrude: ρ = m/(ne2τ) and R = ρL/A.
  1. vd = eEτ/m, I = neAvd = ne2AτV/(mL).
  2. R = V/I = mL/(ne2Aτ).

Answer: option (1) — R = mLe2nAτ

Q272CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q648NTA final key
The figure below shows a part of an electric circuit. The current marked IA is :
  1. 1 A
  2. 1.3 A
  3. 1.7 A
  4. 3 A
Concept to recallKirchhoff’s junction rule: current in = current out at every node.
  1. At B: current from A to B = 1.2 + 0.5 = 1.7 A (both leave B).
  2. At A: 0.2 + 0.2 + IA = 1.7 ⇒ IA = 1.3 A.

Q273CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q660NTA final key
Arrange the following materials in the increasing order of their resistivity.
(A) Copper   (B) Platinum   (C) Silver   (D) Aluminium

  2. (C), (A), (D), (B)
  3. (C), (B), (A), (D)
  4. (B), (D), (A), (C)

Q274CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q661NTA final key
For the given equation of charge Q = 3t2 + 6t, where Q is in coulomb and t is time in sec, the initial value of current is :
  1. 0 A
  2. 2 A
  3. 6 A
  4. 9 A

Q275CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q662NTA final key
In the circuit shown below the current in the 1 Ω resistor is :
  1. 1.3 A from P to Q
  2. 0 A
  3. 0.13 A from Q to P
  4. 0.13 A from P to Q
Concept to recallThree branches between the same two nodes P and Q: Kirchhoff (or Millman) — VP − VQ = Σ(Ek/Rk)/Σ(1/Rk).
  1. Take VQ = 0. Left branch (6 V cell, + towards the left corner, then 3 Ω): it pushes P down by 6 V ⇒ E = −6 V, R = 3 Ω.
  2. Right branch (2 Ω, 9 V with + at the top, 3 Ω): E = +9 V, R = 5 Ω. Middle: E = 0, R = 1 Ω.
  3. VP = (−6/3 + 9/5)/(1/3 + 1/5 + 1) = (−0.2)/(23/15) = −0.13 V.
  4. VQ > VP, so 0.13 A flows through 1 Ω from Q to P.

Answer: option (3) — 0.13 A from Q to P

Q276CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q682NTA final key
The Wheatstone bridge is an arrangement of four resistances, say R1, R2, R3 and R4. The null point condition is given by :
  1. R1/R2 = R3/R4
  2. R1 + R2 = R3 + R4
  3. R1 − R2 = R2 − R4
  4. R1 × R2 = R3 × R4
Concept to recallBalanced bridge: no current in the galvanometer when the ratios of adjacent arms are equal.
  1. P/Q = R/S, i.e. R1/R2 = R3/R4.

Answer: option (1) — R1/R2 = R3/R4

Q277CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q11 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
V-I graph for a platinum wire at temperatures T1 and T2 is shown in the given figure. The temperature difference (T2 − T1) is proportional to:
  1. sin 2θ
  2. cos 2θ
  3. tan 2θ
  4. cot 2θ
Concept to recallSlope of a V–I graph = R; for a metal R ≈ R0(1 + αΔT), so ΔT ∝ ΔR.
  1. T1 line makes θ with the I-axis: R1 = tanθ.
  2. T2 line makes θ with the V-axis, i.e. 90° − θ with the I-axis: R2 = cotθ.
  3. R2 − R1 = cotθ − tanθ = (cos2θ − sin2θ)/(sinθ cosθ) = 2 cot 2θ.
  4. So T2 − T1 ∝ cot 2θ.

Answer: option (4) — cot 2θ

Q280CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q47 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q284CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q17 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q286CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q25 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A resistance of 15Ω is connected in series with an unknown resistance R1. This combination is connected to one gap of a meter bridge, while a resistance R2 is connected in the other gap. The balance point is at 50 cm. When 15 Ω is removed, the balance point shifts by 10 cm. The value of R1 is

Q290CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q33 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In the potentiometer circuit the balance point is at X. The balance point will be shifted right towards B when:
(A) Resistance R is increased keeping all other parameters constant
(B) Resistance S is increased keeping all other parameters constant
(C) Cell P is replaced by another cell whose emf is lower than Q
(D) The polarity of Q is reversed
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) only
  2. (B) and (D) only
  3. (A), (B) only
  4. (B) and (C) only
Concept to recallBalance length l = V/k, where k is the potential gradient of AB and V the p.d. across Q's terminals. With S (key closed) across Q, Q drives a current through S, so V = εQS/(S + r) — the NCERT internal-resistance circuit.
  1. (A) Larger R ⇒ smaller current in AB ⇒ smaller k ⇒ longer l: the point moves towards B. True.
  2. (B) Larger S ⇒ less current drawn from Q ⇒ less lost on its internal resistance ⇒ larger V ⇒ longer l. True.
  3. (C) If εP < εQ the whole wire cannot balance Q: no balance point at all. False.
  4. (D) Reversing Q also leaves no balance point (both drive current the same way through G). False.
  5. So (A) and (B).

Answer: option (3) — (A), (B) only

TrapS is not in series with the galvanometer: it is across the cell (the shunt used to find internal resistance), so it does change the balance point.

Q292CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q5 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. E ∝ vd: EI > EII > EIII. (B) false.
  3. All copper: conductivity is a material property, the same. (D) true.

Answer: option (3) — (A) and (D) only

Q301CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q13 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A potentiometer wire of length L and a resistance r are connected in series with a battery of emf E0 and a resistance r1. An unknown emf E is balanced at a length l of the potentiometer wire. The emf E will be:

  1. Current in the wire: I = E0/(r + r1) (driver cell taken ideal).
  2. k = Ir/L = E0r/[(r + r1)L].
  3. E = kl = [E0r/(r + r1)]·l/L.

  1. A flat ρ–T line means α ≈ 0.
  2. Copper: ρ rises with T; semiconductors: ρ falls; nichrome: small but noticeable α.
  3. Manganin has the smallest α — the graph fits it.

Q303CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q36 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Choose the wrong statement:

  3. Terminal potential difference versus current graph for a cell is a straight line with a negative slope.
  4. Terminal potential difference when cell is being charged V = E + Ir.
Concept to recallInternal resistance comes from the electrolyte; ions move more sluggishly when cold, so r rises as temperature falls.
  1. (1) V = E − Ir < E on discharge — true.
  2. (3) V = E − rI: slope −r — true. (4) charging: V = E + Ir — true.
  3. (2) is wrong: r increases when the electrolyte is cooled.

Answer: option (2) — Internal resistance of the cell decreases with decrease in temperature of electrolyte.

Q313CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q41 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. −r2

  2. Slope m = −r (intercept on the V-axis is the emf).

Answer: option (4) — −r

Q314CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q48 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A car has a fresh storage battery of e.m.f. 15 V and internal resistance 4 × 10−2 Ω. If the starter motor draws a current of 85 A, what is the terminal voltage of the battery when the starter is on?
  1. 3.4 V
  2. 11.6 V
  3. 12 V
  4. 12.5 V
Concept to recallTerminal voltage on discharge V = E − Ir.
  1. Ir = 85 × 0.04 = 3.4 V.
  2. V = 15 − 3.4 = 11.6 V.

Answer: option (2) — 11.6 V

Trap3.4 V is the lost volts, not the terminal voltage.
Q315CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q7 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The current flowing through the two bulbs marked as 60 W, 240 V each when connected in series with 240 V source is:
  1. 0.125 A
  2. 0.25 A
  3. 4 A
  4. 2 A
Concept to recallBulb resistance from its rating: R = V2/P.
  1. R = 2402/60 = 960 Ω each; in series 1920 Ω.
  2. I = 240/1920 = 0.125 A.

Answer: option (1) — 0.125 A

Q316CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q10key re-derived
The metre bridge wire is made of alloys such as nichrome because they have:
  1. high temperature coefficient of resistance and high resistivity
  2. low temperature coefficient of resistance and low resistivity
  3. low temperature coefficient of resistance and high resistivity
  4. high temperature coefficient of resistance and low resistivity
Concept to recallBridge and potentiometer wires: high ρ (a usable resistance in a short wire) and low α (resistance does not drift as the wire warms).
  1. Low α keeps R per cm constant while current heats the wire.
  2. High ρ gives a measurable potential drop along a 1 m wire.

Answer: option (3) — low temperature coefficient of resistance and high resistivity

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the metre bridge.
Q317CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q13key re-derived
The current flow in the circuit of two battery with internal resistance and two external resistance as shown in figure will be
  1. 1.5 A
  2. 0.67 A
  3. 0.9 A
  4. 1.0 A
Concept to recallSingle loop: I = (net emf)/(total resistance). Cells whose positive terminals face each other oppose: net emf = ε1 − ε2.
  1. The cells oppose: net emf = 15 − 5 = 10 V.
  2. Total resistance = 9 + 4 + 1.2 + 0.8 = 15 Ω.
  3. I = 10/15 = 0.67 A.

Answer: option (2) — 0.67 A

TrapAdding the emfs gives 20/15 = 1.33 A, which is not offered; 1.0 A would need 15 V/15 Ω.
Q318CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q2key re-derived
Match List – I with List – II.
List – IList – II
(A) [M0 L−2 T0 A1](I) Conductance
(B) [M−1 L−2 T3 A2](II) Electrical conductivity
(C) [M L3 T−3 A−2](III) Current density
(D) [M−1 L−3 T3 A2](IV) Specific resistance
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
  2. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  3. (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
  4. (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Concept to recall[R] = [M L2 T−3 A−2]; ρ = RA/l adds L1; conductance = 1/R, conductivity = 1/ρ; J = I/A.

  2. Conductance 1/R = [M−1 L−2 T3 A2] → (B)-(I).
  3. Resistivity ρ = R·L = [M L3 T−3 A−2] → (C)-(IV).
  4. Conductivity 1/ρ = [M−1 L−3 T3 A2] → (D)-(II).

Answer: option (3) — (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

Q319CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q35key re-derived
The current flowing through a wire as a function of time is given as I = 3t2 + 2t + 5. The charge flowing through any cross-section of the wire in first 2 s is:
  1. 5 C
  2. 17 C
  3. 16 C
  4. 22 C

Q320CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q6key re-derived
The resistivity of a potentiometer wire is 10−7 Ω m and its cross-section area is 10−6 m2. When a current of 0.1 A flows through the wire, its potential gradient is:
  1. 10−1 V/m
  2. 10−2 V/m
  3. 10−4 V/m
  4. 10 V/m
Concept to recallPotential gradient k = V/L = I(R/L) = Iρ/A.
  1. k = Iρ/A = 0.1 × 10−7/10−6
  2. = 10−2 V/m.

Answer: option (2) — 10−2 V/m

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the potentiometer.
Q321CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q11NTA final key
Six equal resistances are connected between points P, Q and R as shown in the figure. The net resistance will be maximum between :
  1. P and Q
  2. Q and R
  3. P and R
  4. All points will have same resistance
Concept to recallBetween two corners of a triangle: the direct side in parallel with the other two sides in series.
  1. Sides: PQ = r, QR = r/2, PR = r/3.
  2. RPQ = r ∥ (r/2 + r/3) = r ∥ 5r/6 = 5r/11.
  3. RQR = (r/2) ∥ (4r/3) = 4r/11; RPR = (r/3) ∥ (3r/2) = 3r/11.
  4. Maximum: between P and Q.

Answer: option (1) — P and Q

Q322CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q47NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct ?
(A) The resistivity of a semiconductor decreases with increasing temperature.
(B) The potentiometer is unaffected by the internal resistance of the source.
(C) In ionic crystals and electrolytic liquids electrons carry the electric current.
(D) Ohm’s law fails if V depends on I non-linearly.
(E) Kirchhoff’s rules are used for analysis of electric circuits.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (B), (C) and (E) only
  2. (A), (B), (D) and (E) only
  3. (C), (D) and (E) only
  4. (A), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallElectrolytes conduct by ions; a null method draws no current from the cell being measured.
  1. (A) true (semiconductor). (B) true: at balance no current flows in the cell.
  2. (C) false: ions (positive and negative) carry the current. (D), (E) true.

Answer: option (2) — (A), (B), (D) and (E) only

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the potentiometer.
Q323CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q7NTA final key
Which of the following statement is correct for a potentiometer ?
  1. It cannot measure resistance
  2. It cannot measure the capacitance of a capacitor
  3. It cannot measure current
  4. It cannot measure potential difference
Concept to recallA potentiometer compares potential differences by a null method; from pd it also yields emf, internal resistance, an unknown resistance and (across a known resistor) a current.
  1. pd, emf, resistance and current (via V/R) can all be found with it.
  2. Capacitance is not a dc steady-state potential drop: it cannot be measured this way.

Answer: option (2) — It cannot measure the capacitance of a capacitor

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the potentiometer.
Q324CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q8NTA final key

List-IList-II

(B) Current density(II) [M−1 L−3 T3 A2]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
  2. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

Q325CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q9NTA final key
A bulb of 100 W glows for 6 hours a day. The units of energy consumed in 7 days would be :
  1. 2.4 units
  2. 4.2 units
  3. 600 units
  4. 4200 units
Concept to recall1 unit = 1 kWh; energy = P × t.
  1. Energy = 0.1 kW × 6 h × 7 = 4.2 kWh = 4.2 units.

Answer: option (2) — 4.2 units

Q326CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q11NTA final key
If three cells are connected in parallel as shown in figure, then equivalent emf would be:
  1. Eeq = Σi=03 Ei/ri ∕ Σi=03 ri
  2. Eeq = Σi=03 ri/Ei ∕ Σi=03 1/Ei
  3. Eeq = Σi=13 Ei/ri ∕ Σi=13 1/ri
  4. Eeq = Σi=13 ri/Ei ∕ Σi=13 ri
Concept to recallCells in parallel: 1/req = Σ1/ri and Eeq/req = ΣEi/ri.
  1. Each cell is a source Ei with internal resistance ri; the short-circuit currents Ei/ri add.
  2. So Eeq = (ΣEi/ri)/(Σ1/ri), with i running 1 to 3.

Answer: option (3) — Eeq = Σi=13 Ei/ri ∕ Σi=13 1/ri

TrapOptions with i = 0 count a fourth, non-existent cell.
Q327CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q7NTA final key
Two wires of copper have lengths L and 2L and cross sectional area 2A and A, respectively. The ratio of their specific resistance would be-
  1. 1:2
  2. 1:8
  3. 1:1
  4. 1:4
Concept to recallResistivity (specific resistance) is a property of the material and temperature only.
  1. Both are copper at the same temperature, so ρ1 : ρ2 = 1 : 1.

Answer: option (3) — 1:1

Trap1 : 4 is the ratio of their resistances (R = ρL/A), not resistivities.
Q328CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q8NTA final key
The drift speed of electrons in a conductor is estimated to be only a few mm s−1, But on closing a circuit, how current is established almost instantly in an electric circuit?
  1. Electrons are accelerated towards the positive end of the conductor while their velocity increases towards the other end
  2. Drift velocity of electrons increases
  3. Electric field is established throughout the circuit with the speed of an electromagnetic wave, causing at every point local electron drift causing current.
  4. The electrons drift towards the negative end
Concept to recallThe signal (electric field) travels at nearly the speed of light; the electrons themselves only drift slowly.
  1. On closing the switch the field is set up everywhere in the wire almost at once.
  2. Free electrons everywhere start drifting simultaneously, so current appears instantly.

Answer: option (3) — Electric field is established throughout the circuit with the speed of an electromagnetic wave, causing at every point local electron drift causing current.

Q329CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q9NTA final key
Six equal resistances each of 4 Ω are connected to form a network as shows in figure. The resistance between A and B would be:
  1. 2 Ω
  2. 4 Ω
  3. 1/2 Ω
  4. 1/4 Ω
Concept to recallSymmetry: points at equal potential carry no current between them (balanced Wheatstone bridge).
  1. Every pair of the four nodes A, B, C, O is joined by one 4 Ω resistor.
  2. By symmetry C and O are at the same potential, so the C–O resistor carries no current.
  3. Remaining: A–B (4) ∥ A–C–B (8) ∥ A–O–B (8): 1/R = 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/8 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω.

Answer: option (1) — 2 Ω

TrapIgnoring the bridge and adding series pairs blindly gives 4 Ω.
Q330CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q10NTA final key
A room heater is rated 750 W, 220 V. An electric bulb rated 200 W, 220 V is connected in series with this heater. What will be the power consumed by the bulb and the heater respectively, when the supply is at 220 V?
  1. PB = 124.8 W, PH = 33.25 W
  2. PB = 33.25 W, PH = 124.8 W
  3. PB = 124.8 W, PH = 124.8 W
  4. PB = 33.25 W, PH = 33.25 W
Concept to recallR = V2/Prated; in series the same current flows, so P = I2R ∝ R.
  1. RH = 2202/750 = 64.5 Ω; RB = 2202/200 = 242 Ω.
  2. I = 220/306.5 = 0.718 A.
  3. PB = 0.515 × 242 ≈ 124.7 W; PH = 0.515 × 64.5 ≈ 33.2 W.

Answer: option (1) — PB = 124.8 W, PH = 33.25 W

TrapIn series the lower-wattage bulb (higher R) takes the larger share.
Q331CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q11NTA final key
A cell of constant emf is first connected to a resistance R1 and then to R2. If power delivered in both cases are same, then the internal resistance of the cell is:
  1. √R1 R2
  2. √R1 / R2
  3. R1 + R22
  4. R1 − R22
Concept to recallP = ε2R/(R + r)2.
  1. R1/(R1 + r)2 = R2/(R2 + r)2.
  2. Cross-multiplying: (R1 − R2)(r2 − R1R2) = 0, so r = √(R1R2).

Answer: option (1) — √R1 R2

Q332CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q47NTA final key
Mobility of electrons
A. decreases with increase in potential difference
B. increases with increase in potential difference
C. does not depend on potential difference
D. decreases with decrease in temperature of conductor
E. independent to the temperature of conductor
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A and E only
  2. B and E only
  3. C and D only
  4. C and E only
Concept to recallMobility μ = vd/E = eτ/m: fixed by the relaxation time, not by the applied voltage.
  1. C is true: μ does not depend on the applied p.d.
  2. E is false: τ, hence μ, depends on temperature.
  3. NTA pairs C with D.

Answer: option (3) — C and D only

NoteDisagreement with the key: NTA’s final key gives “C and D”. In a metal, cooling reduces lattice collisions, so τ and the mobility increase as temperature falls; statement D is therefore false for a metallic conductor and only C is sound. Of the options, “C and D” is the only one containing C without the clearly false E, which is presumably why NTA chose it. The key is kept.
Q333CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q7NTA final key
Kirchhoff’s Second Law is based on law of conservation of:
  1. Charge
  2. Energy
  3. Momentum
  4. Mass and Energy
Concept to recallJunction rule ↔ charge; loop rule (ΣIR = Σε) ↔ energy.
  1. Going round a closed loop a charge returns to the same potential: net work zero, i.e. conservation of energy.

Answer: option (2) — Energy

Q334CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q8NTA final key
Identify the graph from the following showing the temperature dependence of resistivity for a typical semiconductor?
Concept to recallSemiconductor: ρ falls rapidly (roughly exponentially) as T rises, because carrier density grows.
  1. Metals: ρ rises roughly linearly with T (graph 1).
  2. Semiconductors: ρ decreases steeply and then levels off: graph 3.

Answer: option (3) —

Q335CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q9NTA final key
In a potentiometer arrangement a cell of 1.5 V gives a balance point at 45.0 cm length of the wire. If the cell is replaced by another cell and the balance point shifts to 75.0 cm, what is the emf of the second cell?
  1. 2.5 V
  2. 1.0 V
  3. 1.1 V
  4. 1.5 V
Concept to recallPotentiometer: ε ∝ balancing length, ε1/ε2 = l1/l2.
  1. ε2 = 1.5 × 75/45 = 2.5 V.

Answer: option (1) — 2.5 V

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the potentiometer.
Q336CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q10NTA final key
Drift velocity of electrons is directly proportional to the :
  1. Temperature
  2. Voltage applied
  3. Length of the conductor
  4. Area of cross section of conductor
Concept to recallvd = eEτ/m = eVτ/(mL).
  1. E = V/L, so vd = eτV/(mL) ∝ V.
  2. It is inversely proportional to L, independent of area, and falls with temperature (τ decreases).

Answer: option (2) — Voltage applied

Q337CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q7NTA final key
Find the value of current in the circuit.
  1. 4 A
  2. 3 A
  3. 2 A
  4. 1 A
Concept to recallA Wheatstone bridge with P/Q = R/S is balanced: the middle arm carries no current and can be removed.
  1. Name the junctions: L (battery +), P, M, N (battery −). Arms: LP, PN, LM, MN, and PM between them.
  2. All four arms are 2 Ω, so the bridge is balanced: no current in PM.
  3. R = (2 + 2) ∥ (2 + 2) = 2 Ω.
  4. i = 2 V / 2 Ω = 1 A.

Answer: option (4) — 1 A

TrapTreating all five resistors as series–parallel blocks gives 4 A or 2 A.
Q338CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q8NTA final key
A voltmeter of resistance 150 Ω is connected across A and B in the given circuit. The reading of the voltmeter will be :
  1. 40 V
  2. 20 V
  3. 15 V
  4. 25 V
Concept to recallA real voltmeter is a resistor in parallel with the part it measures; it lowers the reading.
  1. 100 Ω ∥ 150 Ω = 15000/250 = 60 Ω.
  2. Total R = 60 + 100 = 160 Ω; I = 40/160 = 0.25 A.
  3. VAB = 0.25 × 60 = 15 V.

Answer: option (3) — 15 V

Trap20 V is the reading of an ideal (infinite-resistance) voltmeter.
Q339CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q9NTA final key
A potentiometer with a cell of 2.4 volt and internal resistance of 2 Ω maintains a potential drop across the resistance wire AB of length 2 meters and resistance 10 Ω. A standard cell which maintains a constant emf of ‘V’ volt with internal resistance 0.2 Ω gives a balance point at 1.6 m length of the wire. The value of emf of second (standard) cell (V) is :
  1. 2.0 volt
  2. 1.9 volt
  3. 1.8 volt
  4. 1.6 volt
Concept to recallPotential gradient k = I Rwire/L; at balance no current flows in the cell, so its internal resistance does not matter: ε = k l.
  1. Driver current I = 2.4/(10 + 2) = 0.2 A.
  2. Gradient k = 0.2 × 10 / 2 = 1 V m−1.
  3. V = k × 1.6 = 1.6 V (the 0.2 Ω is irrelevant at balance).

Answer: option (4) — 1.6 volt

TrapForgetting the driver cell’s 2 Ω (k = 1.2 V/m) gives 1.9 V.

Q340CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q13 (NTA Q.No. 403)NTA final key
A positive charge enters a magnetic field and travels parallel to the magnetic field. The charge experiences
  1. an upward force
  2. a downward force
  3. a force in the direction of magnetic field.
  4. no force
Concept to recallF = qvB sin θ = 0 at θ = 0°.
  1. Velocity parallel to B: v × B = 0, so no force and the charge moves on in a straight line.

Answer: option (4) — no force

Q341CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q15 (NTA Q.No. 405)NTA final key

  1. πνer2
  2. πνr2e
  3. πνer
  4. πer2ν
Concept to recallA charge circulating at frequency ν is a current I = eν; magnetic moment m = IA.

  2. m = πνer2.

Answer: option (1) — πνer2

Q342CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q16 (NTA Q.No. 406)NTA final key
Identify the correct statements among the following.
A. The torque acting on a planar current loop in a magnetic field changes when its shape is changed without changing its area.
B. Two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions attract each other.
C. An ideal ammeter has zero resistance and an ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance.
D. A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting a high resistance in series.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B and C only
  2. B, C and D only
  3. C and D only
  4. A and C only
Concept to recallτ = NIAB sin θ depends on area, not shape; unlike currents repel; ammeter: low R in series, voltmeter: high R in parallel.

  2. C and D true.

Answer: option (3) — C and D only

Q343CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q17 (NTA Q.No. 407)NTA final key
A 0.5 m long solenoid has 500 turns and has a flux density of 2.52 x 10−3 T at its center. The current in the solenoid is (Given, μ0 = 4π × 10−7 H/m)
  1. 1.2 A
  2. 2.0 A
  3. 2.8 A
  4. 3.4 A
Concept to recallLong solenoid: B = μ0nI, n = N/l.
  1. n = 500/0.5 = 1000 m−1.
  2. I = 2.52 × 10−3/(4π × 10−7 × 1000) = 2.0 A.

Q344CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q19 (NTA Q.No. 409)NTA final key
A wire shown in figure carries a current of 10 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre O is: (Given: radius of the bent coil is 3 cm.)
  1. 1 × 10−4 T
  2. 1.57 × 10−3 T
  3. 1.57 × 10−4 T
  4. 2.41 × 10−5 T
Concept to recallArc of angle θ at its centre: B = (θ/2π)(μ0I/2R). A straight wire whose line passes through O gives zero field at O.
  1. The leads lie along radii, so only the 270° arc counts: fraction 3/4.
  2. B = ¾ × 4π × 10−7 × 10/(2 × 0.03) = 1.57 × 10−4 T.

Answer: option (3) — 1.57 × 10−4 T

TrapUsing the full loop (2.1 × 10−4 T) or forgetting the 2 in 2R.
Q345CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5 also 2026 18 May S1 Q5 (memory-based, collegedunia); 2026 18 May S2 Q5 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
A steady current I flows through a long straight wire of radius a. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wire at distances a/4 and 3a respectively from the axis of the wire is:
  1. 3 : 4
  2. 4 : 3
  3. 2 : 3
  4. 1 : 4
Concept to recallAmpere’s law: inside, B = μ0Ir/(2πa2) (B ∝ r); outside, B = μ0I/(2πr) (B ∝ 1/r).
  1. At a/4 (inside): B1 = μ0I(a/4)/(2πa2) = μ0I/(8πa).
  2. At 3a (outside): B2 = μ0I/(6πa).
  3. B1/B2 = 6/8 = 3/4.

Answer: option (1) — 3 : 4

TrapUsing 1/r for both points gives 12 : 1, not an option; using r for both gives 1 : 12.
Q346CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2 also 2026 18 May S2 Q2 (memory-based, collegedunia) (site key there printed the −1 option)key re-derived
Current I is flowing in conductor shaped as shown in the figure. The radius of the curved part is r and the length of straight portion is very large. The value of the magnetic field at the centre O will be
  1. (μ0I/4πr)(3π/2 + 1)
  2. (μ0I/4πr)(3π/2 − 1)
  3. (μ0I/4πr)(π/2 + 1)
  4. (μ0I/4πr)(π/2 − 1)
Concept to recallArc of angle θ: B = μ0Iθ/(4πr). Semi-infinite wire with O opposite one end: B = μ0I/(4πr). A wire whose line passes through O gives zero.
  1. Upper straight wire lies on the line through O: dl × r = 0, so it contributes nothing.
  2. Arc: three-quarters of a circle, θ = 3π/2, traversed clockwise: (μ0I/4πr)(3π/2), into the page.
  3. Lower straight wire: semi-infinite, distance r, current towards the arc: μ0I/(4πr), also into the page.
  4. Same direction, so add: B = (μ0I/4πr)(3π/2 + 1).

Answer: option (1) — (μ0I/4πr)(3π/2 + 1)

TrapTaking both straight wires at distance r makes them cancel or double; only the lower one is at distance r.
NoteThe 18 May S1 write-up gives (3π/2 + 1); the S2 write-up prints (3π/2 − 1) after cancelling the two straight wires against each other, which is wrong: the upper wire passes through O and contributes nothing.
Q347CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3 also 2026 18 May S2 Q3 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
The magnetic induction at the centre O in the figure shown is
  1. (μ0i/4)(1/R1 − 1/R2)
  2. (μ0i/4)(1/R1 + 1/R2)
  3. (μ0i/4)(R1 − R2)
  4. (μ0i/4)(R1 + R2)
Concept to recallA semicircle of radius R gives μ0i/(4R) at its centre; radial leads point at O and give nothing.
  1. Inner semicircle: μ0i/(4R1); outer: μ0i/(4R2).
  2. The current goes round them in opposite senses, so the fields oppose.
  3. B = (μ0i/4)(1/R1 − 1/R2).

Answer: option (1) — (μ0i/4)(1/R1 − 1/R2)

Q348CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4 also 2026 18 May S2 Q4 (memory-based, collegedunia)key re-derived
Three long, straight parallel wires, carrying current, are arranged as shown in figure. The force experienced by a 25 cm length of wire C is
  1. 10−3 N
  2. 2.5 × 10−3 N
  3. Zero
  4. 1.5 × 10−3 N
Concept to recallF/L = μ0I1I2/(2πd); parallel currents attract, antiparallel repel.
  1. D on C: (2 × 10−7)(30)(10)/0.03 = 2 × 10−3 N/m, repulsive (towards G).
  2. G on C: (2 × 10−7)(20)(10)/0.02 = 2 × 10−3 N/m, repulsive (towards D).
  3. Equal and opposite: net force on C is zero, whatever the length.

Answer: option (3) — Zero

Q349CUET 2026 · 18 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived
In the figure shown, the magnetic field induction at the point O will be
  1. μ0i/2πr
  2. (μ0/4π)(i/r)(π + 2)
  3. (μ0/4π)(i/r)(π + 1)
  4. (μ0i/4πr)(π − 2)
Concept to recallSemicircle: μ0i/(4r). Semi-infinite wire with O opposite its end: μ0i/(4πr).
  1. O is the centre of the semicircle, at distance r from each straight wire (they are 2r apart).
  2. Semicircle: (μ0/4π)(i/r)π; each straight wire: (μ0/4π)(i/r).
  3. Top current to the left, arc anticlockwise, bottom current to the right: all three out of the page.
  4. B = (μ0/4π)(i/r)(π + 2).

Answer: option (2) — (μ0/4π)(i/r)(π + 2)

Q350CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
The magnetic field at the center of a circular current carrying loop depends on:
  1. Only the radius of the loop
  2. Only the current flowing
  3. Current and radius of the loop
  4. Resistance of the wire only
Concept to recallB = μ0NI/(2R).
  1. B grows with I and falls with R, so it depends on both.

Answer: option (3) — Current and radius of the loop

Q351CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived
In a moving coil galvanometer, the magnetic field is made radial so that the:
  1. Resistance decreases
  2. Current sensitivity decreases
  3. Deflection becomes directly proportional to current
  4. Coil does not rotate
Concept to recallRadial field keeps the plane of the coil parallel to B at every deflection, so τ = NIAB (sin θ = 1).
  1. NIAB = kφ ⇒ φ = (NAB/k)I: a linear scale.

Answer: option (3) — Deflection becomes directly proportional to current

Q352CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived
A long solenoid has 1000 turns per meter and carries a current of 2 A. The magnetic field inside the solenoid is: (μ0 = 4π × 10−7 T m A−1)
  1. 8π × 10−4 T
  2. 4π × 10−4 T
  3. 2π × 10−4 T
  4. 16π × 10−4 T
Concept to recallInside a long solenoid B = μ0nI.
  1. B = (4π × 10−7)(1000)(2) = 8π × 10−4 T.

Answer: option (1) — 8π × 10−4 T

Q353CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5 also 2026 1 June S1 Q3 (memory-based, collegedunia) (date uncertain) (last option “Resistance of coil”)key re-derived
The magnetic field at the center of a circular coil carrying current is directly proportional to:
  1. Radius of coil
  2. Square of radius
  3. Current through coil
  4. Resistance of wire
Concept to recallB = μ0NI/(2R).
  1. B ∝ I (and ∝ 1/R, not R).

Answer: option (3) — Current through coil

Q354CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived
A charged particle enters perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The path followed by the particle is:
  1. Straight line
  2. Parabolic
  3. Circular
  4. Elliptical
Concept to recallF = qv × B is always perpendicular to v: constant speed, constant-magnitude centripetal force.
  1. qvB = mv2/r ⇒ r = mv/(qB): a circle.

Answer: option (3) — Circular

TrapA parabola is the path in a uniform electric field.
Q355CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived
A straight wire of mass 200 g and length 1.5 m carries a current of 2 A. It is suspended in mid-air by a uniform horizontal magnetic field B. The magnitude of B is (g = 10 m s−2):
  1. 2 T
  2. 1.5 T
  3. 0.55 T
  4. 0.67 T
Concept to recallSuspended in mid-air: BIl = mg (field perpendicular to the wire).
  1. B = mg/(Il) = (0.2 × 10)/(2 × 1.5) = 0.67 T.

Answer: option (4) — 0.67 T

Q356CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
A straight wire of mass 500 g and length 7 m carries a current of 1.4 A. It is suspended in mid-air by a uniform horizontal magnetic field B perpendicular to the length of the wire. The magnitude of the magnetic field is:
  1. 3.5 T
  2. 0.7 T
  3. 0.5 T
  4. 2.5 T
Concept to recallBIl = mg.
  1. B = (0.5 × 10)/(1.4 × 7) = 5/9.8 = 0.51 ≈ 0.5 T (with g = 9.8, exactly 0.5 T).

Answer: option (3) — 0.5 T

Q357CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
If a straight wire of length 175 cm and mass 250 g is suspended freely in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.7 T, then the current flowing through the wire is:
  1. 20 A
  2. 0.02 A
  3. 2 A
  4. 0.2 A
Concept to recallBIl = mg.
  1. I = mg/(Bl) = (0.25 × 9.8)/(0.7 × 1.75) = 2.45/1.225 = 2 A.

Answer: option (3) — 2 A

Q358CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
A wire carrying current i, bent as shown in the figure, is placed in a uniform magnetic field B directed normally out of the plane of the figure. The force on the wire is:
  1. 4BiR, directed vertically downward
  2. 3BiR, directed vertically upward
  3. Bi(2R + πR), directed vertically downward
  4. 2BiR, from P to Q
Concept to recallIn a uniform B, any wire feels the same force as a straight wire joining its ends: F = i Leff × B.
  1. End-to-end displacement: R + 2R + R = 4R, left to right.
  2. F = i(4R x̂) × (B ẑ) = 4BiR(−ŷ): 4BiR, vertically downward.

Answer: option (1) — 4BiR, directed vertically downward

TrapBi(2R + πR) uses the curved length instead of the chord.
Q359CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived
A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω gives full-scale deflection when a current of 2 mA passes through it. The value of shunt resistance required to convert it into an ammeter of range 2 A is
  1. 0.05 Ω
  2. 0.5 Ω
  3. 5 Ω
  4. 50 Ω
Concept to recallShunt in parallel: IgG = (I − Ig)S.
  1. S = IgG/(I − Ig) = (0.002 × 50)/(1.998) = 0.05 Ω.

Answer: option (1) — 0.05 Ω

Q360CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
A long straight conductor carries a current of 10 A. The magnetic field at a point 20 cm away from the conductor is (μ0 = 4π × 10−7 T m A−1)
  1. 1 × 10−5 T
  2. 2 × 10−5 T
  3. 5 × 10−6 T
  4. 4 × 10−5 T
Concept to recallLong straight wire: B = μ0I/(2πr).
  1. B = (2 × 10−7)(10)/0.20 = 1 × 10−5 T.

Answer: option (1) — 1 × 10−5 T

Q361CUET 2026 · file dated 6 June, headed 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
A circular coil carries a current of 4 A. If the current is doubled, the magnetic field at its centre becomes
  1. Half
  2. Double
  3. Four times
  4. Unchanged
Concept to recallB = μ0NI/(2R) ∝ I.
  1. Doubling I doubles B.

Answer: option (2) — Double

Q362CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q18NTA final key
A long wire with a small current element of length 1 cm is placed at the origin and carries a current of 10 A along the x-axis. The magnitude of the magnetic field, due to the element, on the y-axis at a distance 0.5 m from it, would be
  1. 4 × 10−8 T
  2. 5 × 10−8 T
  3. 6 × 10−8 T
  4. 2 × 10−8 T
Concept to recallBiot–Savart: dB = (μ0/4π) I dl sin θ / r2.
  1. dl along x, point on the y-axis: θ = 90°.
  2. dB = 10−7 × 10 × 0.01/(0.5)2 = 4 × 10−8 T.

Answer: option (1) — 4 × 10−8 T

Q363CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q19NTA final key
A conductor is placed along z-axis carrying current in z direction in uniform magnetic field directed along y-axis. The magnetic force acting on the conductor is directed along:
  1. positive x-axis
  2. positive y-axis
  3. positive z-axis
  4. negative x-axis
Concept to recallF = I l × B; cyclic order î → ĵ → k̂.
  1. F ∝ k̂ × ĵ = −î.
  2. So the force is along the negative x-axis.

Answer: option (4) — negative x-axis

Trapĵ × k̂ = +î is the reverse order and gives +x.
Q364CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q20NTA final key
A galvanometer of resistance 520 Ω is shunted with 20 Ω resistance to convert it into an ammeter. The resistance of the ammeter will be
  1. 16.8 Ω
  2. 540 Ω
  3. 19.3 Ω
  4. 18 Ω
Concept to recallAmmeter = galvanometer in parallel with a small shunt: RA = GS/(G + S).
  1. RA = 520 × 20/540 = 19.3 Ω (always a little less than the shunt).

Answer: option (3) — 19.3 Ω

Trap540 Ω adds them in series, which is how a voltmeter is made.
Q365CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q21NTA final key
The magnitude of magnetic field inside a solenoid of length 0.3 m having 800 turns carrying a current of 6 A is
  1. 2.03 T
  2. 60.3 mT
  3. 20 mT
  4. 6.03 T
Concept to recallLong solenoid: B = μ0nI, n = N/l.
  1. n = 800/0.3 = 2667 m−1.
  2. B = 4π × 10−7 × 2667 × 6 = 2.0 × 10−2 T = 20 mT.

Answer: option (3) — 20 mT

Q366CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q22NTA final key
A charged particle accelerated through a potential difference of V volts acquires a speed u. The particle is then made to enter perpendicularly in a uniform magnetic field B. The radius of the circular path followed by the charged particle will be proportional to
  1. V/u
  2. u/V
  3. V2/u2
  4. u2/V2
Concept to recallr = mu/(qB) and qV = ½mu2.
  1. From qV = ½mu2: m/q = 2V/u2.
  2. r = (m/q)(u/B) = (2V/u2)(u/B) = 2V/(uB) ∝ V/u.

Answer: option (1) — V/u

TrapWriting r ∝ u alone forgets that m/q is fixed by the accelerating voltage.
Q367CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q10 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A long straight conductor carries a current of 304 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field due to the current at a distance of 6 cm from the conductor is
  1. 3.002 mT
  2. 1003 mT
  3. 1.013 mT
  4. 2.012 T
Concept to recallLong straight wire: B = μ0I/(2πr).
  1. B = 2 × 10−7 × 304/0.06 = 1.013 × 10−3 T = 1.013 mT.

Answer: option (3) — 1.013 mT

Q368CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q22 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A proton enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T with speed v. It describes a semicircular path of radius 5 cm and comes out of the field. The final speed of the proton will be
  1. 0.5 v
  2. v
  3. 4 v
  4. 0.02 v
Concept to recallThe magnetic force qv × B is always perpendicular to v, so it does no work: speed is unchanged.
  1. Only the direction turns (by 180° on a semicircle); the kinetic energy is unchanged.
  2. Final speed = v. The values 0.2 T and 5 cm are not needed.

Answer: option (2) — v

TrapThe data tempt you to compute something; the answer needs none of them.
Q369CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q28 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A circular coil with 5 turns, each of radius 7 cm, carries a current of 1.4 A. The magnetic field at the center of the coil is:
  1. 10−5 T
  2. 2 × 10−5 T
  3. π × 10−5 T
  4. 2π × 10−5 T
Concept to recallCentre of a circular coil: B = μ0NI/(2R).
  1. B = 4π × 10−7 × 5 × 1.4/(2 × 0.07) = 4π × 10−7 × 50 = 2π × 10−5 T.

Answer: option (4) — 2π × 10−5 T

Q370CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q33 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Two concentric coils of radius 2π cm each are placed with their planes at right angles to each other and carry currents of 3 A and 4 A, respectively. The net magnetic field in Wb/m2 at the center of the coils will be
  1. 10−5
  2. zero
  3. 7 × 10−5
  4. 5 × 10−5
Concept to recallB = μ0I/(2R) at the centre, along the coil’s axis; perpendicular planes ⇒ perpendicular fields.
  1. R = 2π × 10−2 m: B1 = 4π × 10−7 × 3/(4π × 10−2) = 3 × 10−5 T; B2 = 4 × 10−5 T.
  2. B = √(32 + 42) × 10−5 = 5 × 10−5 T.

Answer: option (4) — 5 × 10−5

Trap7 × 10−5 adds the fields as scalars.
Q371CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q43 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
At an instant of time, a magnetic field is applied along the velocity of the particle. The acceleration produced in the particle will be
  1. along the velocity.
  2. Opposite to the direction of velocity.
  3. Perpendicular to the direction of velocity.
  4. Zero.
Concept to recallF = qvB sin θ; with B parallel to v, θ = 0 so F = 0.
  1. v × B = 0 when the two are parallel.
  2. No force ⇒ no acceleration; the particle keeps moving in a straight line.

Answer: option (4) — Zero.

Q372CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q25worked here
An electron moves with a velocity of 1200 m s−1 in a magnetic field of 0.4 T at an angle of 30°. What will be the approximate radius of its path? (Take e/m of electron = 1.76 × 1011 C kg−1)
  1. 9 × 10−8 m
  2. 8.6 × 10−9 m
  3. 4.4 × 10−10 m
  4. 1.5 × 10−11 m
Concept to recallOnly v⊥ = v sinθ bends the path: r = mv sinθ/(eB) (helix radius).
  1. v⊥ = 1200 × sin30° = 600 m s−1.
  2. r = 600/(1.76 × 1011 × 0.4) = 8.5 × 10−9 m ≈ 8.6 × 10−9 m.

Answer: option (2) — 8.6 × 10−9 m

TrapUsing the full 1200 m s−1 doubles the radius to 1.7 × 10−8 m.
Q373CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q29worked here
The frequency of revolution of an electron revolving in a circular path in a magnetic field of 7.8 × 10−4 T will be (Take e = −1.6 × 10−19 C, me = 9.1 × 10−31 kg, π = 22/7)
  1. 42 MHz
  2. 21.8 MHz
  3. 220 MHz
  4. 46 MHz
Concept to recallCyclotron frequency ν = qB/(2πm), independent of speed.
  1. ν = 1.6 × 10−19 × 7.8 × 10−4 / (2 × 22/7 × 9.1 × 10−31)
  2. = 1.248 × 10−22/5.72 × 10−30 = 2.18 × 107 Hz = 21.8 MHz.

Answer: option (2) — 21.8 MHz

TrapForgetting the 2π gives the angular frequency qB/m, about 137 × 106 rad s−1.
Q374CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q30worked here
Consider three long straight parallel wires as shown in the figure. Length of wire B is 25 cm. Choose the correct options
  1. (A) Net force experienced by wire B is 2 × 10−4 N towards left
  2. (B) Magnitude of repulsion force by wire A on B is 5 × 10−4 N
  3. (C) Magnitude of repulsion force by wire C on B is 2 × 10−4 N
  4. (D) Net force experienced by wire B is 2 × 10−4 N towards right
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (B) and (D) only
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallF = (μ0/2π) I1I2l/d; parallel currents attract, antiparallel repel.
  1. A on B (antiparallel, repel, pushes B right): 2 × 10−7 × 30 × 10 × 0.25/0.03 = 5 × 10−4 N. (B) true.
  2. C on B (antiparallel, repel, pushes B left): 2 × 10−7 × 20 × 10 × 0.25/0.05 = 2 × 10−4 N. (C) true.
  3. Net = 3 × 10−4 N to the right, so (A) and (D) are both false.

Answer: option (2) — (B) and (C) only

Q375CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q32worked here
The coil of a moving coil galvanometer is wound over a metallic frame
  1. to increase moment of inertia
  2. to provide electromagnetic damping
  3. to increase its sensitivity
  4. to reduce hysteresis loss
Concept to recallEddy currents induced in a moving conductor oppose its motion (Lenz).
  1. As the frame swings, eddy currents in it oppose the motion.
  2. So the coil settles quickly at its deflection: electromagnetic damping.

Answer: option (2) — to provide electromagnetic damping

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: eddy currents.
Q376CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q42worked here
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: Physical quantityList-II: Formula
(A) Current sensitivity of galvanometer(I) μ0I2R
(B) Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil(II) NABkR
(C) magnetic field due to a long straight wire carrying a current(III) NABk
(D) Voltage sensitivity of galvanometer(IV) μ0I2πR
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) – (III), (B) – (I), (C) – (II), (D) – (IV)
  2. (A) – (IV), (B) – (II), (C) – (III), (D) – (I)
  3. (A) – (III), (B) – (I), (C) – (IV), (D) – (II)
  4. (A) – (II), (B) – (I), (C) – (IV), (D) – (III)
Concept to recallφ/I = NAB/k; φ/V = NAB/(kR); centre of loop μ0I/2R; straight wire μ0I/2πR.
  1. (A) NAB/k (III); (B) μ0I/2R (I); (C) μ0I/2πR (IV); (D) NAB/kR (II).

Answer: option (3) — (A) – (III), (B) – (I), (C) – (IV), (D) – (II)

Q377CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q6worked here
A long straight wire of a circular cross-section of radius ‘a’ is carrying steady current I. The current I is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. What will be the magnetic field in the region r < a and r > a?
  1. B ∝ r (r < a) and B ∝ r−1 (r > a)
  2. B ∝ r (r > a) and B ∝ r−1 (r < a)
  3. B = 0 (r < a) and B ∝ r−1 (r > a)
  4. B ∝ r (r < a) and B = 0 (r > a)
Concept to recallAmpère: B(2πr) = μ0Ienclosed.
  1. Inside: Ienc = I r2/a2 ⇒ B = μ0Ir/(2πa2) ∝ r.
  2. Outside: Ienc = I ⇒ B = μ0I/(2πr) ∝ 1/r.

Answer: option (1) — B ∝ r (r < a) and B ∝ r−1 (r > a)

TrapB = 0 inside is true for a thin hollow tube, not a solid wire.
Q378CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q15worked here
To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter
  1. a very small resistance is added in series with the galvanometer
  2. a high resistance is added in series with the galvanometer
  3. a very small resistance is added in parallel with the galvanometer
  4. a high resistance is added in parallel with the galvanometer
Concept to recallAmmeter = galvanometer + low shunt S = IgG/(I − Ig) in parallel.
  1. Most of the current must bypass the coil, so a small resistance goes in parallel.

Answer: option (3) — a very small resistance is added in parallel with the galvanometer

Q379CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q23worked here
An ammeter should have very low resistance
  1. to show large deflection
  2. to generate less heat
  3. to protect the galvanometer from damage
  4. so that it may not change the value of the actual current in the circuit
Concept to recallAn ammeter goes in series; its resistance adds to the circuit.
  1. Near-zero resistance leaves the circuit current essentially unchanged.

Answer: option (4) — so that it may not change the value of the actual current in the circuit

Q380CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q31worked here
The overhead horizontal power transmission line carries a current of 75 A from east to west direction. The magnetic field above it at a vertical distance of 1.2 m will be
  1. 1.25 × 10−5 T, towards south
  2. 4.4 × 10−5 T, towards west
  3. 6.25 × 10−5 T, towards north
  4. 1.25 × 10−5 T, towards north
Concept to recallB = μ0I/(2πr); direction by the right-hand grip rule.
  1. B = 2 × 10−7 × 75/1.2 = 1.25 × 10−5 T.
  2. Thumb pointing west, the field lines above the wire point north (Î × r̂ = (−east) × up = north).

Answer: option (4) — 1.25 × 10−5 T, towards north

Q381CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q34worked here
Two long parallel wires separated by a distance of 2.50 cm, repel each other with a force of 4 × 10−5 N/m. The current in one wire is 0.5 A. The current in the second wire will be
  1. 5 A
  2. 10 A
  3. 4 A
  4. 0.5 A
Concept to recallF/l = μ0I1I2/(2πd).
  1. I2 = 4 × 10−5 × 0.025/(2 × 10−7 × 0.5) = 10 A (opposite direction, since they repel).

Q382CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q35worked here
Two particles P1 and P2, having equal charges accelerated by the same potential difference enter a region of a uniform magnetic field and describe circular paths of radii R1 and R2, respectively. The ratio of the mass of P1 to that of P2 will be
  1. (R1/R2)2
  2. (R1/R2)
  3. (R1/R2)0.5
  4. (R2/R1)2
Concept to recallr = mv/(qB) = √(2mK)/(qB) with K = qV.
  1. Same q, V, B: r ∝ √m.
  2. m1/m2 = (R1/R2)2.

Answer: option (1) — (R1/R2)2

Q383CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q39worked here
The radius of curvature of the path of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field is directly proportional to the
  1. charge of the particle
  2. momentum of the particle
  3. kinetic energy of the particle
  4. flux density of the field
Concept to recallr = p/(qB).
  1. r grows linearly with momentum p; it falls with q and B, and goes as √K.

Answer: option (2) — momentum of the particle

Q384CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q44worked here
A positive charge is moving vertically upwards. When it enters a region of magnetic field directed towards north, the direction of force on the charge would be
  1. East
  2. West
  3. North
  4. South
Concept to recallF⃗ = q v⃗ × B⃗.
  1. Take east = x̂, north = ŷ, up = ẑ.
  2. v⃗ × B⃗ = ẑ × ŷ = −x̂: west.

Answer: option (2) — West

Q385CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q50worked here
A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at an angle of 45° with the field. The path along which the particle moves in the field will be
  1. linear
  2. circular
  3. helical with axis along magnetic field
  4. helical with axis perpendicular to magnetic field
Concept to recallv∥ is unaffected by B; v⊥ gives circular motion.

Answer: option (3) — helical with axis along magnetic field

Q386CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q15worked here

Q388CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q26worked here
The sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer can be increased by decreasing

Q389CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q30worked here

Q390CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q42worked here

Q391CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q48worked here
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: ItemList-II: Property
(A) Shunt resistance(I) infinite resistance
(B) An ammeter resistance(II) connected in parallel with the galvanometer coil
(C) An ideal voltmeter(III) zero resistance
(D) An ideal ammeter(IV) less than that of the shunt resistance
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) – (I), (B) – (IV), (C) – (II), (D) – (III)
  2. (A) – (II), (B) – (IV), (C) – (I), (D) – (III)
  3. (A) – (III), (B) – (IV), (C) – (III), (D) – (I)
  4. (A) – (II), (B) – (I), (C) – (IV), (D) – (III)
Concept to recallAmmeter = G ∥ S, so RA = GS/(G + S) < S.
  1. Shunt: in parallel with the coil (II).
  2. Ammeter resistance: less than the shunt (IV).
  3. Ideal voltmeter: infinite (I). Ideal ammeter: zero (III).

Answer: option (2) — (A) – (II), (B) – (IV), (C) – (I), (D) – (III)

Q392CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q9worked here
Two concentric coils, each of radius 2π cm, are placed at right angles to each other. Currents of 3 A and 4 A respectively are flowing through the two coils. The magnetic induction at the center of the coils will be:
  1. 50 μT
  2. 70 μT
  3. 12 μT
  4. 0.1 μT

  1. R = 0.02π m: B1 = 4π × 10−7 × 3/(0.04π) = 30 μT; B2 = 40 μT.
  2. B = √(302 + 402) = 50 μT.

Q393CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q1 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The dipole moment of a circular loop carrying a current I is m and the magnetic field at the centre of the loop is B1. When the dipole moment is made three times by keeping the current I same, the magnetic field at the centre of the loop becomes B2. The ratio of B1 and B2 is:
  1. √2 : 1
  2. 2 : 1
  3. √3 : 1
  4. 1 : √3
Concept to recallm = IπR2; field at the centre of a loop B = μ0I/2R.
  1. Same I, m × 3 ⇒ R2 × 3 ⇒ R2 = √3 R1.
  2. B ∝ 1/R ⇒ B1/B2 = R2/R1 = √3.

Answer: option (3) — √3 : 1

TrapB falls when the loop grows, so the ratio is √3 : 1, not 1 : √3.
Q394CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q11 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A charge moving ________ to the direction of the magnetic field does not experience any magnetic Lorentz force.
(A) parallel
(B) perpendicular
(C) antiparallel
(D) at any acute angle

  1. (A) and (B) only
  2. (B) and (D) only
  3. (A) and (C) only
  4. (A) and (D) only
Concept to recallF = qvB sin θ vanishes for θ = 0° or 180°.
  1. Parallel: sin 0° = 0. Antiparallel: sin 180° = 0.
  2. Perpendicular gives the maximum force; an acute angle gives a non-zero force.

Answer: option (3) — (A) and (C) only

Q395CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q14 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Two long and parallel straight wires A and B carrying currents of 8.0 A and 5.0 A in the same direction are separated by a distance of 4.0 cm. Estimate the force on 10 cm length of wire B:

  2. 5 × 10−5 N, attractive
  3. 2 × 10−5 N, attractive
  4. 2 × 10−5 N, repulsive

Answer: option (3) — 2 × 10−5 N, attractive

Q396CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q4 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A proton moves from south to north with a speed of 2 × 107 m/s. When a magnetic field is applied from west to east, the proton gets an acceleration of 1012 m/s2. The mass of the proton is 1.6 × 10−27 kg. The value of the magnetic field is:
  1. 5 × 10−4 T
  2. 5 × 10−5 T
  3. 1 × 10−3 T
  4. 1 × 10−4 T
Concept to recallLorentz force F = qvB sin θ (θ = 90° here) = ma.
  1. B = ma/qv = (1.6 × 10−27 × 1012)/(1.6 × 10−19 × 2 × 107).
  2. = 10−15/(2 × 10−12) = 5 × 10−4 T.

Answer: option (1) — 5 × 10−4 T

Q397CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q9 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The figure shows a current loop having two circular arcs joined by two radial lines. If radius OA is ‘a’ and OD is ‘b’, the magnetic field at the centre O is:
  1. (θ/2π)(μ0i/2a)
  2. (θ/2π)(μ0/2b)
  3. (θ/2π)(μ0i/2)((b − a)/ab)
  4. zero
Concept to recallArc of angle θ at its centre: B = (θ/2π)(μ0i/2r). Radial segments point at O and give zero field there.
  1. The two arcs carry current in opposite senses about O, so their fields at O are opposite.
  2. Inner arc (radius a) is the stronger: B = (θ/2π)(μ0i/2)(1/a − 1/b).
  3. = (θ/2π)(μ0i/2)(b − a)/ab.

Answer: option (3) — (θ/2π)(μ0i/2)((b − a)/ab)

TrapThe radial lines DA and CB contribute nothing (dl × r = 0), and the arcs subtract, they do not add.
Q398CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q10NTA final key
In the circuit shown below, a current 3I enters at A. The semicircular parts ABC and ADC have equal radii ‘r’ but resistances 2R and R respectively. The magnetic field at the center of the circular loop ABCD is ___________.
  1. μ0I4r out of the plane
  2. μ0I4r into the plane
  3. μ03I4r out of the plane
  4. μ03I4r into the plane
Concept to recallA semicircle of radius r carrying current i gives μ0i/(4r) at its centre; parallel branches share current inversely as resistance.
  1. ABC (2R) carries I; ADC (R) carries 2I.
  2. ABC (left to right over the top) runs clockwise ⇒ μ0I/(4r) into the plane.
  3. ADC (left to right along the bottom) runs anticlockwise ⇒ μ0(2I)/(4r) out of the plane.
  4. Net: μ0I/(4r) out of the plane.

Answer: option (1) — μ0I4r out of the plane

TrapSplitting the current equally makes the two halves cancel; adding magnitudes gives 3μ0I/4r.
Q399CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q11NTA final key
A square loop with each side 1 cm, carrying a current of 10 A, is placed in a magnetic field of 0.2 T. The direction of magnetic field is parallel to the plane of the loop. The torque experienced by the loop is _____.
  1. zero
  2. 2 × 10−4 Nm
  3. 2 × 10−2 Nm
  4. 2 Nm
Concept to recallτ = NIAB sinθ, θ between the area vector (normal) and B.
  1. B in the plane ⇒ normal ⊥ B, θ = 90°.
  2. τ = 10 × (10−2)2 × 0.2 = 2 × 10−4 N m.

Answer: option (2) — 2 × 10−4 Nm

Trap“Field parallel to the plane” is the position of maximum torque, not zero.
Q400CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q31NTA final key
A wire carrying current I, bent as shown in the figure, is placed in a uniform field B that emerges normally out from the plane of the figure. The force on this wire is ____________.
  1. 4BIR, directed vertically downward
  2. 3BIR, directed vertically upward
  3. BI (2R + πR), vertically downward
  4. 2π BIR, from P to Q
Concept to recallIn a uniform field the force on any current-carrying wire equals that on the straight line joining its ends: F = I(L⃗ × B⃗).
  1. PQ = R + 2R + R = 4R, so |F| = 4BIR.
  2. Direction: I along +x, B along +z (out): x̂ × ẑ = −ŷ, vertically downward.

Answer: option (1) — 4BIR, directed vertically downward

TrapUsing the arc length πR for the semicircle gives BI(2R + πR).
Q401CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q9NTA final key
Two infinitely long straight parallel conductors carrying currents I1 and I2 are held at a distance d apart in vacuum. The force F on a length L of one of the conductors due to the other is ____________.
  1. proportional to L but independent of I1 × I2
  2. proportional to I1 × I2 but independent of length L
  3. proportional to I1 × I2 × L
  4. proportional to LI1 × I2
Concept to recallF = μ0I1I2L/(2πd).
  1. The field of one wire at the other is μ0I1/(2πd).
  2. Force on length L of the second: F = I2LB = μ0I1I2L/(2πd) ∝ I1I2L.

Answer: option (3) — proportional to I1 × I2 × L

Q402CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q638NTA final key

Q403CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q647NTA final key
A galvanometer with resistance 100 Ohm gives full scale deflection with a current of 2 mA. The resistance required to convert galvanometer into ammeter of range 0 to 20 A is nearly :

Q404CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q663NTA final key

Q405CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q664NTA final key
Current through ABC and A′B′C′ is I as shown in the given figure. If PB = PB′ = r and C′B′PBC are collinear, the magnetic field at P is :
  1. 2I/4πr
  2. 2μ0I/4πr

List-I RuleList-II Statement

Q407CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q683NTA final key

Q408CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q25 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In the situation shown in the figure, the straight wire is fixed but the loop can move under magnetic force. The loop will:
  1. remains stationary
  2. moves towards the wire
  3. moves away from the wire
  4. rotates about the wire
Concept to recallParallel currents attract, antiparallel repel; the force falls as 1/r.
  1. The near side of the loop carries current parallel to i1: attracted.
  2. The far side carries the opposite current: repelled, but it is farther away so the force is weaker.
  3. The forces on the two horizontal sides cancel. Net force: towards the wire.

Answer: option (2) — moves towards the wire

Q409CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q35 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
If charge is moving parallel to uniform magnetic field, its path will be:

  2. circular

Q410CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q49 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Current carrying wire produces:
  1. Electric field only

  4. Electric flux only

  1. Moving charges → magnetic field (Oersted); net charge zero → no external electric field.

Q411CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q5 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Two identical circular wires P and Q each of radius R and carrying current I are kept in perpendicular planes such that they have a common centre as shown in figure. Find the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic field at the common centre of the two coils
  1. zero
  2. √32 μ0IR, β = 60°
  3. μ0I√2R, β = 45°
  4. I, β = 90°
Concept to recallCentre of a circular loop: B = μ0I/2R along the loop's axis. Fields add as vectors.
  1. Each coil gives B0 = μ0I/2R, along its own axis.
  2. The planes are perpendicular, so the two axes (and the two fields) are perpendicular.
  3. B = √2 B0 = √2 μ0I/2R = μ0I/(√2 R), at β = 45° to either field (equal components).

Answer: option (3) — μ0I√2R, β = 45°

Q413CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q16 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following statements are correct?

Q415CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q47 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q417CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q24 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q418CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q6 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  3. All four sides add in the same direction: B = 4B1 = 2√2 μ0I/(πL).

Q423CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q29 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A long wire carrying current I is bent in the form of a circle as shown in the figure. The B⃗ at point O is:
  1. (μ0/4π)(2I/r)(1 − π) perpendicularly outward
  2. (μ0/4π)(2πI/r) perpendicularly inward
  3. (μ0/4π)(2I/r)(1 + π) perpendicularly outward
  4. (μ0/4π)(2I/r)(1 + π) perpendicularly inward
Concept to recallInfinite straight wire: B = μ0I/2πr. Circular turn at its centre: B = μ0I/2r.
  1. Straight wire at distance r: (μ0/4π)(2I/r).
  2. Loop: μ0I/2r = (μ0/4π)(2πI/r), in the same direction (the wire runs on into the turn the same way round).
  3. Total (μ0/4π)(2I/r)(1 + π). With the current left to right along the top, the field below the wire is into the page.

Answer: option (4) — (μ0/4π)(2I/r)(1 + π) perpendicularly inward

NoteThe Prepp figure shows no current arrow; the direction (inward) assumes the current runs left to right, as the label I at the left end suggests. Prepp prints the options as “μ0/4π = 2I/r(1 + π)”; the stray “=” is read as a product.
Q424CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q6 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The wire loop PQRSP formed by joining two semicircular wires of radii R1 & R2 carries a current I as shown in the fig. The magnitude of magnetic field at the centre C is
  1. μ0I/2 (1/R1 + 1/R2)
  2. μ0I/4 (1/R1 + 1/R2)
  3. μ0I/2 (1/R1 − 1/R2)
  4. μ0I/4 (1/R1 − 1/R2)
Concept to recallA semicircular arc of radius R gives μ0I/4R at its centre; the straight parts through the centre give nothing.
  1. PQ and RS point at C: dl × r = 0, no field.
  2. The current goes round the two arcs in opposite senses, so their fields oppose.
  3. B = μ0I/4R1 − μ0I/4R2 = (μ0I/4)(1/R1 − 1/R2).

Answer: option (4) — μ0I/4 (1/R1 − 1/R2)

TrapA full loop gives μ0I/2R; a semicircle gives half of that.
Q425CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q8 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A neutron is moving with a velocity of V in non-uniform magnetic field as shown in figure. Velocity v⃗ of neutron would be
  1. Maximum at B
  2. Same at A, B and C
  3. Minimum at A and C
  4. Maximum at A and C
Concept to recallThe magnetic force qv × B needs a charge; a neutron has none.
  1. q = 0 ⇒ F = 0 everywhere, whatever the field strength.
  2. No force, so the velocity is unchanged: the same at A, B and C.

Answer: option (2) — Same at A, B and C

TrapThe crowding of field lines is a distractor; it would matter only for a charged particle (and even then the speed would not change).
Q426CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q29worked here
A charged particle having charge q is moving in a circle of radius R with a uniform speed υ. The associated magnetic moment μ is given by:
  1. qυR2
  2. qυ2R2
  3. qυR22
  4. qυR
Concept to recallAn orbiting charge is a current I = q/T = qυ/(2πR); μ = IA.
  1. μ = [qυ/(2πR)] × πR2 = qυR/2.

Answer: option (1) — qυR2

Q427CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q38worked here
A proton is moving in a circular path of radius R in a uniform magnetic field B. It carries a kinetic energy of 2 MeV. What should be the energy of an α-particle to move in a circle of same radius in the same field?
  1. 1 MeV
  2. 2 MeV
  3. 4 MeV
  4. 3 MeV
Concept to recallr = p/(qB) = √(2mK)/(qB) ⇒ for equal r and B, K ∝ q2/m.
  1. α: q = 2e, m = 4mp ⇒ q2/m = 4/4 = same as the proton.
  2. Kα = 2 MeV.

Answer: option (2) — 2 MeV

Q428CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q42worked here
A moving coil galvanometer has N number of turns in the coil with area A. It carries a current I and the magnetic field is B. The torque acting on the coil is:
  1. NIB2A2
  2. NI2BA
  3. N2IBA
  4. NIBA
Concept to recallTorque on a coil τ = NIAB sin θ; the radial field of a galvanometer keeps sin θ = 1.
  1. τ = NIBA (radial field).

Answer: option (4) — NIBA

Q429CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q49worked here
A moving charge produces:
  1. magnetic field only
  2. electric field only
  3. magnetic field and electric field both
  4. neither electric field nor magnetic field
Concept to recallAny charge has an electric field; a moving charge (a current) also produces a magnetic field (Biot–Savart).
  1. The electric field does not switch off when the charge moves; motion adds a magnetic field.

Answer: option (3) — magnetic field and electric field both

Q430CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q11 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A long straight wire of circular cross section with radius a carries steady current I which is uniformly distributed across the cross-section. The magnetic field in the region r < a and r > a is represented by:
Concept to recallAmpère’s law: inside, B = μ0Ir/2πa2 (∝ r); outside, B = μ0I/2πr (∝ 1/r).
  1. Inside: enclosed current Ir2/a2 ⇒ B rises linearly from 0 at the axis.
  2. Maximum at r = a, then a 1/r curve (not a straight line) outside.
  3. Graph (4).

Answer: option (4) —

TrapGraphs (2) and (3) fall in a straight line outside; 1/r is a hyperbola that never reaches zero.
Q431CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q25 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A 300 turns rectangular coil of length 20 cm and breadth 12 cm is carrying a current of 12 A, when placed in a magnetic field of 6 T. The plane of the coil is making an angle of 60° with the magnetic field. What is the torque acting on the coil?
  1. 518.4 N m
  2. 259.2 N m
  3. 447.8 N m
  4. 366.6 N m
Concept to recallτ = NIAB sin θ, with θ the angle between B and the normal to the coil.
  1. Plane at 60° to B ⇒ normal at 30°.
  2. τ = 300 × 12 × (0.20 × 0.12) × 6 × sin 30°
  3. = 518.4 × 0.5 = 259.2 N m.

Answer: option (2) — 259.2 N m

TrapUsing sin 60° (angle with the plane) gives 448.9 N m; 518.4 N m is the maximum torque.
Q432CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q30 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
An alpha-particle moves with a speed of (5 × 105 î) m s−1. It enters a region where there is a magnetic field of magnitude 4 T, directed at an angle of 45° to the X-axis and lying in XY plane. The magnitude of magnetic force on alpha particle is:
  1. 1.6 × 10−14 N
  2. 3.2 × 10−13 N
  3. 4.5 × 10−13 N
  4. 1.6 × 10−13 N
Concept to recallF = qvB sin θ; an α-particle carries q = 2e.
  1. F = 2 × 1.6 × 10−19 × 5 × 105 × 4 × sin 45°
  2. = 6.4 × 10−13 × 0.707 = 4.5 × 10−13 N.

Answer: option (3) — 4.5 × 10−13 N

TrapUsing q = e gives half the answer.
Q433CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q39 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
An electron moves around the nucleus in a hydrogen atom of radius 0.05 nm with a velocity of 2 × 106 m s−1. The magnetic field produced at the center of nucleus is:
  1. 0.128 T
  2. 6.4 T
  3. 128 T
  4. 12.8 T
Concept to recallAn orbiting charge is a current I = ev/2πr; at the centre B = μ0I/2r = μ0ev/4πr2.
  1. B = 10−7 × 1.6 × 10−19 × 2 × 106/(5 × 10−11)2
  2. = 3.2 × 10−20/2.5 × 10−21 = 12.8 T.

Q434CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q43 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
(A) 1 T(I) V s
(B) 1 H(II) 1 m2 A
(C) J T−1(III) Wb/m2
(D) 1 Wb(IV) Wb/A

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  2. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
  3. (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
