  1. T = Wb/m2 (III); H = Wb/A (IV).
  2. J/T is the unit of magnetic moment = A m2 (II); Wb = V s (I).

Answer: option (4) — (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

Q435CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q14key re-derived
A very long solenoid has 800 turns per unit length. A current of 1.6 A flows through it. Then the magnetic induction in the middle of the solenoid on its axis is approximately:
  1. 16 × 10−4 T
  2. 8 × 10−4 T
  3. 32 × 10−4 T
  4. 4 × 10−4 T
Concept to recallInside a long solenoid B = μ0nI (at the ends it is half this).
  1. B = 4π × 10−7 × 800 × 1.6
  2. = 1.61 × 10−3 ≈ 16 × 10−4 T.

Answer: option (1) — 16 × 10−4 T

Trap8 × 10−4 T is the field at an end.
Q436CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q16key re-derived
An insulating rod of length L carries charge q distributed uniformly on it. The rod is pivoted at one end and is rotated at a frequency f about a fixed perpendicular axis. Then the magnetic dipole moment of the system is:
  1. πqfL2
  2. (1/3)πqfL2
  3. qfL
  4. qfL2
Concept to recallA charge dq going round f times a second is a current dq·f; its loop moment is (current) × (area).
  1. Slice at distance x: dq = (q/L)dx, current dI = f dq, area πx2.
  2. m = ∫0L (qf/L)πx2 dx = πqfL2/3.

Answer: option (2) — (1/3)πqfL2

TrapπqfL2 puts all the charge at the far end.
Q437CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q30key re-derived
An electron enters a crossed electrical and magnetic field region with a speed of 100 m s−1 along +x-axis and passes undeviated. The strength of magnetic field is 5.0 T and it acts along +z-axis. Give the electrical field in vector notations indicating its magnitude as well as direction:
  1. (500 V m−1)ĵ
  2. −(500 V m−1)k̂
  3. (100 V m−1)ĵ
  4. −(100 V m−1)k̂
Concept to recallVelocity selector: undeviated when qE = −q(v × B), i.e. E = −v × B, |E| = vB.
  1. |E| = vB = 100 × 5 = 500 V/m.
  2. v × B = 500(î × k̂) = −500 ĵ, so E = −v × B = +500 ĵ V/m.
  3. Check with the electron: magnetic force −e(v×B) is along +ĵ, electric force −eE along −ĵ: they cancel.

Answer: option (1) — (500 V m−1)ĵ

TrapE = −v × B holds for either sign of charge; the electron’s sign flips both forces together.
Q438CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q45key re-derived
What uniform magnetic field applied perpendicular to a beam of electrons moving at 1.3 × 106 m/s, is required to make the electrons travel in a circular arc of radius 0.35 m?
  1. 2.1 × 10−5 G
  2. 6 × 10−5 T
  3. 2.1 × 10−5 T
  4. 6 × 10−5 G
Concept to recallCircular motion in B: r = mv/(qB) ⇒ B = mv/(qr).
  1. B = 9.1 × 10−31 × 1.3 × 106/(1.6 × 10−19 × 0.35)
  2. = 2.1 × 10−5 T.

Answer: option (3) — 2.1 × 10−5 T

TrapSame number in gauss (option 1) is 104 times too small: 1 T = 104 G.
Q439CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q48key re-derived
A strong magnetic field is applied on a stationary electron:
  1. The electron moves in the direction of the field
  2. The electron moves in an opposite direction
  3. The electron remains stationary
  4. The electron starts spinning
Concept to recallMagnetic force F = q(v × B) is zero when v = 0.
  1. v = 0 ⇒ F = 0, so the electron stays at rest.

Answer: option (3) — The electron remains stationary

Q440CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q16NTA final key
For a long wire carrying a current of 10 A, the magnitude of magnetic field at a point 4 cm away from it will be :
  1. 4 × 10−5 T
  2. 2 × 10−5 T
  3. 10−5 T
  4. 5 × 10−5 T
Concept to recallB = μ0I/(2πr) = 2 × 10−7 I/r.
  1. B = 2 × 10−7 × 10/0.04 = 5 × 10−5 T.

Answer: option (4) — 5 × 10−5 T

Q441CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q17NTA final key
A charge of 5 μC moves with a speed of 2 × 106 m/s along the positive y-axis. A magnetic field B of strength (2î + k̂)T exists in space. The magnetic force acting on the charge is :
  1. (−20k̂ + 10î) N
  2. (20k̂ − 10î) N
  3. (20k̂ + 10î) N
  4. (10î + 5k̂) N
Concept to recallF = q(v × B); ĵ × î = −k̂, ĵ × k̂ = î.
  1. qv = 5 × 10−6 × 2 × 106 = 10, along ĵ.
  2. F = 10 ĵ × (2î + k̂) = 10(−2k̂ + î) = (−20k̂ + 10î) N.

Answer: option (1) — (−20k̂ + 10î) N

TrapWriting ĵ × î = +k̂ flips the k̂ component.
Q442CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q10NTA final key
A galvanometer having a resistance of 8 Ω is shunted by a wire of resistance 2 Ω. If the current is 1 A, the part of it passing through the shunt will be:
  1. 0.25 A
  2. 0.78 A
  3. 0.2 A
  4. 0.8 A
Concept to recallParallel branches share current in inverse ratio of resistance: Is = I · G/(G + S).
  1. Is = 1 × 8/(8 + 2) = 0.8 A (and 0.2 A through the galvanometer).

Answer: option (4) — 0.8 A

Trap0.2 A is the galvanometer’s share.
Q443CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q14 also CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q13 (same options in the order: low–series, high–series, high–parallel, low–parallel; NTA key: low resistance in parallel)NTA final key
Which of the following is connected to the coil of the galvanometer, to protect it from possible damages due to large current ?
  1. High resistance wire in parallel
  2. Low resistance wire in parallel
  3. High resistance wire in series
  4. Low resistance wire in series
Concept to recallA shunt is a low resistance in parallel with the galvanometer; it bypasses most of the current.
  1. A low resistance in parallel carries the bulk of a large current, so only a small, safe fraction passes through the coil.

Answer: option (2) — Low resistance wire in parallel

TrapA high resistance in series converts it into a voltmeter; it limits current but is not the protective shunt.
Q444CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q15NTA final key
If a copper wire carries a direct current, the magnetic field associated with the current would be:
  1. Only inside the wire
  2. Only outside the wire
  3. Both inside and outside of the wire
  4. No magnetic field would exists due to direct current
Concept to recallAmpere’s law for a long straight wire: outside B = μ0I/2πr; inside a uniform wire B = μ0Ir/2πR2.
  1. The NCERT picture of the field of a current is circles around the wire, i.e. outside it; that is the answer NTA keeps.
  2. Strictly, Ampere’s law also gives a field inside a thick wire, rising linearly from zero on the axis.

Answer: option (2) — Only outside the wire

NoteNTA’s final key gives “Only outside the wire”. By Ampere’s law the field is non-zero inside a wire of finite thickness too (B ∝ r), so “both inside and outside” is the physically complete answer. The key is kept as published.
Q445CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q16NTA final key
A wire is bent as shown in figure is placed in a uniform field B that emerges from the plane of the paper, outward as shown. The magnitude of force on the given wire is :
  1. 4BIR
  2. BI(πR)
  3. BIR(2 + π)
  4. Zero
Concept to recallIn a uniform field the force on any current-carrying wire equals I Leff × B, where Leff joins its ends.
  1. Ends A and E are R + 2R + R = 4R apart in a straight line.
  2. Leff ⊥ B, so F = BI(4R) = 4BIR.

Answer: option (1) — 4BIR

TrapUsing the wire’s actual length (2R + πR) gives BIR(2 + π).
Q446CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q17NTA final key
What is the magnetic force acting on a proton (charge +1.6 × 10−19 C) moving at an angle of 30° across a magnetic field of 5.3 × 10−3 T at a speed of 3.0 × 105 m s−1?
  1. 1.272 × 10−19 N
  2. 1.3 × 10−16 N
  3. 1.272 × 1016 N
  4. 2.2 × 10−16 N
Concept to recallF = qvB sin θ.
  1. F = 1.6 × 10−19 × 3 × 105 × 5.3 × 10−3 × 0.5 = 1.27 × 10−16 N ≈ 1.3 × 10−16 N.

Answer: option (2) — 1.3 × 10−16 N

TrapUsing sin 60° (= cos 30°) gives 2.2 × 10−16 N.
Q447CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q14NTA final key
The charge which is a source of electric field but not of magnetic field is -
  1. A charge moving in a straight line
  2. A charge static in space having zero speed
  3. A charge moving on helical path of pitch
  4. A charge oscillating with frequency ‘ν’
Concept to recallEvery charge produces E; only a moving charge produces B.
  1. A charge at rest produces only an electrostatic field.

Answer: option (2) — A charge static in space having zero speed

Q448CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q15NTA final key
There is a thin conducting wire carrying current. The value of magnetic field induction at any point on the conductor would be:
  1. Zero
  2. Constant
  3. Positive
  4. Negative
Concept to recallBiot–Savart: dB ∝ I dl × r; for points along the line of the current dl × r = 0.
  1. A point on (the axis of) a thin straight wire lies along the direction of every current element.
  2. sin θ = 0 for each element, so B = 0.

Answer: option (1) — Zero

Q449CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q17NTA final key
Magnetic field |B| at a point P in the following network is:
  1. μ0I4πR(32π)
  2. μ0I4πR(32π + 2)
  3. μ0I4πR(32π − 2)
  4. 32 μ0IR
Concept to recallArc of angle θ: B = μ0Iθ/(4πR). Semi-infinite wire with P on the perpendicular through its end: B = μ0I/(4πR).
  1. Arc (3/4 circle, θ = 3π/2): B = (μ0I/4πR)(3π/2).
  2. Each straight wire is tangent at an end of the arc, so P is at distance R on the perpendicular through its end: B = μ0I/(4πR) each.
  3. In both wires the current circulates about P opposite to the arc’s sense, so their fields oppose it.
  4. Net: (μ0I/4πR)(3π/2 − 2).

Answer: option (3) — μ0I4πR(32π − 2)

TrapAdding the straight-wire fields (option 2) ignores their direction.
Q450CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q12NTA final key
A proton and an alpha particle moving with same kinetic energy enter in the region of uniform magnetic field perpendicular to it. The ratio of radii of their trajectories will be :
  1. 1 : 1
  2. √2 : 1
  3. 4 : 1
  4. 1 : √2
Concept to recallr = mv/(qB) = √(2mK)/(qB).
  1. r ∝ √m / q at equal K and B.
  2. Proton: √m/e. Alpha: √(4m)/(2e) = √m/e.
  3. rp : rα = 1 : 1.

Answer: option (1) — 1 : 1

TrapAt equal speed the ratio would be 1 : 2; at equal accelerating voltage, 1 : √2.
Q451CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q13NTA final key
An electron is projected in a uniform magnetic field along the direction of field, the electron will experience :
  1. a force opposite to the magnetic field
  2. a force in the direction of magnetic field
  3. no force in magnetic field
  4. a force perpendicular to the magnetic field
Concept to recallF = q(v × B) = qvB sinθ.
  1. v is parallel to B: θ = 0, sinθ = 0.
  2. F = 0; the electron moves on in a straight line.

Answer: option (3) — no force in magnetic field

Q452CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q14NTA final key
Magnetic field due to the current carrying wire as shown in the figure at point “O” will be :
  1. μ0 I2 R
  2. μ0 I4 R
  3. μ0 I2 π R
  4. μ0 I4 π R
Concept to recallArc of angle θ at its centre: B = (μ0I/4πR)θ. A straight wire gives no field at a point on its own line.
  1. The two straight parts point straight at O: dl × r = 0, no field.
  2. Semicircle (θ = π): B = μ0Iπ/(4πR) = μ0I/(4R).

Answer: option (2) — μ0 I4 R

Trapμ0I/2R is the full circular loop.
Q453CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q15NTA final key
An electron is shot into the uniform magnetic field, normal to the direction of field. Then the frequency of revolution of the electron in its circular orbit :
  1. is independent of its speed
  2. decreases with its speed
  3. increases with its speed
  4. increase with radius of revolution
Concept to recallCyclotron frequency f = qB/(2πm), independent of v and r.
  1. r = mv/(qB), so T = 2πr/v = 2πm/(qB).
  2. Faster electrons move on bigger circles in the same time: f does not depend on speed.

Answer: option (1) — is independent of its speed

Q454CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q16NTA final key
To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter, one should connect :
  1. high resistance in series with galvanometer
  2. low resistance in series with galvanometer
  3. low resistance in parallel with galvanometer
  4. high resistance in parallel with galvanometer
Concept to recallAmmeter: low shunt S = IgG/(I − Ig) in parallel. Voltmeter: high R in series.
  1. Most of the current must bypass the galvanometer, so a small resistance (shunt) goes in parallel.
  2. The ammeter’s total resistance is then small, as it should be for a series instrument.

Answer: option (3) — low resistance in parallel with galvanometer

TrapHigh resistance in series converts it into a voltmeter.
Q455CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q17NTA final key
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The electric field produced by a scalar source is known as electric charge.
Statement II : The magnetic field produced by a vector source is known as current element (I dl).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. Both Statement I and Statement II are true
  2. Both Statement I and Statement II are false
  3. Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
  4. Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Concept to recallCoulomb’s law: the source of E is the scalar charge q. Biot–Savart law: the source of B is the vector current element I dl.
  1. The (awkwardly worded) statements mean: E is produced by a scalar source, the charge; B is produced by a vector source, the current element I dl.
  2. Both are what NCERT says when comparing Coulomb and Biot–Savart: both true.

Answer: option (1) — Both Statement I and Statement II are true

Magnetism and Matter40 questions

Q456CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q14 (NTA Q.No. 404)NTA final key
If a ferromagnetic material is inserted in a current carrying solenoid, the magnetic field inside the solenoid
  1. increases
  2. decreases
  3. remains unchanged
  4. becomes zero
Concept to recallWith a core, B = μ0μrnI; ferromagnets have μr ≫ 1.
  1. The core magnetises along the field and adds its own field: B increases enormously (the electromagnet).

Answer: option (1) — increases

Q457CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q18 (NTA Q.No. 408)NTA final key
A bar magnet of dipole moment 3 Am2 rests with its centre on a frictionless point. A force F is applied at right angles to the axis of the magnet, 10 cm from the point. It is observed that an external magnetic field of 0.25 T is required to hold the magnet in equilibrium at an angle of 30° with the field. The value of F is:
  1. 2.75 N
  2. 2.93 N
  3. 3.75 N
  4. 4.08 N
Concept to recallRotational equilibrium: torque of F (= Fd) balances the magnetic torque mB sin θ.
  1. mB sin 30° = 3 × 0.25 × 0.5 = 0.375 N m.
  2. F = 0.375/0.10 = 3.75 N.

Answer: option (3) — 3.75 N

Q458CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8worked here
A solenoid has a core made of material with relative permeability 400. The magnetic field produced in the interior of solenoid is 1.0 T. The magnetic intensity in SI units is α × 105. The value of α is ________. (Given: μ0 = 4π × 10−7 SI units)
  1. 25/π
  2. 1/16π
  3. 1/π
  4. 1/4π
Concept to recallB = μ0μrH, so H = B/(μ0μr).
  1. H = 1.0/(4π × 10−7 × 400) = 1/(16π × 10−5) = (1/16π) × 105 A/m.
  2. So α = 1/16π (H ≈ 2.0 × 103 A/m).

Answer: option (2) — 1/16π

TrapDropping μr gives H 400 times too large.
NoteThe site prints 25/π, which would make H = 8 × 105 A/m: that is B/(μ0) with the μr = 400 left out. With the core included, α = 1/16π.
Q459CUET 2026 · 29 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
The most exotic diamagnetic materials are superconductors. They exhibit perfect diamagnetism and perfect conductivity. The values of magnetic susceptibility (χ) and relative permeability (μr) for such materials are:
  1. χ = 1, μr = 0
  2. χ = −1, μr = 0
  3. χ = 0, μr = 1
  4. χ = −1, μr = 1
Concept to recallμr = 1 + χ. Perfect diamagnet (Meissner effect): B = 0 inside.
  1. B = μ0μrH = 0 ⇒ μr = 0 ⇒ χ = μr − 1 = −1.

Answer: option (2) — χ = −1, μr = 0

Q460CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q16NTA final key

  4. 25 A m

Answer: option (4) — 25 A m

Q461CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q17NTA final key
Match List-I with List-II

(B) Magnetic moment(II) T m A−1
(C) Pole strength(III) J T−1 m−1
(D) Permeability of free space(IV) Wb m−2

  2. (A) – (IV), (B) – (I), (C) – (III), (D) – (II)

  4. (A) – (IV), (B) – (III), (C) – (I), (D) – (II)
Concept to recallB in tesla = Wb m−2; U = −m·B gives m in J T−1; qm = m/(2l) in J T−1 m−1 (= A m); B = μ0I/(2πr) gives μ0 in T m A−1.
  1. (A) field → Wb m−2 (IV).
  2. (B) moment → J T−1 (I).
  3. (C) pole strength = moment/length → J T−1 m−1 (III).

Q462CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q2 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following properties are desired in materials for permanent magnets ?
  1. (A) High retentivity
  2. (B) High coercivity
  3. (C) High permeability
  4. (D) low permeability
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (D) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B) and (C) only
  4. (A) and (C) only
Concept to recallPermanent magnet (e.g. steel, alnico): high retentivity, so a strong magnetisation remains when the field is removed, and high coercivity, so stray fields, heat or knocks cannot easily demagnetise it.
  1. (A) and (B) are the two essential properties, so the answer must contain both.
  2. Only “(A), (B) and (C) only” does. The textbook line it follows: a high permeability lets the material be magnetised strongly when it is made into a magnet.
  3. (C) and (D) contradict each other, so at most one of them can be in the answer.

Answer: option (3) — (A), (B) and (C) only

Trap“(A) and (D) only” leaves out high coercivity, the property that keeps a permanent magnet magnetised.
NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: hysteresis (retentivity, coercivity). Judgement call: no official key could be matched to this re-typeset. Strictly, permeability is not a criterion for a permanent magnet, and hard magnetic materials such as steel in fact have a lower permeability than soft iron. But every option that includes (D) leaves out (B), which is certainly desired. The standard textbook statement (high retentivity, high coercivity and high permeability), and the key a third-party mock gives, both point to (A), (B) and (C).
Q463CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q24 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

TrapDropping the π gives the second option.

Q466CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q36worked here

Q467CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q24 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q469CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q40NTA final key

Q470CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q41NTA final key

Q471CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q8NTA final key

Q472CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q649NTA final key

Q474CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q34 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Choose the correct statements:

  1. A & C only

  3. D & E only
  4. B, C & D only

Q475CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q20 · Prepp reconstructionworked here
When temperature of a ferromagnetic material is increased by 20%, What is the percentage change in it's magnetic susceptibility?
  1. 16.7%
  2. 83.3%
  3. 1.67%
  4. 8.33%
Concept to recallCurie law (the intended model here): χ = C/T, so χ ∝ 1/T.
  1. T′ = 1.2 T ⇒ χ′ = χ/1.2 = 0.833 χ.
  2. Change = 1 − 0.833 = 0.167, i.e. a 16.7% decrease.

Answer: option (1) — 16.7%

Trap83.3% is the new value as a percentage of the old, not the change.
NotePrepp's unofficial key gives option (3); the working above shows why that cannot be right. The question means Curie's law (strictly that is for paramagnets; above TC a ferromagnet follows χ ∝ 1/(T − TC), which needs TC and gives none of the options).

  3. high permeability and high hysteresis loss
  4. low permeability and low hysteresis loss
Concept to recallTransformer core: soft iron, i.e. high μ (links the flux) and a narrow hysteresis loop (little energy lost per cycle).
  1. The core is magnetised and demagnetised 50 times a second: loss per cycle (loop area) must be small.
  2. High permeability concentrates the flux between the coils.

Answer: option (2) — high permeability and low hysteresis loss

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: hysteresis (retentivity, coercivity).
Q492CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q12NTA final key
Ferromagnetic material core used for transformer must have
  1. low permeability and low hysteresis loss
  2. low permeability and high hysteresis loss
  3. high permeability and low hysteresis loss
  4. high permeability and high hysteresis loss
Concept to recallTransformer core: carry flux easily (high μ) and waste little energy per cycle (thin hysteresis loop, low retentivity and coercivity).
  1. High permeability links nearly all the flux to the secondary.
  2. The core is magnetised and demagnetised 50 times a second, so its hysteresis loss must be small (soft iron).

Answer: option (3) — high permeability and low hysteresis loss

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: hysteresis (retentivity, coercivity).
Q493CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q13NTA final key
A bar magnet when suspended horizontally and perpendicular to earth’s field experiences a torque of 3 × 10−4 N m. The Magnetic moment of the magnet would be:
(take horizontal component of Earth’s magnetic field at the place 0.4 × 10−4 T)
  1. 7.5 J T−1
  2. 5.7 J T−1
  3. 0.75 J T−1
  4. 0.57 J T−1
Concept to recallτ = mB sin θ; perpendicular means θ = 90°.
  1. m = τ/BH = 3 × 10−4/(0.4 × 10−4) = 7.5 J T−1.

Answer: option (1) — 7.5 J T−1

Q494CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q12NTA final key
A uniform magnetic field, parallel to the plane of the paper existed in space initially directed from left to right. When a bar of soft iron is placed in the field parallel to it, the lines of force passing through it will be represented by:
Concept to recallSoft iron is ferromagnetic (μr ≫ 1): field lines crowd into it.
  1. A ferromagnet draws the lines into itself, so they crowd together through the bar (picture 2).
  2. Lines bulging away from the bar (picture 3) describe a diamagnet; undisturbed lines describe a non-magnetic material.

Answer: option (2) —

Q495CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q16NTA final key
The coercivity of a bar magnet is 140 A m−1. To demagnetize it, it is placed inside a solenoid of length 1.6 m and number of turns 112. What is the current flowing through the solenoid?
  1. 9 A
  2. 2.25 A
  3. 2 A
  4. 1.25 A
Concept to recallInside a solenoid H = nI = (N/l)I; demagnetise by applying H equal to the coercivity.
  1. I = Hl/N = 140 × 1.6/112 = 2 A.

Answer: option (3) — 2 A

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: hysteresis (retentivity, coercivity).

Electromagnetic Induction73 questions

Q496CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q20 (NTA Q.No. 410)NTA final key
The mutual inductance of a pair of coils placed close to each other depends upon
  1. The rate at which currents are changing in the two coils.
  2. Relative position and orientation of the two coils
  3. The materials of the wires of the coils
  4. The current in the two coils
Concept to recallM is geometric: turns, areas, separation, orientation and the core’s permeability; not currents or their rates.
  1. M = μ0n1n2Al for coaxial solenoids — only geometry (and core).
  2. Currents and their rates decide the emf, not M.

Answer: option (2) — Relative position and orientation of the two coils

Q497CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q21 (NTA Q.No. 411)NTA final key
If the number of turns in a coil is tripled, the value of the magnetic flux linked with the coil:
  1. remains unchanged
  2. becomes 13 times
  3. is tripled
  4. becomes 23 times
Concept to recallFlux linkage = NΦper turn.
  1. Same field and area per turn: total flux linked NBA triples with N.

Answer: option (3) — is tripled

NoteRead “flux linked” as flux linkage NΦ, which is what NTA’s key assumes; the flux through a single turn would not change.
Q498CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q25 (NTA Q.No. 415)NTA final key
A coil with an average diameter of 0.02 m is placed with its plane perpendicular to a magnetic field of 6000 T. The induced emf in the coil is 11 V, when the magnetic field is changed to 1000 T in 4 s. The number of turns in the coil is
  1. 16
  2. 18
  3. 24
  4. 28
Concept to recallFaraday: |ε| = NA|ΔB|/Δt.
  1. A = π(0.01)2 = 3.14 × 10−4 m2; ΔB/Δt = 5000/4 = 1250 T/s.
  2. emf per turn = 0.393 V; N = 11/0.393 = 28.

Answer: option (4) — 28

TrapUse the radius 0.01 m, not the diameter 0.02 m, in πr2.
NoteThe fields (thousands of tesla) are unphysical but the arithmetic is what is tested.
Q499CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q8key re-derived
Let a rod AB of length l having resistance r is moving perpendicular to a magnetic field B with constant velocity v. If the ends of the rod are connected to a wire PQRS of negligible resistance, then current passing through the wire will be:
  1. Blv/2r
  2. Blv/r
  3. Blv/4
  4. 3Blv/4r
Concept to recallMotional emf ε = Blv; the rod is the source with internal resistance r, and the external wire has none.
  1. emf in the rod: ε = Blv.
  2. Total resistance of the loop = r + 0 = r, so I = Blv/r.

Answer: option (2) — Blv/r

NoteThe set prints no figure; the slide draws the usual arrangement (rod sliding on a frame PQRS).
Q500CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived
The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
  1. Tesla
  2. Weber
  3. Henry
  4. Coulomb
Concept to recallΦ = BA: T m2 = weber (Wb).
  1. Tesla is the unit of B, henry of inductance; flux is in weber.

Answer: option (2) — Weber

Q501CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
A circular current loop of radius R is placed inside a square loop of side length L (L ≫ R) such that they are co-planar and their centers coincide. The permeability of free space is μ0. The mutual inductance between circular loop and square loop is ________.
  1. 2√2 μ0L2/R
  2. √2 μ0L2/R
  3. √2 μ0R2/L
  4. 2√2 μ0R2/L
Concept to recallM = Φ/I: drive current in the big loop, find its (nearly uniform) field at the centre and multiply by the small area. Each side of a square at distance L/2 gives μ0I(2 sin 45°)/(4π(L/2)).
  1. Centre of the square: B = 4 × μ0I(√2)/(4π(L/2)) = 2√2 μ0I/(πL).
  2. Flux through the circle: Φ = BπR2 = 2√2 μ0IR2/L.
  3. M = Φ/I = 2√2 μ0R2/L.

Answer: option (4) — 2√2 μ0R2/L

Q502CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
The self inductance of a coil depends upon:
  1. Number of turns only
  2. Magnetic permeability of core only
  3. Geometry of coil and medium
  4. Current flowing through coil
Concept to recallSolenoid: L = μrμ0n2Al: turns, size, shape and core.
  1. L depends on N, area, length and μ of the core, but not on the current.

Answer: option (3) — Geometry of coil and medium

Q503CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
Two coils have mutual inductance 0.5 H. If the current in the primary coil changes at the rate of 4 A s−1, the induced emf in the secondary coil is
  1. 0.5 V
  2. 1 V
  3. 2 V
  4. 4 V
Concept to recallε2 = −M dI1/dt.
  1. |ε| = 0.5 × 4 = 2 V.

Answer: option (3) — 2 V

Q504CUET 2026 · file dated 6 June, headed 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
A coil experiences a change in magnetic flux from 0.2 Wb to 0.8 Wb in 0.1 s. The average induced emf in the coil is
  1. 2 V
  2. 4 V
  3. 6 V
  4. 8 V
Concept to recallFaraday: |ε| = ΔΦ/Δt.
  1. |ε| = (0.8 − 0.2)/0.1 = 6 V.

Answer: option (3) — 6 V

Q505CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q23NTA final key
Figure shows a coil C connected to a galvanometer G. When the North-pole of a bar magnet is pushed towards the coil, the pointer in the galvanometer deflects. Regarding this set up, the following statements are given:
  1. (A) It indicates the presence of electric current in the coil.
  2. (B) The deflection is found to be smaller when the magnet is pushed towards the coil faster.
  3. (C) There is repulsion in the moving magnet and the magnetic pole induced in the coil facing towards the N pole of the magnet.
  4. (D) If the bar magnet does not move, there is no induced current in the coil.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (C) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallFaraday: |ε| = |dΦ/dt|; Lenz: the induced current opposes the change (an approaching N pole meets an N face).
  1. Deflection = induced current: (A) true.
  2. Faster motion ⇒ faster flux change ⇒ larger emf and deflection: (B) false.
  3. The coil face towards the magnet becomes an N pole, so it repels the approaching magnet: (C) true.
  4. No relative motion ⇒ no change of flux ⇒ no current: (D) true.

Answer: option (1) — (A), (C) and (D) only

Q506CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q24NTA final key
Figure shows a rectangular conductor PQRS in which the conductor PQ is free to move. The conductor PQ is moved towards the left with a constant velocity V as shown in the figure. Assume that there is no loss of energy due to friction. What will be the magnetic flux linked with the loop PQRS and the motional emf?
  1. Magnetic flux = Bl(xV); Motional emf = Blx
  2. Magnetic flux = Blx; Motional emf = (BlV)/t
  3. Magnetic flux = Blx; Motional emf = BlV
  4. Magnetic flux = B/(lx); Motional emf = BlV
Concept to recallΦ = B × (enclosed area); motional emf |ε| = |dΦ/dt| = Bl|dx/dt| = BlV.
  1. Area of PQRS = l × x, so Φ = Blx.
  2. x decreases at the rate V, so |ε| = Bl|dx/dt| = BlV.

Answer: option (3) — Magnetic flux = Blx; Motional emf = BlV

Q507CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q25NTA final key
The average emf induced in a coil is 2 V when current is changed in 0.4 s
  1. (A) from 5 A to 2 A and the self-inductance of the coil is 0.266 mH
  2. (B) from 4 A to 4 A in the opposite direction, the self-inductance of the coil is 0.10 mH
  1. (A) is correct, (B) is incorrect
  2. Both (A) and (B) are correct
  3. (A) is incorrect, (B) is correct
  4. Both (A) and (B) are incorrect
Concept to recall|ε| = L ΔI/Δt, so L = |ε|Δt/ΔI. Reversing 4 A to −4 A is a change of 8 A.
  1. (A) ΔI = 3 A: L = 2 × 0.4/3 = 0.267 H, not 0.266 mH.
  2. (B) ΔI = 4 − (−4) = 8 A: L = 2 × 0.4/8 = 0.10 H, not 0.10 mH.
  3. Both numbers are right but the unit is wrong (H, not mH), so both statements are incorrect.

Answer: option (4) — Both (A) and (B) are incorrect

TrapThe numbers match, so it is tempting to call both correct; the prefix “m” makes each 1000 times too small.
Q508CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q27NTA final key
A 12 V battery connected to a 6 Ω, 10 mH coil through a switch drives a constant current in the circuit. The switch is suddenly opened. Assuming that it took 1 ms to open the switch, the average emf induced across the coil would be
  1. 10 V
  2. 20 V
  3. 200 V
  4. 12 V
Concept to recallSteady current I = V/R (the inductor has no effect on dc); on breaking, |ε| = LΔI/Δt.
  1. I = 12/6 = 2 A, falling to 0 in 1 ms.
  2. ε = 10 × 10−3 × 2/10−3 = 20 V.

Answer: option (2) — 20 V

Q509CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q29NTA final key
Which of the following statements is not correct for electromagnetic induction?
  1. The magnitude of induced emf in a circuit is equal to the time rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit.
  2. The magnitude of induced emf in a circuit is equal to the total change of magnetic flux through the circuit.
  3. The induced emf can be increased by increasing the number of turns N of a closed coil.
  4. The polarity of induced emf is such that it tends to produce a current which opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it
Concept to recallFaraday: ε = −N dΦ/dt (a rate, not a total change); Lenz fixes the sign.
  1. The emf equals the rate of change of flux, not the total change: that statement is wrong.
  2. The rate statement, ε ∝ N, and Lenz’s law are all correct.

Answer: option (2) — The magnitude of induced emf in a circuit is equal to the total change of magnetic flux through the circuit.

Q510CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q13 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In Faraday’s experiment on Electromagnetic Induction, in which of the following situations, more deflection will be shown by the galvanometer?
  1. magnet is at rest inside the coil
  2. magnet is accelerated towards the coil
  3. magnet is in uniform motion towards the coil
  4. magnet is decelerated away from the coil
Concept to recallDeflection ∝ induced emf ∝ rate of change of flux, which grows with the magnet’s speed and closeness.
  1. At rest: no change of flux, no deflection.
  2. Accelerating towards the coil: speed and nearness both increase, so dΦ/dt is largest.
  3. Uniform approach is smaller; decelerating away is smaller still.

Answer: option (2) — magnet is accelerated towards the coil

Q511CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q18 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Two long coaxial solenoids of the same length L have inner and outer coils with diameters D1 and D2 and number of turns N1 and N2, respectively. What will be the ratio of the self-inductance of the inner solenoid to the mutual inductance of both the solenoids?
  1. N1N2−1
  2. N2N1−1
  3. N2D22/(N1D12)
  4. N2D2/(N1D1)
Concept to recallL1 = μ0N12A1/L; M = μ0N1N2A1/L (the flux is confined to the inner area A1).
  1. L1/M = N12A1/(N1N2A1) = N1/N2 = N1N2−1.

Answer: option (1) — N1N2−1

TrapUsing the outer area A2 in M brings in D2; the common flux only fills the inner coil.
Q512CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q21 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The magnetic flux through a coil placed in a magnetic field is given by φ = 5t3 + 4t2 + 2t − 5 Wb. The resistance of the coil is 10 Ω. The induced current through the coil at t = 2 s is:
  1. 7.8 A
  2. 15.6 A
  3. 0.78 A
  4. 3.9 A
Concept to recall|ε| = dφ/dt; I = ε/R.
  1. dφ/dt = 15t2 + 8t + 2 = 60 + 16 + 2 = 78 V at t = 2 s.
  2. I = 78/10 = 7.8 A.

Answer: option (1) — 7.8 A

Q513CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q34 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In a coil, the current is changed from 12 A to 24 A in 1 s. The self-induced emf of the coil is 24 V. The change in energy in the coil is
  1. 432J
  2. 360 J
  3. 216 J
  4. 108 J
Concept to recallL = εΔt/ΔI; energy stored U = ½LI2.
  1. L = 24 × 1/12 = 2 H.
  2. ΔU = ½ × 2 × (242 − 122) = 576 − 144 = 432 J.

Answer: option (1) — 432J

Trap½L(ΔI)2 = 144 J is not the change in energy.
Q514CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q42 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A magnetic field energy of 34 × 10−6 J is stored in an inductor of inductance 1.7 mH in an LC circuit. The current flowing in the inductor is:
  1. 0.141 A
  2. 0.2 A
  3. 1.41 A
  4. 0.004 A
Concept to recallEnergy in an inductor U = ½LI2.
  1. I2 = 2U/L = 68 × 10−6/(1.7 × 10−3) = 0.04.
  2. I = 0.2 A.

Answer: option (2) — 0.2 A

Trap0.141 A forgets the factor 2 (I2 = U/L).
Q515CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q1worked here
The elements which may be considered for an ideal inductor as a solenoid,
  1. (A) which is made of a thick wire
  2. (B) which has negligible resistance
  3. (C) which has a sufficiently large inductance
  4. (D) which is made of a thin wire
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (C) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallAn ideal inductor stores energy in its magnetic field and dissipates none: R → 0, L large.
  1. Negligible resistance (B) and large inductance (C) define an ideal inductor.
  2. A thick wire has small resistance (R = ρl/A), so (A) helps; a thin wire raises R, so (D) is wrong.
  3. Correct set: (A), (B), (C).

Answer: option (1) — (A), (B) and (C) only

TrapA thin wire lets you wind more turns, but it adds resistance, which an ideal inductor must not have.
Q516CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q17worked here
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: FormulaList-II: Physical Quantity
(A) ε = −L dI/dt(I) Self inductance
(B) ε = −M dI/dt(II) Mutual inductance
(C) L = Φ/I(III) Mutual Induced emf
(D) M = Φ/I(IV) Self Induced emf
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) – (I), (B) – (II), (C) – (III), (D) – (IV)
  2. (A) – (IV), (B) – (III), (C) – (I), (D) – (II)
  3. (A) – (I), (B) – (II), (C) – (IV), (D) – (III)
  4. (A) – (III), (B) – (IV), (C) – (I), (D) – (II)
Concept to recallSelf: Φ = LI, ε = −L dI/dt. Mutual: Φ2 = MI1, ε2 = −M dI1/dt.
  1. (A) self-induced emf (IV); (B) mutually induced emf (III); (C) self inductance (I); (D) mutual inductance (II).

Q517CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q20worked here
The armature coil of a generator has 20 turns and its area is 0.127 m2. How fast approximately should it be rotated in a magnetic field of 0.2 Wb m−2, so that the peak value of induced emf is 160 V?
  1. 20 rps
  2. 50 rps
  3. 100 rps
  4. 200 rps
Concept to recallAC generator: ε0 = NBAω, ω = 2πν.
  1. ω = 160/(20 × 0.2 × 0.127) = 315 rad s−1.
  2. ν = 315/2π ≈ 50 rps.

Q518CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q44worked here
A 1.0 m long metallic rod is rotated with an angular frequency of 500 rad s−1 with one end hinged at the center and the other end at the circumference of a circular metallic ring of radius 1 m about an axis passing through the center and perpendicular to the plane of the ring. A constant and uniform magnetic field of 0.6 T parallel to the axis exists everywhere. The emf developed between the center and the ring is
  1. 300 V
  2. 375 V
  3. 225 V
  4. 150 V

Q519CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q10worked here
An aeroplane having a wing span of 40 m flies due north at a speed of 100 m s−1 in magnetic field 5 × 10−5 T acting vertically downward. The potential difference between the tips of the wings is
  1. 0.2 V
  2. 0.5 V
  3. 0.8 V
  4. 2.0 V
Concept to recallMotional emf ε = Bvlv (vertical component, wings horizontal).
  1. ε = 5 × 10−5 × 40 × 100 = 0.2 V.

Q520CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q29worked here
In which of the following cases emf would be induced-
  1. When a coil and a magnet move with the same velocity in the same direction.
  2. When a magnet is rotated about its own axis.
  3. Whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes even if the circuit is open.
  4. When a closed loop moves totally inside a uniform magnetic field.
Concept to recallFaraday: ε = −dΦ/dt, whether or not a current can flow.
  1. Options 1, 2 and 4 leave the linked flux unchanged: no emf.
  2. Any change of flux induces an emf; an open circuit simply carries no current.

Q521CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q5worked here

  2. 2.4 mV
  3. 1.6 mV
  4. 3.2 mV
Concept to recallFaraday: |ε| = rate at which flux is cut, ΔΦ/Δt.
  1. The wire sweeps through (cuts) 8 × 10−4 Wb in 0.5 s.
  2. ε = 8 × 10−4/0.5 = 1.6 × 10−3 V = 1.6 mV.

Answer: option (3) — 1.6 mV

NoteRepaired reading: the paper says the wire is dragged “in the region of magnetic flux 8 × 10−4 Wb in 0.5 s”; the only sensible meaning, and the one every option assumes, is that it cuts that much flux in 0.5 s.
Q522CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q3worked here
If both the number of turns and length of an inductor are tripled, keeping other factors constant, the self-inductance of the inductor will be
  1. tripled

Concept to recallSolenoid: L = μ0N2A/l.

  2. L grows 9/3 = 3 times.

Q523CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q34worked here
The mutual inductance of a pair of solenoids depends on

Q524CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q40worked here
The magnetic flux through a coil perpendicular to the plane is varying according to the relation φ = (7t3 + 3t2 − 2t − 2) Wb. If the resistance of the coil is 10 Ω, the induced current through the coil at t = 2 s, will be

Q525CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q18 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q526CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q46 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

  1. remains the same

Q527CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q50 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A 10 cm long air-core solenoid of cross-sectional area 1.0 cm2 contains 300 turns. Its inductance is:
  1. 36π × 10−6 H
  2. 4π × 10−6 H
  3. 4π × 10−5 H
  4. 36 × 10−6 H
Concept to recallLong solenoid: L = μ0N2A/l.
  1. L = 4π × 10−7 × 3002 × 10−4/0.1.
  2. = 4π × 10−7 × 90 = 360π × 10−7 = 36π × 10−6 H.

Answer: option (1) — 36π × 10−6 H

TrapDropping the π gives the last option.
Q528CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q7 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Two coaxial solenoids having number of turns per unit length 50 and 200, respectively, have same length 50 cm. The area of cross-section of the two solenoids are 4 cm2 and 6 cm2, respectively. The mutual inductance of the two solenoids is:
  1. 8π × 10−3 H
  2. 4π × 10−4 H
  3. 8π × 10−7 H
  4. 1.6π × 10−2 H
Concept to recallCoaxial solenoids: M = μ0n1n2Al, with A the area of the inner (smaller) solenoid.
  1. A = 4 cm2 = 4 × 10−4 m2, l = 0.5 m.
  2. M = 4π × 10−7 × 50 × 200 × 4 × 10−4 × 0.5 = 8π × 10−7 H.

Answer: option (3) — 8π × 10−7 H

TrapUsing the outer area (6 cm2) overcounts: only the flux through the inner solenoid links both.
Q529CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q13NTA final key
In a pair of adjacent coils, for a change of current in one of the coils from 0 A to 10 A in 0.25 s, the magnetic flux in the adjacent coil changes by 15 Wb. The mutual inductance of the coils is ______.
  1. 120 H
  2. 12 H
  3. 1.5 H
  4. 0.75 H
Concept to recallNΦ2 = M I1 ⇒ M = ΔΦ/ΔI.
  1. M = 15 Wb / 10 A = 1.5 H. The time 0.25 s is not needed.

Answer: option (3) — 1.5 H

TrapThe 0.25 s is a distractor: M relates flux to current, not to its rate of change.
Q530CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q14NTA final key
A wire of irregular shape in figure (a) and a circular loop of wire in figure (b) are placed in different uniform magnetic fields as shown in the figures below. In figure (a), the magnetic field is perpendicular into the plane. In figure (b), the magnetic field is perpendicular out of the plane.
The wire in figure (a) is turning into a circular loop and that in figure (b) into a narrow straight wire. The direction of induced current will be ____________.
  1. clockwise in both (a) and (b)
  2. anticlockwise in both (a) and (b)
  3. clockwise in (a) and anticlockwise in (b)
  4. anticlockwise in (a) and clockwise in (b)
Concept to recallLenz’s law: the induced current opposes the change of flux. For a fixed perimeter a circle encloses the largest area.
  1. (a) Becoming a circle, the area grows, so the inward flux grows; the induced field must point out ⇒ anticlockwise.
  2. (b) Collapsing to a line, the area shrinks, so the outward flux falls; the induced field must point out to make it up ⇒ anticlockwise.

Answer: option (2) — anticlockwise in both (a) and (b)

Q531CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q42NTA final key
A conducting ring of radius r is placed in a varying magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the ring. If the rate at which the magnetic field varies is x, the electric field intensity at any point of the ring is ____________.
  1. rx
  2. rx/2
  3. 2rx
  4. 4r/x
Concept to recallFaraday: ∮ E·dl = −dΦ/dt; the induced field is tangential and uniform round the ring.
  1. E(2πr) = πr2x.
  2. E = rx/2.

Answer: option (2) — rx/2

Q532CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q43NTA final key
A 50 Hz ac current of crest value 1 A flows through the primary of a transformer. If the mutual inductance between the primary and secondary be 0.5 H, the crest voltage induced in the secondary is ____________.
  1. 75 V
  2. 150 V
  3. 100 V
  4. 200 V
Concept to recalle2 = −M dI1/dt; for I = I0 sinωt the peak of dI/dt is ωI0.
  1. NTA’s final key is 100 V. It takes the current rising from 0 to its crest 1 A in a quarter period, T/4 = 1/200 s = 5 ms, so the rate of change is 1/0.005 = 200 A/s.
  2. e = M ΔI/Δt = 0.5 × 200 = 100 V.
  3. Strictly that is the average emf over the quarter cycle. The true crest of e = M dI/dt is MωI0 = 0.5 × 2π(50) × 1 = 50π ≈ 157 V, which is not printed.

Answer: option (3) — 100 V

NoteNTA’s final key is option (3), 100 V (Book A Q43; the same answer in Books B, C and D). That is MΔI/Δt with the current rising 0 → 1 A in a quarter period, i.e. the average emf. The exact crest value is MωI0 = 50π ≈ 157 V, which no option prints; 150 V is not the key.
Q533CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q44NTA final key
A long solenoid of diameter 0.1 m has 2 × 104 turns per meter. At the centre of the solenoid a coil of 100 turns and radius 0.01 m is placed with its axis coinciding with the solenoid axis. The current in the solenoid reduces at a constant rate to 0 A from 4 A in 0.05 s. If the resistance of the coil is 10π2 Ω, then the total charge flowing through the coil during this time is ____________.
  1. 16 μC
  2. 32 μC
  3. 16π μC
  4. 32π μC
Concept to recallInduced charge Q = Δ(NΦ)/R — independent of how fast the change happens.
  1. B = μ0nI = 4π × 10−7 × 2 × 104 × 4 = 32π × 10−3 T.
  2. NΦ = 100 × 32π × 10−3 × π(0.01)2 = 32π2 × 10−5 Wb.
  3. Q = 32π2 × 10−5/(10π2) = 3.2 × 10−5 C = 32 μC.

Answer: option (2) — 32 μC

TrapUse the coil’s area (r = 0.01 m), not the solenoid’s.
Q534CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q650NTA final key
In a coil, an increase in current from 5 A to 10 A in 100 ms induces an induced emf of 100 V. The self inductance of the coil is :
  1. 2 H
  2. 10 H
  3. 20 H
  4. 2000 H
Concept to recall|e| = L dI/dt.
  1. dI/dt = 5/0.1 = 50 A/s.
  2. L = 100/50 = 2 H.

Answer: option (1) — 2 H

Q535CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q651NTA final key
A 200 turn circular coil of area 103 cm2 rotates at 60 revolutions per minute in a uniform magnetic field of 0.02 T perpendicular to the axis of rotation of the coil. The maximum voltage induced in the coil is :
  1. 25π V
  2. 14π V
  3. 45π V
  4. 125π V
Concept to recallAC generator: e0 = NBAω.
  1. A = 103 cm2 = 0.1 m2; ω = 2π(60/60) = 2π rad/s.
  2. e0 = 200 × 0.02 × 0.1 × 2π = 0.8π = (4/5)π V.

Answer: option (3) — 45π V

TrapForgetting to convert rpm to rad/s (using ω = 60) gives a far larger answer.
Q536CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q666NTA final key
Two identical coaxial coils P and Q carrying equal current in the same direction are brought nearer. The current in :
  1. P increases while in Q decreases
  2. Q increases while in P decreases
  3. Both P and Q increases
  4. Both P and Q decreases
Concept to recallLenz’s law: induced currents oppose the change in flux.
  1. Coming closer, each coil receives more flux from the other, in the same sense as its own.
  2. The induced current opposes this, i.e. flows opposite to the existing current: both currents decrease.

Answer: option (4) — Both P and Q decreases

Q537CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q1 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The magnetic flux (Φ) is:
  1. Scalar quantity and its SI unit is Wb/m2.
  2. Vector quantity and its SI unit is Tm2.
  3. Scalar quantity and its SI unit is Tm2.
  4. Vector quantity and its SI unit is Wb/m2.
Concept to recallΦ = B·A = BA cosθ — a dot product, so a scalar. Unit: weber, 1 Wb = 1 T m2.
  1. A dot product of two vectors is a scalar, so flux is scalar.
  2. Unit = T × m2 = T m2 (= Wb). Wb/m2 is the tesla, the unit of B, not of Φ.

Answer: option (3) — Scalar quantity and its SI unit is Tm2.

TrapWb/m2 is the unit of flux density B, not of flux.
NoteThe paper prints “SL unit” in option (3); read as SI.
Q538CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q8 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. The relative motion between a magnet and a coil is responsible for induction of electric current in the coil.
B. Magnetic flux is a vector quantity.
C. In a closed coil, the magnitude of emf induced is equal to the time rate of change of magnetic flux.
D. Eddy currents oppose the magnetic braking effect in trains.
E. Lenz's law gives the polarity of the induced emf clearly.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. B, C and D only
  2. A, B, D and E only
  3. A, B and D only
  4. A, C and E only
Concept to recallFaraday: |ε| = |dΦ/dt|; Lenz: the induced current opposes the change (gives the sign). Eddy currents produce magnetic braking.
  1. A true (Faraday's experiments). C true (Faraday's law). E true (Lenz).
  2. B false: flux is scalar. D false: eddy currents are the braking mechanism, they do not oppose it.

Answer: option (4) — A, C and E only

Q539CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q35 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A metal plate is getting heated. It can be because of-
A. An alternating current is passing through the plate.
B. It is placed in a time varying magnetic field.
C. A direct current is passing through the plate.
D. It is placed in a space varying magnetic field, but does not vary with time.
E. It is placed in a time constant magnetic field.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C Only
  2. C, D, E Only
  3. A, D, E Only
  4. B, C, D Only
Concept to recallJoule heating needs a current: either driven (ac or dc) or induced (eddy currents need a changing flux).
  1. A and C: I2R heating. B: changing flux induces eddy currents, which heat the plate.
  2. D and E: a static field through a stationary plate induces nothing.

Answer: option (1) — A, B, C Only

Q540CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q37 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The magnetic flux passing perpendicular to the plane of coil is changing according to the equation Φ = 6t2 + 7t + 1, where 'Φ' is in m Wb and 't' in sec. The magnitude of induced emf at t = 2 s is
  1. 31 mV
  2. 38 mV
  3. 39 mV
  4. 32 mV
Concept to recall|ε| = dΦ/dt.
  1. dΦ/dt = 12t + 7 = 31 mWb/s at t = 2 s, so |ε| = 31 mV.

Answer: option (1) — 31 mV

Q541CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q43 · Prepp reconstructionworked here
A metal conductor of length 1m rotates in vertical plane about an axis passing through one of its ends at angular velocity 4 rad s−1. What is the emf developed between the two ends of the conductor, if the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field is 0.2 G?
  1. 4mV
  2. 40mV
  3. 4μV
  4. 40μV
Concept to recallRod rotating about one end perpendicular to B: ε = ½Bωl2. 1 G = 10−4 T.
  1. B = 0.2 G = 2 × 10−5 T, and it is perpendicular to the plane of rotation.
  2. ε = ½ × 2 × 10−5 × 4 × 12 = 4 × 10−5 V = 40 μV.

Answer: option (4) — 40μV

TrapForgetting the gauss-to-tesla factor (10−4) inflates the answer by 104.
NotePrepp's unofficial key gives option (1); the working above shows why that cannot be right. 4 mV would need B = 20 G, a hundred times the given field.
Q542CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q31 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In an AC generator when the plane of the armature is perpendicular to the magnetic field, what will be the magnitude of the magnetic flux passing through the coil and the emf induced in the coil be?
  1. Both the magnetic flux and the induced emf are maximum
  2. Both the magnetic flux and the induced emf are zero
  3. The magnetic flux is zero and the induced emf is maximum
  4. The magnetic flux is maximum and the induced emf is zero
Concept to recallΦ = NBA cosωt, ε = NBAω sinωt: when one is maximum the other is zero.
  1. Plane ⊥ B means the coil's normal is along B: Φ maximum, and its rate of change is zero, so ε = 0.

Answer: option (4) — The magnetic flux is maximum and the induced emf is zero

Q543CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q48 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Two coils of self-inductances L1 and L2 are kept close to each other so that the effective flux in one is completely linked with the other. What is the mutual inductance M between them?
  1. L1L2
  2. L1L2−1
  3. (L1L2)2
  4. (L1L2)1/2
Concept to recallM = k√(L1L2), with k = 1 for perfect flux linkage.
  1. Complete linkage: k = 1, M = √(L1L2).

Q544CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q50 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A boat is moving due east in a region where the Earth's magnetic field is 5.0 × 10−5 NA−1m−1 due north and horizontal. The boat carries a vertical aerial 2 m long. If the speed of the boats is 1.5 ms−1, the magnitude of the induced emf is:
  1. 0.50 mV
  2. 0.15 mV
  3. 1.00 mV
  4. 0.75 mV
Concept to recallMotional emf ε = Bvl when B, v and l are mutually perpendicular.
  1. B (north), v (east) and the aerial (vertical) are mutually perpendicular.
  2. ε = 5 × 10−5 × 1.5 × 2 = 1.5 × 10−4 V = 0.15 mV.

Answer: option (2) — 0.15 mV

Q545CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q23NTA final key
A metal plate is getting heated. It can be because of-
A. An alternating current is passing through the plate.
B. It is placed in a time varying magnitude field.
C. A direct current is passing through the plate.
D. It is placed in a space varying magnitude field, but does not vary with time.
E. It is placed in a time constant magnetic filed.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C Only
  2. C, D, E Only
  3. A, D, E Only
  4. B, C, D Only
Concept to recallJoule heating needs a current: either passed through the plate (AC or DC) or induced in it by a changing flux (eddy currents).
  1. A and C: Joule heating by the current passed through it.
  2. B: a time-varying field induces eddy currents, which heat it.
  3. D and E: a steady field through a stationary plate induces nothing.

Answer: option (1) — A, B, C Only

Q546CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q35NTA final key
A metal conductor of length 1m rotates in vertical plane about an axis passing through one of its ends at angular velocity 4 rad s−1. What is the emf developed between the two ends of the conductor, if the horizontal component of the earth’s magnetic field is 0.2 G?
  1. 4mV
  2. 40mV
  3. 4μV
  4. 40μV
Concept to recallRotating rod: ε = ½Bωl2; 1 G = 10−4 T.
  1. Rotating in a vertical plane, it cuts the horizontal component BH = 0.2 × 10−4 T.
  2. ε = ½ × 0.2 × 10−4 × 4 × 12 = 4 × 10−5 V = 40 μV.

Q547CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q4NTA final key
The magnetic flux passing perpendicular to the plane of coil is changing according to the equation Φ = 6t2 + 7t + 1, where ‘Φ’ is in mWb and ‘t’ in sec.
The magnitude of induced emf at t = 2 s is
  1. 31mV
  2. 38mV
  3. 39mV
  4. 32mV
Concept to recallFaraday: |ε| = dΦ/dt.
  1. dΦ/dt = 12t + 7 mWb s−1.
  2. At t = 2 s: 31 mV.

Q548CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q26 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A short solenoid of radius a and n1 number of turns per unit length and length L is kept coaxially inside a very long solenoid of radius b and n2 number of turns per unit length. What is the mutual inductance of the system?
  1. μ0πb2n1n2L
  2. μ0πa2n1n2L2
  3. μ0πa2n1n2L
  4. μ0πb2n1n2L2
Concept to recallM = (flux linkage of one coil)/(current in the other); the field of the long outer solenoid is μ0n2I.
  1. Current I in the outer solenoid: B = μ0n2I inside it.
  2. Flux through the inner coil, area πa2, turns n1L: Φ = n1L·μ0n2I·πa2.
  3. M = μ0πa2n1n2L.

Answer: option (3) — μ0πa2n1n2L

TrapUse the smaller area πa2: the field is only linked where both coils overlap.
Q549CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q31 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
(A) Rod rotated with angular velocity ω in a uniform magnetic field(I) e = e0 sin ωt
(B) Coil is rotated with angular velocity in a uniform magnetic field(II) e = Bvl
(C) Rod is moved with linear velocity v in uniform magnetic field(III) Constant
(D) When a rectangular coil is moved in a magnetic field induced emf is(IV) e = Bωl2/2

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
  2. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  3. (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
  4. (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Concept to recallMotional emf: rod sliding e = Bvl; rod rotating about one end e = ½Bωl2; coil rotating e = NBAω sin ωt.
  1. (A) rotating rod → ½Bωl2 (IV).
  2. (B) rotating coil → sinusoidal (I).
  3. (C) sliding rod → Bvl (II).
  4. (D) a coil moved steadily through a field: the emf is constant (zero in a uniform field) (III).

Q550CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q45 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The induced e.m.f. in a coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field will increase if
A. Total number of turns in the coil decreases
B. Magnetic field increases
C. Speed of rotation of coil decreases
D. Area of the coil increases
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, C and D only
  2. B and D only
  3. A, B and C Only
  4. A, B, C and D only
Concept to recallPeak emf of a rotating coil e0 = NBAω.
  1. e0 rises with N, B, A and ω.
  2. Fewer turns (A) or slower rotation (C) lower it. B and D raise it.

Answer: option (2) — B and D only

Q551CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q17worked here
A square coil of side 10 cm, 500 turns and resistance 3 Ω is placed with its plane perpendicular to the horizontal component of the Earth’s magnetic field. It is rotated about vertical axis passing through centre by 180° in 0.25 second. Estimate the magnitude of the emf and current induced in the coil. Horizontal component of the Earth’s magnetic field at the place is 3.0 × 10−5 T.
  1. 9 × 10−6 V, 3 × 10−6 A
  2. 21 × 10−6 V, 7 × 10−6 A
  3. 12 × 10−6 V, 4 × 10−6 A
  4. 12 × 10−4 V, 4 × 10−4 A
Concept to recallAverage emf = N|ΔΦ|/Δt. Turning a coil through 180° reverses the flux: |ΔΦ| = 2BA.
  1. ΔΦ per turn = 2 × 3 × 10−5 × 0.01 = 6 × 10−7 Wb.
  2. ε = 500 × 6 × 10−7/0.25 = 1.2 × 10−3 V = 12 × 10−4 V.
  3. I = ε/R = 1.2 × 10−3/3 = 4 × 10−4 A.

Answer: option (4) — 12 × 10−4 V, 4 × 10−4 A

TrapArea 10 cm × 10 cm = 10−2 m2; using 10−4 gives the 10−6 options.
Q552CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q28worked here
A cylindrical bar magnet is kept along the axis of a circular coil. If the magnet is rotated about its axis, then:
  1. a current will be induced in the coil
  2. no current will be induced in the coil
  3. an emf will be induced in the coil
  4. no magnetic flux would be linked with coil
Concept to recallAn emf is induced only when the flux through the coil changes.
  1. The field of a cylindrical magnet is symmetric about its axis, so spinning it about that axis leaves the flux through the coil unchanged.
  2. No change of flux ⇒ no emf, no current (though flux is linked).

Answer: option (2) — no current will be induced in the coil

Q553CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q43worked here
Self inductance of coil causes:
  1. decays of current through it only
  2. the growth of current through it only
  3. both the growth and decay of current through it
  4. neither the growth nor the decay of current through it
Concept to recallSelf-induced emf ε = −L dI/dt opposes any change of current (electrical inertia).
  1. Self-inductance opposes (delays) both the growth and the decay of current; the options use “causes” loosely for “affects”.

Answer: option (3) — both the growth and decay of current through it

Q554CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q9 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Let a rod AB of length l having resistance r is moving perpendicular to a magnetic field B with constant velocity v. If the ends of the rod is connected to a wire PQRS of negligible resistance, then current passing through the wire will be: (see fig.)
  1. Blv/2r
  2. Blv/r
  3. Blv/4
  4. 3Blv/4r
Concept to recallA moving rod is a cell of emf Blv and internal resistance r.
  1. emf = Blv.
  2. The rod’s ends are joined through two zero-resistance paths (A–Q–R–B and A–P–S–B): external resistance 0.
  3. I = Blv/r.

Answer: option (2) — Blv/r

TrapSplitting the current between the two loops (giving Blv/2r) answers a different question: the question asks for the current the rod drives.
Q555CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q39key re-derived
We can reduce eddy currents in the core of transformer by:
  1. increasing the number of turns in the secondary coil
  2. taking laminated core
  3. making step down transformer
  4. using a weak AC at high potential
Concept to recallEddy currents circulate in bulk metal; thin insulated laminations break up their paths and raise the resistance they meet.
  1. A laminated core (insulated sheets) cuts the eddy-current loops and the heating loss.

Answer: option (2) — taking laminated core

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: eddy currents.
Q556CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q19NTA final key
The statement that is NOT true about induced emf is :
  1. The induced emf lasts so long as the change in magnetic flux continues
  2. The direction of induced emf is given by Lenz’s law
  3. Whenever the amount of magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced in the circuit
  4. Larger the amount of magnetic flux linked with a circuit greater is the emf induced in it
Concept to recallFaraday: ε = −dΦ/dt depends on the rate of change of flux, not on the flux itself.
  1. A large but steady flux induces nothing; statement (4) is false.
  2. The other three are Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws.

Answer: option (4) — Larger the amount of magnetic flux linked with a circuit greater is the emf induced in it

Q557CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q20NTA final key
The magnitude of electric current is increasing from A towards B. If there is any induced current in the loop as shown in the figure, its direction will be :
  1. Clockwise
  2. Anticlockwise
  3. No induced current
  4. Can not be predicted
Concept to recallRight-hand rule for the wire’s field, then Lenz: the induced current opposes the change in flux.
  1. Current to the right: above the wire its field points out of the page.
  2. The current grows, so the outward flux through the loop grows.
  3. The induced current makes an inward field inside the loop: clockwise.

Answer: option (1) — Clockwise

Q558CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q21NTA final key
A coil having ‘n’ turns and resistance ‘R’ Ω is connected with a galvanometer of resistance ‘4R’ Ω. What is the induced current in the circuit when this combination (coil+galvanometer) is moved in time t from a magnetic flux φ1 to φ2 ?
  1. −n(φ2 − φ1)4Rt
  2. −n(φ2 − φ1)Rt
  3. −n(φ2 − φ1)5Rt
  4. −(φ2 − φ1)nRt
Concept to recallε = −n Δφ/Δt; current = ε/(total resistance).
  1. ε = −n(φ2 − φ1)/t.
  2. Total resistance R + 4R = 5R.
  3. I = −n(φ2 − φ1)/(5Rt).

Answer: option (3) — −n(φ2 − φ1)5Rt

Q559CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q22NTA final key
An emf of 0.5 V is developed in the secondary coil, when current in primary coil changes from 5.0 A to 2.0 A in 300 milliseconds. The mutual inductance of two coils would be :
  1. 0.02 H
  2. 0.03 H
  3. 0.01 H
  4. 0.05 H
Concept to recall|ε2| = M |dI1/dt|.
  1. dI/dt = 3.0/0.3 = 10 A/s.
  2. M = 0.5/10 = 0.05 H.

Answer: option (4) — 0.05 H

Q560CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q18NTA final key
The mutual inductance M12 of coil 1 with respect to coil 2:
  1. depends on the current passing through the coil
  2. increases when the coils are brought nearer
  3. M21 of coil 2 with respect to the coil 1 is not same
  4. increases when any one coil is rotated about its axis
Concept to recallM depends only on geometry (sizes, turns, separation, orientation) and the core; M12 = M21.
  1. Bringing the coils nearer links more flux of one through the other, so M increases.
  2. M is independent of current; M12 = M21; rotating a coil about its own axis changes nothing.

Answer: option (2) — increases when the coils are brought nearer

Q561CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q21NTA final key
What is the self inductance of a solenoid of length 50 cm, if area of cross section is 10 cm2 and total number of turns is 600?
  1. 1.44 × 10−4 H
  2. 7.20 × 10−4 H
  3. 2.88 × 10−4 H
  4. 9.04 × 10−4 H
Concept to recallL = μ0N2A/l.
  1. A = 10 cm2 = 10−3 m2, l = 0.5 m.
  2. L = 4π × 10−7 × 3.6 × 105 × 10−3/0.5 = 9.05 × 10−4 H.

Answer: option (4) — 9.04 × 10−4 H

Trap10 cm2 is 10−3 m2, not 10−4 or 10−2.
Q562CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q18NTA final key
Which one out of the following is not an application of eddy currents?
  1. Transformers
  2. Speedometers
  3. Magnetic Brakes
  4. Induction furnace
Concept to recallEddy currents are used in brakes, speedometers, induction furnaces and damping; in transformers they are a loss to be reduced (laminated core).
  1. A transformer does not use eddy currents; its core is laminated to suppress them.

Answer: option (1) — Transformers

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: eddy currents.
Q563CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q20NTA final key
A square loop of copper wire is pulled through a region of uniform magnetic field as shown. Rank the pulling forces FA, FB, FC and FD that must be applied to keep the loop moving with constant speed (v):
  1. FB = FD, FA = FC
  2. FC > FB = FD > FA
  3. FC > FD > FB > FA
  4. FD > FB > FA = FC
Concept to recallA force is needed only while the flux changes: F = B2l2v/R when one edge is in the field.
  1. A (outside) and C (wholly inside): flux constant, no current, F = 0.
  2. B (entering) and D (leaving): one side cuts the field, same emf Blv, same current, same force.
  3. So FB = FD and FA = FC (= 0).

Answer: option (1) — FB = FD, FA = FC

Q564CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q46NTA final key
A metal rod PQ rests on the rails AB, between the poles of a permanent magnet; rails, rod and field are mutually perpendicular. A galvanometer G connects the rails through a switch K. Length of the rod = 15 cm, B = 0.50 T, resistance of the closed loop containing the rod = 180.0 mΩ. Assume the field to be uniform.

Suppose K is open and the rod is moved with a speed of 12 cms−1 in the direction. The magnitude of the induced emf will be :
  1. 4.5 × 10−3 V
  2. 9.0 × 10−3 V
  3. 18.0 × 10−3 V
  4. 27.0 × 10−3 V
Concept to recallMotional emf ε = Blv (exists even with the circuit open).
  1. ε = 0.50 × 0.15 × 0.12 = 9.0 × 10−3 V.

Answer: option (2) — 9.0 × 10−3 V

Q565CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q47NTA final key
A metal rod PQ rests on the rails AB, between the poles of a permanent magnet; rails, rod and field are mutually perpendicular. A galvanometer G connects the rails through a switch K. Length of the rod = 15 cm, B = 0.50 T, resistance of the closed loop containing the rod = 180.0 mΩ. Assume the field to be uniform.

The magnetic force experienced by the rod when K is closed will be :
  1. 7.5 × 10−2 N
  2. 3.25 × 10−2 N
  3. 6.45 × 10−2 N
  4. 3.75 × 10−2 N
Concept to recallClosed loop: I = ε/R, and the rod feels F = BIl opposing its motion (Lenz).
  1. I = ε/R = 9.0 × 10−3/0.180 = 0.05 A.
  2. F = BIl = 0.50 × 0.05 × 0.15 = 3.75 × 10−3 N.

Answer: option (4) — 3.75 × 10−2 N

NoteThe correct force is 3.75 × 10−3 N. All four options are printed with 10−2; NTA keyed option (4), whose digits match, so read it as a misprinted exponent.
Q566CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q48NTA final key
A metal rod PQ rests on the rails AB, between the poles of a permanent magnet; rails, rod and field are mutually perpendicular. A galvanometer G connects the rails through a switch K. Length of the rod = 15 cm, B = 0.50 T, resistance of the closed loop containing the rod = 180.0 mΩ. Assume the field to be uniform.

The power required (by an external agent) to keep the rod moving at the same speed (= 12 cms−1) when K is closed will :
  1. Zero
  2. 9 × 10−3 W
  3. 4.5 × 10−3 W
  4. 6.4 × 10−3 W
Concept to recallAt constant speed the agent’s force equals the magnetic drag F = BIl, so P = Fv (= εI).
  1. P = Fv = 3.75 × 10−3 × 0.12 = 4.5 × 10−4 W.
  2. Check: εI = 9 × 10−3 × 0.05 = 4.5 × 10−4 W.

Answer: option (3) — 4.5 × 10−3 W

NoteThe correct power is 4.5 × 10−4 W; the option is printed with 10−3 (the same exponent slip as Q47). NTA keyed option (3), whose digits match.
Q567CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q49NTA final key
A metal rod PQ rests on the rails AB, between the poles of a permanent magnet; rails, rod and field are mutually perpendicular. A galvanometer G connects the rails through a switch K. Length of the rod = 15 cm, B = 0.50 T, resistance of the closed loop containing the rod = 180.0 mΩ. Assume the field to be uniform.

The power dissipated as heat in the closed circuit is :
  1. 1.5 × 10−3 W
  2. 3 × 10−3 W
  3. 9.0 × 10−3 W
  4. 4.5 × 10−3 W
Concept to recallEnergy conservation: the mechanical power fed in appears as Joule heat, I2R = ε2/R.
  1. P = I2R = (0.05)2 × 0.180 = 4.5 × 10−4 W.
  2. It equals the external power of Q48, as it must.

Answer: option (4) — 4.5 × 10−3 W

NoteCorrect value 4.5 × 10−4 W; printed with 10−3. NTA keyed option (4).
Q568CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q50NTA final key
A metal rod PQ rests on the rails AB, between the poles of a permanent magnet; rails, rod and field are mutually perpendicular. A galvanometer G connects the rails through a switch K. Length of the rod = 15 cm, B = 0.50 T, resistance of the closed loop containing the rod = 180.0 mΩ. Assume the field to be uniform.

The induced emf produced in the moving rod if the magnetic field becomes parallel to the rails instead of being perpendicular will be :
  1. 3 × 10−3 V
  2. 6 × 10−3 V
  3. 9 × 10−3 V
  4. Zero
Concept to recallε = (v × B)·l; zero when v is parallel to B.
  1. The rod moves along the rails; if B is also along the rails, v ∥ B and v × B = 0.
  2. No force on the free electrons, so no emf.

Answer: option (4) — Zero

Alternating Current69 questions

Q569CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q22 (NTA Q.No. 412)NTA final key
Identify the correct statement(s) among the following.
A. In a d.c. circuit, a capacitor can conduct but not an inductor.
B. In a d.c. circuit, an inductor can conduct but not a capacitor.
C. In a d.c. circuit, both the inductor and capacitor cannot conduct.
D. An inductor has infinite resistance in a d.c. circuit.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A and C only
  2. B and D only
  3. B only
  4. A, C and D only
Concept to recallFor d.c. (ω = 0): XL = ωL = 0, XC = 1/ωC = ∞.
  1. An inductor passes steady d.c. (zero reactance); a capacitor blocks it once charged.
  2. Only B is true.

Answer: option (3) — B only

Q570CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q23 (NTA Q.No. 413)NTA final key
An a.c. voltage is applied to a pure inductor . The current in the inductor would be
  1. leading the voltage by π2
  2. lagging the voltage by π2
  3. leading the voltage by π4
  4. in phase with the voltage.
Concept to recallPure L: v = L di/dt, so i = im sin(ωt − π/2).
  1. Current lags voltage by π/2 in a pure inductor (it leads in a pure capacitor).

Answer: option (2) — lagging the voltage by π2

Q571CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q24 (NTA Q.No. 414)NTA final key
A pure inductor of 0.25 H is connected to a source of 220 V. If the frequency of the source is 50 Hz, then the rms current in the circuit will be.
  1. 1.6 A
  2. 4.0 A
  3. 2.8 A
  4. 28 A
Concept to recallXL = 2πfL; Irms = Vrms/XL.
  1. XL = 2π × 50 × 0.25 = 78.5 Ω.
  2. I = 220/78.5 = 2.8 A.

Answer: option (3) — 2.8 A

Q572CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A. The current lags behind the emf by π/4 in phaseI. A.C. circuit containing only an inductor
B. The e.m.f. lags behind the current by π/4 in phaseII. A.C. circuit with resistance and inductance in series
C. The current lags behind the e.m.f. in phase by π/2III. A.C. circuit containing only a capacitor
D. The e.m.f. lags behind the current in phase by π/2IV. A.C. circuit with resistance and capacitor in series
  1. A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
  2. A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
  3. A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
  4. A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
Concept to recallPure L: current lags by π/2. Pure C: current leads by π/2. RL: lags by less than π/2. RC: leads by less than π/2.
  1. C (lag π/2) → pure inductor I; D (emf lags, i.e. current leads, by π/2) → pure capacitor III.
  2. A (lag π/4) → RL series II; B (lead π/4) → RC series IV.

Answer: option (2) — A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

Q573CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived
The efficiency of an ideal transformer is:
  1. 25%
  2. 50%
  3. 75%
  4. 100%
Concept to recallIdeal transformer: no copper, iron or flux losses, so VpIp = VsIs.
  1. Output power = input power: efficiency 100%.

Answer: option (4) — 100%

Q574CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
In a series LCR circuit, resonance occurs when:
  1. XL > XC
  2. XC > XL
  3. XL = XC
  4. R = 0
Concept to recallZ = √(R2 + (XL − XC)2) is least, and current greatest, when XL = XC.
  1. ωL = 1/(ωC) ⇒ ω0 = 1/√(LC); then Z = R.

Answer: option (3) — XL = XC

Q575CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
In an AC circuit, the average value of alternating current over one complete cycle is:
  1. Maximum
  2. Minimum
  3. Infinite
  4. Zero
Concept to recallThe mean of sin ωt over a full period is zero (equal positive and negative half-cycles).
  1. <I0 sin ωt> over one cycle = 0; over a half-cycle it is 2I0/π.

Answer: option (4) — Zero

Q576CUET 2026 · 30 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
In an AC circuit containing a pure resistor, the phase difference between voltage and current is
  1. 90°
  2. 180°
  3. 45°
  4. 0°
Concept to recallFor a resistor i = v/R at every instant.
  1. Voltage and current rise and fall together: in phase, φ = 0°.

Answer: option (4) — 0°

Q577CUET 2026 · 31 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q2key re-derived
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): In a pure inductive AC circuit, current lags voltage by 90°.
Reason (R): An inductor opposes the change in current flowing through it.
  1. Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
  2. Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
  3. A is true but R is false
  4. A is false but R is true
Concept to recallv = L di/dt: the voltage is largest when the current is changing fastest, i.e. a quarter cycle before the current peaks.
  1. A true (i = I0 sin(ωt − π/2)). R true, and the self-induced back emf opposing di/dt is exactly what delays the current.

Answer: option (1) — Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Q578CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q26NTA final key
An inductor of 500 mH is in series with a resistance and a variable capacitor connected to a source of frequency 0.4 kHz. The value of capacitance of the capacitor to get a maximum current will be
  1. 2.3 μF
  2. 0.32 μF
  3. 63 μF
  4. 0.62 μF
Concept to recallMaximum current in series LCR = resonance: XL = XC, so C = 1/(ω2L), ω = 2πf.
  1. ω = 2π × 400 = 2513 rad s−1.
  2. C = 1/(25132 × 0.5) = 3.2 × 10−7 F = 0.32 μF.

Answer: option (2) — 0.32 μF

TrapUsing f instead of ω = 2πf inflates C by (2π)2 ≈ 39.
Q579CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q28NTA final key
For an ac source rated at 220 V, 50 Hz, which of the following statements is correct?
  1. The peak value over a period of (1/50) s is 220 V.
  2. The average value over a period of (1/50) s is 220 V.
  3. The average value over a period of (1/50) s is 0 V.
  4. The average value over a period of (1/50) s is 220√2 V.
Concept to recallRatings are rms values; V0 = √2 Vrms. A sinusoid averages to zero over a full period.
  1. 1/50 s is exactly one period (f = 50 Hz).
  2. Over a full cycle the positive and negative halves cancel: average = 0 V.
  3. The peak is 220√2 ≈ 311 V, not 220 V.

Answer: option (3) — The average value over a period of (1/50) s is 0 V.

Trap220 V is the rms value, neither the peak nor the full-cycle average.
Q580CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q23 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The main causes of energy loss in transformers are
  1. (A) Hysteresis loss
  2. (B) Flux leakage
  3. (C) Eddy current
  4. (D) Damping
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallTransformer losses (NCERT): flux leakage, copper (I2R) loss in windings, eddy currents in the core, and hysteresis of the core.
  1. Hysteresis, flux leakage and eddy currents are all core/flux losses.
  2. A transformer has no moving parts, so “damping” is not a loss mechanism.

Answer: option (2) — (A), (B) and (C) only

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: eddy currents.
Q581CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q6 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In a series LCR circuit, C = 80 μF, L = 5.0 H and R = 40 Ω are connected to a variable frequency source of 240 V. The angular frequency of the source which drives the circuit at resonance will be:
  1. 5 rad s−1
  2. 25 rad s−1
  3. 0.05 rad s−1
  4. 50 rad s−1
Concept to recallResonance: ω0 = 1/√(LC), independent of R and of the source voltage.
  1. LC = 5.0 × 80 × 10−6 = 4 × 10−4 s2.
  2. ω0 = 1/(2 × 10−2) = 50 rad s−1.

Answer: option (4) — 50 rad s−1

Q582CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q13worked here
In an AC circuit, the instantaneous values of emf and current are E = 100 sin(314t) V and I = sin(314t + π/3) A. The average power consumed in the circuit is:
  1. 200 W
  2. 100 W
  3. 50 W
  4. 25 W
Concept to recallPav = VrmsIrms cosφ = ½V0I0 cosφ.
  1. φ = π/3, cosφ = ½.
  2. P = ½ × 100 × 1 × ½ = 25 W.

Answer: option (4) — 25 W

Trap50 W forgets the power factor; 100 W uses peak values with no ½.
Q583CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q26worked here
In a step-down transformer, 22 kV is converted into 220 V. The number of turns in the primary coil is 60000. The number of turns in the secondary coil will be
  1. 60000
  2. 6000
  3. 600
  4. 60
Concept to recallIdeal transformer: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np.
  1. Ns = 60000 × 220/22000 = 600.

Answer: option (3) — 600

Q584CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q16worked here
A domestic appliance draws 2.5 A from a 220 V, 50 Hz power supply. The amplitude of current is
  1. 3.5 A
  2. 2.5 A
  3. 1.8 A
  4. 0 A
Concept to recallMains ratings are rms: I0 = √2 Irms.
  1. I0 = 1.414 × 2.5 = 3.54 A ≈ 3.5 A.

Answer: option (1) — 3.5 A

Q585CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q19worked here
A 50 W, 100 V bulb is to be used on a 200 V, 50 Hz a.c. supply. Calculate the inductance of inductor used so that the bulb glows with normal brightness.
  1. 2√3π H
  2. √3π H
  3. 100√3π H
  4. 200√3π H
Concept to recallBulb resistance R = V2/P; series L: Z = √(R2 + XL2) with I fixed at the rated value.
  1. R = 1002/50 = 200 Ω; rated I = 50/100 = 0.5 A.
  2. Z = 200/0.5 = 400 Ω ⇒ XL = √(4002 − 2002) = 200√3 Ω.
  3. L = XL/(2π × 50) = 200√3/(100π) = 2√3/π H.

Answer: option (1) — 2√3π H

Q586CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q9worked here
A sinusoidal voltage with peak value 220 V and variable frequency is applied to a series LCR circuit in which R = 10 Ω, L = 4 mH, and C = 100 mF. Consider the following:
  1. (A) Resonant angular frequency (ω0) = 50 rad/s
  2. (B) Resonant frequency (ν0) = 25/π Hz
  3. (C) Resonant frequency (ν0) = 50/π Hz
  4. (D) The rms current at resonance is 15.5 A
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (C) only
  2. (A), (B) and (D) only
  3. (A), (C) and (D) only
  4. (B) and (D) only
Concept to recallω0 = 1/√(LC); at resonance Z = R.
  1. ω0 = 1/√(4 × 10−3 × 0.1) = 1/0.02 = 50 rad/s. (A) true.
  2. ν0 = 50/2π = 25/π Hz. (B) true, (C) false.
  3. Irms = (220/√2)/10 = 15.6 A ≈ 15.5 A. (D) true.

Answer: option (2) — (A), (B) and (D) only

Q587CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q29worked here
A 14.0 μF capacitor is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz source. The value of peak current in the circuit is (Given: π = 22/7 and √2 = 1.414)
  1. 1.57 A
  2. 1.47 A
  3. 1.37 A
  4. 1.27 A
Concept to recallXC = 1/(ωC); I0 = √2 Vrms/XC.
  1. ωC = 2 × 22/7 × 50 × 14 × 10−6 = 4.4 × 10−3 S.
  2. Irms = 220 × 4.4 × 10−3 = 0.968 A; I0 = 1.414 × 0.968 = 1.37 A.

Q588CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q36worked here
A coil with an inductance of 0.2 H has an inductive reactance of 62.8 Ω at a certain frequency. The frequency is
  1. 20 Hz
  2. 30 Hz
  3. 40 Hz
  4. 50 Hz

  1. ν = 62.8/(2 × 3.14 × 0.2) = 62.8/1.256 = 50 Hz.
