Q589CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q5worked here
A voltage V = 200 sin(400t) V AC source is connected to a series combination of an inductance 20 mH and resistance 6 Ω. The rms current in the AC circuit is:
  1. 33.3 A
  2. 20 A
  3. 14.14 A
  4. 10 A
Concept to recallZ = √(R2 + XL2), XL = ωL; Irms = I0/√2.
  1. XL = 400 × 0.02 = 8 Ω; Z = √(36 + 64) = 10 Ω.
  2. I0 = 200/10 = 20 A; Irms = 20/√2 = 14.14 A.

Q590CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q7worked here
A power transmission line feeds input power at 2400 V to a step-down transformer with its primary windings having 5000 turns. The output power is delivered at 240 V by the transformer. If the current in the primary coil of the transformer is 5 A and its efficiency is 95% then the current in the secondary will be
  1. 50 A
  2. 47.5 A
  3. 45 A
  4. 4.75 A
Concept to recallEfficiency η = VsIs/(VpIp).
  1. Output = 0.95 × 2400 × 5 = 11400 W.
  2. Is = 11400/240 = 47.5 A.

Q591CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q10 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following statements are true regarding alternating current:
(A) In an a.c. circuit containing resistance only, a.c. power is expressed in the same form as d.c. power (P = I2R), using a special value of current called root mean square (rms) or effective current, denoted by Irms.
(B) A phasor is a vector.
(C) Resonance phenomenon is exhibited by a circuit even if both L and C are not present in the circuit.
(D) For circuits used for transporting electric power, a low power factor implies less power loss in transmission.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A) and (B) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallAverage power in R is Irms2R; a phasor is a rotating vector; resonance needs both L and C; low power factor means large current for the same power.
  1. (A) true — that is the definition of rms current.
  2. (B) true — NCERT: “a phasor is a vector which rotates about the origin”.
  3. (C) false — resonance needs L and C together so that XL and XC can cancel.
  4. (D) false — P = VI cos φ: low cos φ needs a larger I, so I2R loss is larger.

Answer: option (2) — (A) and (B) only

Q592CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q39 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
An 80 Ω resistor is connected to a 240 V, 50 Hz AC supply. The net power consumed over a full cycle is:
  1. zero
  2. 240 W
  3. 339 W
  4. 720 W
Concept to recallAverage power in a resistor: P = Vrms2/R (the 240 V is the rms value).
  1. P = 2402/80 = 57600/80 = 720 W.

Answer: option (4) — 720 W

Trap“Zero over a full cycle” is true for an ideal L or C, not for a resistor.
Q593CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q6 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A resistor of resistance 30 Ω and a capacitor of capacitance (250 π−1) μF are connected in series to a 220 V, 50 Hz source. The current in the circuit is
  1. 7.3 A
  2. 5.5 A
  3. 4.4 A
  4. 4.0 A
Concept to recallXC = 1/(2πfC), Z = √(R2 + XC2), I = V/Z.
  1. XC = 1/(2π × 50 × 250 × 10−6/π) = 1/0.025 = 40 Ω.
  2. Z = √(302 + 402) = 50 Ω.
  3. I = 220/50 = 4.4 A.

Answer: option (3) — 4.4 A

TrapAdding R + XC = 70 Ω gives 3.1 A; 220/30 gives the 7.3 A distractor.
Q594CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q12NTA final key
In an ac circuit, the current leads the voltage by π/2. The circuit is ____________.
  1. purely resistive
  2. should have circuit elements with resistance equal to reactance.
  3. purely inductive
  4. purely capacitive
Concept to recallPhase of current relative to voltage: R in phase; L lags by π/2; C leads by π/2.
  1. A lead of exactly π/2 needs a pure capacitor (R = 0 ⇒ tanφ infinite).

Answer: option (4) — purely capacitive

TrapR = X gives a phase of π/4, not π/2.
Q595CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q15NTA final key
Match List-I has four graphs showing variation of opposition to flow of ac versus frequency with circuit characteristic in List-II.
List-IList-II
(A) graph A(I) Impedance
(B) graph B(II) Capacitive reactance
(C) graph C(III) Inductive reactance
(D) graph D(IV) Resistance
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)
  3. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)

Q613CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q12 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  5. E: voltage up ⇒ current down — true.

Q634CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q21NTA final key
Find the effective impendance in the circuit if the source is a) DC source and b) High frequency AC source
  1. For DC, Z = R2 + R3 and for AC, Z = R1 + R3
  2. For DC, Z = R1 and for AC, Z = R2 + R3
  3. For DC, Z = ∞ and for AC, Z = 0
  4. For DC, Z = 0 and for AC, Z = ∞
Concept to recallDC (ω = 0): XL = 0 (inductor = wire), XC = ∞ (capacitor = open). Very high ω: the reverse.
  1. DC: C2 and C1 open, so the middle branch and R3 are cut off; L1, L2 are wires. Only R1 joins the terminals: Z = R1.
  2. High-frequency AC: L1, L2 open, so the top branch carries nothing; C2 is a short. Path C2–R2–R3: Z = R2 + R3.

Answer: option (2) — For DC, Z = R1 and for AC, Z = R2 + R3

Q635CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q22NTA final key
In AC circuits, the relation that holds is Z = E0I0 where,
A. Z = √(R2 + XL2) in case of a.c. circuit containing R and L in series.
B. Z = √(R2 + XC2) in case of a.c. circuit containing R and C in series.
C. Z = XL − XC in case of a.c. circuit containing L and C in series.
D. Z = √(R2 + (XL − XC)2) in case of a.c. circuit containing R, L and C in series.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, C, D only
  2. A, B, C only
  3. A, B, D only
  4. A, B, C, D only
Concept to recallGeneral series impedance Z = √(R2 + (XL − XC)2); every other case is a special case of it.
  1. D is the general result. Put XC = 0 for A, XL = 0 for B.
  2. Put R = 0 for C: Z = XL − XC (its magnitude). All four hold.

Answer: option (4) — A, B, C, D only

NoteNTA’s final key is option (4), A, B, C and D. Strictly the LC impedance is |XL − XC|, so C as printed holds only when XL > XC; the key reads it as a magnitude.
Q636CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q23NTA final key

  4. 100 Ω and 0.93 H

Q637CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q37NTA final key
A circuit element ‘X’ when connected to peak voltage of 200 V, a peak current of 5A flows which lags behind the voltage by π2. The rms value of current through the circuit will be :
  1. 5 A
  2. 5√2 A
  3. 2.5 A
  4. 5√2 A
Concept to recallCurrent lagging by π/2 ⇒ pure inductor; in phase ⇒ resistor. Series: Z = √(R2 + X2); Irms = I0/√2.
  1. X: XL = 200/5 = 40 Ω. Y: R = 200/5 = 40 Ω.
  2. Series: Z = 40√2 Ω; I0 = 200/(40√2) = 5/√2 A.
  3. Irms = I0/√2 = 2.5 A.

Answer: option (3) — 2.5 A

Trap5/√2 A is the peak current; the question asks for rms.

Q644CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1worked here
An electromagnetic wave travels in free space along the x-direction. At a particular point in space and time, B = 2 × 10−7 ĵ T is associated with this wave. The value of corresponding electric field E at this point is __________ V/m.

  2. −60k̂
  3. 30k̂
  4. −600k̂
Concept to recall|E| = c|B|, and E × B points along the direction of propagation.
  1. |E| = (3 × 108)(2 × 10−7) = 60 V/m.
  2. Need E × ĵ along +î: since k̂ × ĵ = −î, E must be along −k̂.
  3. E = −60k̂ V/m.

Answer: option (2) — −60k̂

TrapGetting the magnitude (60) is the easy half; the sign comes from E × B.
NoteThe site prints +60k̂. With B along +ĵ and the wave along +x, +60k̂ would make E × B point along −x; the correct field is −60k̂ V/m.
Q645CUET 2026 · 22 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q9key re-derived
A magnetic field vector in an electromagnetic wave is represented by B = B0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) ĵ. Its associated electric field vector is ________.
  1. E = −νλB0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) k̂
  2. E = −νλB0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) î
  3. E = νλB0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) k̂
  4. E = νλB0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) î
Concept to recallE0 = cB0 = νλB0; E ⊥ B and E × B along the propagation (+x here, from t − x).

  2. Need E × ĵ along +î, which needs E along −k̂.
  3. E = −νλB0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) k̂.

Answer: option (1) — E = −νλB0 sin(2πνt − 2πx/λ) k̂

Concept to recallv = c/√(εrμr) ⇒ εr = (c/v)2/μr.

  2. Increasing: III (1) < IV (1.125) < I (2.25) < II (4), i.e. (C), (D), (A), (B).

Answer: option (3) — (C), (D), (A), (B)

  2. 3.2 × 10−8 ĵ T

Q718CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q48NTA final key
The electric field vector oscillates according to the equation E = 4 sin[1.8y + (5.4 × 106)t] k̂. The equation of magnetic field vector is:

  2. B = 4 sin[1.8y + (5.4 × 106)t] ĵ
  3. B = 1.33 × 10−8 sin[1.8y + (5.4 × 106)t] k̂
  4. B = 5 sin[1.8y + (5.4 × 106)t] ĵ
Concept to recallB0 = E0/c; E, B and the direction of travel are mutually perpendicular.
  1. B0 = 4/(3 × 108) = 1.33 × 10−8 T.
  2. The wave travels along the y-axis and E is along z, so B must be along x (î). Only option 1 fits.

Answer: option (1) — B = 1.33 × 10−8 sin[1.8y + (5.4 × 106)t] î

NoteNTA’s final key is option (1), B = 1.33 × 10−8 sin[1.8y + (5.4 × 106)t] î. Strictly, a wave of phase (ky + ωt) travels along −y, and E × B along −y requires B along −î; no option carries the minus sign, so option (1) is the only one with the right magnitude and axis.

Q724CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q19NTA final key

Q728CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q37 (NTA Q.No. 427)NTA final key
A concave mirror forms a real image of an object kept at a distance of 9 cm from it. If the object is taken away further from the mirror by 6 cm, the image size is reduced to (1/4)th of its previous size. The focal length of the mirror is:
  1. -5 cm
  2. -7 cm
  3. 15 cm
  4. 18 cm
Concept to recallMirror magnification in terms of u and f: m = f/(f − u).

  2. m2 = m1/4 ⇒ 4(f + 9) = f + 15 ⇒ f = −7 cm.
  3. Check: u = −9 lies beyond F, so the image is real as stated.

Answer: option (2) — -7 cm

Q729CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
What is the relative decrease in focal length of a lens for an increase in optical power by 0.1 D from 2.5 D?
  1. 0.04
  2. 0.40
  3. 0.1
  4. 0.01
Concept to recallf = 1/P, so the fractional change in f is (f1 − f2)/f1 = ΔP/P2 (≈ ΔP/P for small changes).
  1. f1 = 1/2.5 = 0.400 m; f2 = 1/2.6 = 0.3846 m.
  2. Relative decrease = (0.400 − 0.3846)/0.400 = 0.0385 ≈ 0.04 (also ΔP/P = 0.1/2.5 = 0.04).

Answer: option (1) — 0.04

Q730CUET 2026 · 15 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10worked here
Two identical symmetric double convex lenses of focal length f are cut into two equal parts L1, L2 by AB plane and L3, L4 by XY plane as shown in figure respectively. The ratio of focal lengths of lenses L1 and L3 is
  1. 1 : 4
  2. 1 : 1
  3. 2 : 1
  4. 1 : 2
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2). Cutting along the axis keeps both curved faces; cutting across the thickness leaves one curved face and one plane face.
  1. L1 (cut along AB): both surfaces of radius R remain, so f1 = f.
  2. L3 (cut along XY): plano-convex, 1/f3 = (n − 1)/R = 1/(2f), so f3 = 2f.
  3. f1 : f3 = 1 : 2.

Answer: option (4) — 1 : 2

TrapCutting along the axis halves the light gathered, not the power: f is unchanged.
NoteThe site prints 1 : 1. That holds for L1 : L2 (or L3 : L4), not for L1 : L3; the standard answer to this question is 1 : 2.

Concept to recallMirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with the Cartesian signs: u = −30 cm, f = −20 cm.
  1. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60 ⇒ v = −60 cm (real, in front of the mirror).

Answer: option (1) — −60 cm

Trap+60 cm comes from forgetting that f of a concave mirror is negative.
Q734CUET 2026 · 31 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7 also 2026 1 June S1 Q5 (memory-based, collegedunia) (date uncertain) (last option 10 cm)key re-derived
A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. The image distance is
  1. 60 cm
  2. 30 cm
  3. 20 cm
  4. 15 cm
Concept to recallLens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, with u = −30 cm and f = +20 cm.
  1. 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60 ⇒ v = +60 cm (real, on the far side).

Answer: option (1) — 60 cm

Q735CUET 2026 · file dated 6 June, headed 1 June, Shift 1 (date uncertain) · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q5key re-derived
An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The image is formed at
  1. 15 cm
  2. 20 cm
  3. 30 cm
  4. Infinity
Concept to recallObject at 2F of a convex lens: image at 2F.
  1. 1/v = 1/15 − 1/30 = 1/30 ⇒ v = 30 cm on the other side.

Answer: option (3) — 30 cm

Q736CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q33NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct?
  1. (A) All mirrors follow the laws of reflection.
  2. (B) The angle between the ray of incidence and the plane surface of the mirror is equal to the angle between the plane surface of mirror and the ray of reflection for plane mirror
  3. (C) the rays coming parallel to the principal axis will go after reflection through the focus of the curved mirror
  4. (D) the rays coming to the pole of a curved mirror making an angle with axis will be reflected making the equal angle with the axis on the other side of the axis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  2. (A), (C) and (D) only
  3. (A), (B) and (C) only
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallLaws of reflection hold at every point of every mirror; at the pole of a spherical mirror the principal axis is the normal.
  1. (A) true: the laws apply point by point to any mirror.
  2. (B) true: if i = r with the normal, the complements (angles with the surface) are also equal.
  3. (C) true: paraxial rays parallel to the axis pass through (or appear to come from) F.
  4. (D) true: at the pole the axis is the normal, so the reflected ray makes the same angle on the other side.

Answer: option (1) — (A), (B), (C) and (D)

Q737CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q34NTA final key
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
  1. (A) The power of a lens is the ability of the lens to converge or diverge the incident rays.
  2. (B) S.I unit of the power of a lens is dioptre while focal length is in centimetres
  3. (C) For a lens of larger focal length, power is smaller
  4. (D) In any combination of lenses, the power of combination is not algebraic addition of power of combined lenses
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (C) only
  2. (B), (C) and (D) only
  3. (A) and (B) only
  4. (A) only
Concept to recallP = 1/f (f in metres) in dioptre; for thin lenses in contact P = P1 + P2 + …
  1. (A) true: that is the definition.
  2. (B) false: P in dioptre needs f in metres.
  3. (C) true: P = 1/f.
  4. (D) false: for lenses in contact the powers add algebraically.

Answer: option (1) — (A) and (C) only

Q738CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q35NTA final key
In an experiment with a convex lens, the length of an image is 1 cm, and the object length is 5 cm. If the object is placed at a distance of 40 cm from the lens, then the focal length of the lens is
  1. 6.67 cm
  2. 13.5 cm
  3. 5.6 cm
  4. 3.6 cm
Concept to recallLens: m = v/u and 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. A diminished image of a real object by a convex lens is real and inverted.
  1. Real image: m = −1/5 = v/u with u = −40 cm ⇒ v = +8 cm.
  2. 1/f = 1/8 − 1/(−40) = 6/40 ⇒ f = 6.67 cm.

Answer: option (1) — 6.67 cm

TrapTaking m = +1/5 (virtual image) gives v = −8 cm and f = −10 cm, impossible for a convex lens.
Q739CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q37NTA final key
The critical angle of incidence ic for a ray incident from a denser to rarer medium, is that angle for which
  1. the angle of reflection is 90°
  2. the angle of refraction is 90°
  3. the angle of refraction is 0°
  4. the angle of reflection is 0°
Concept to recallAt i = ic the refracted ray grazes the surface: r = 90°, so sin ic = n2/n1.
  1. Snell: n1 sin ic = n2 sin 90°.
  2. For i > ic there is no refracted ray (total internal reflection).

Answer: option (2) — the angle of refraction is 90°

Q740CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q39NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct?
  1. (A) Total internal reflection occurs when a ray of light travels from a rarer transparent medium to a denser medium.
  2. (B) In total internal reflection, the incident ray of light remains in the same medium after reflection.
  3. (C) In total internal reflection, the angle of incidence inside the denser transparent medium is equal to the angle of reflection in the same medium.
  4. (D) In total internal reflection inside a denser medium there is no angle of refraction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (B) and (C) only
  2. (A) and (B) only
  3. (B), (C) and (D) only
  4. (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallTIR needs light going from denser to rarer with i > ic; all the light is reflected, obeying the law of reflection, and there is no refracted ray.
  1. (A) false: TIR needs denser → rarer.
  2. (B) true: the light stays in the denser medium.
  3. (C) true: it is still reflection, so i = r.
  4. (D) true: there is no refracted ray at all.

Answer: option (3) — (B), (C) and (D) only

Q741CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q40NTA final key
If focal length of a concave lens is 50 cm, then the power of the lens would be
  1. +5 D
  2. −5 D
  3. +2 D
  4. −2 D
Concept to recallP = 1/f with f in metres; a concave lens has negative f.
  1. f = −0.50 m ⇒ P = −1/0.5 = −2 D.

Answer: option (4) — −2 D

Trap−5 D comes from using f = 0.2 m or misreading cm; +2 D forgets the sign of a diverging lens.
Q742CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q15 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The radii of curvature of the two surfaces of a concave lens are 20 cm each. The refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5. The power of the lens would be-
  1. −5 D
  2. −1 D
  3. 2.5 D
  4. −0.5 D
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2); for a double-concave lens R1 < 0, R2 > 0.
  1. 1/f = 0.5(−1/20 − 1/20) = −1/20 cm−1 ⇒ f = −20 cm.
  2. P = 1/f(m) = −1/0.20 = −5 D.

Answer: option (1) — −5 D

Q743CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q26 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
An eye specialist prescribes spectacles having a combination of a converging lens of focal length 25 cm and a diverging lens of focal length of 20 cm. The power of the combination of two lenses (in dioptre) is
  1. + 1.0
  2. − 1.0
  3. + 1.1
  4. +2.0
Concept to recallThin lenses in contact: P = P1 + P2, P = 1/f(m), diverging lens negative.
  1. P1 = +1/0.25 = +4 D; P2 = −1/0.20 = −5 D.
  2. P = −1 D.

Answer: option (2) — − 1.0

Q744CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q36 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A printed page is kept pressed by a glass cube-shaped paper-weight of edge 3.0 cm. The refractive index of the glass is μ = 1.5. By what amount will the printed letters appear to be shifted when viewed from the top?
  1. 1.0 cm
  2. 0.5 cm
  3. 2.0 cm
  4. 2.5 cm
Concept to recallNormal viewing through a slab: apparent depth = t/μ; shift = t(1 − 1/μ), towards the viewer.
  1. Apparent depth = 3.0/1.5 = 2.0 cm.
  2. Shift = 3.0 − 2.0 = 1.0 cm (letters appear raised).

Answer: option (1) — 1.0 cm

Trap2.0 cm is the apparent depth, not the shift.
Q745CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q39 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
If the radii of curvature of the faces of a double convex lens are 10 cm and 15 cm, respectively and its refractive index is 1.5, the focal length of the lens in air is
  1. 6 cm
  2. 12 cm
  3. 30 cm
  4. 28 cm
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2), with R1 = +10, R2 = −15 for a double-convex lens.
  1. 1/f = 0.5(1/10 + 1/15) = 0.5 × 1/6 = 1/12.
  2. f = 12 cm.

Answer: option (2) — 12 cm

Trap6 cm forgets the factor (n − 1) = 0.5.
Q746CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q46 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Which of the following statements is correct for a compound microscope?
  1. Both the objective and the eye piece should have large aperture
  2. Both the objective and the eye piece should have large focal lengths.
  3. The eyepiece essentially functions like a simple microscope or a magnifier.
  4. The final image is erect with respect to the original object.
Concept to recallCompound microscope: short-focus, small-aperture objective forms a real, inverted, magnified image; the eyepiece magnifies it like a simple microscope. Final image inverted.
  1. Both focal lengths should be short (m = (L/fo)(D/fe)).
  2. The final image is inverted relative to the object.
  3. The eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier: correct.

Answer: option (3) — The eyepiece essentially functions like a simple microscope or a magnifier.

Q747CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q8 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In Snell’s law of refraction, the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first medium (n21) is:
  1. a characteristic of the medium 1 only
  2. a characteristic of the medium 2 only
  3. independent of the angle of incidence.
  4. not dependent on the wavelength of light
Concept to recalln21 = sin i/sin r = v1/v2: a constant for a given pair of media and a given wavelength.
  1. n21 depends on both media (ratio of speeds), so the first two are wrong.
  2. It depends on wavelength (dispersion), so the last is wrong.
  3. For the pair and colour it is the same for every angle of incidence.

Answer: option (3) — independent of the angle of incidence.

Q748CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q22worked here
The necessary conditions for total internal reflection are
  1. (A) Light must travel from denser to rarer medium.
  2. (B) The angle of incidence in the denser medium must be less than the critical angle for the two media.
  3. (C) Light must travel from rarer to denser medium.
  4. (D) The angle of incidence in the denser medium must be greater than the critical angle for the two media.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (B) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (A) and (D) only
  4. (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallTIR: denser → rarer, and i > C where sin C = nrarer/ndenser.
  1. Only from denser to rarer can the refracted angle reach 90° (A).
  2. Beyond that, i > C (D).

Answer: option (3) — (A) and (D) only

Q749CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q34worked here
For which pair among the following, the refractive index will have the minimum and maximum value, respectively?
  1. Vacuum, diamond
  2. Air, glass
  3. Water, diamond
  4. Crown glass, flint glass (dense)
Concept to recalln = c/v: vacuum has n = 1 exactly (the least); diamond, n ≈ 2.42, is among the highest common values.
  1. Smallest possible n is vacuum (1.00).
  2. Largest in the list is diamond (2.42), above flint glass (~1.65).

Answer: option (1) — Vacuum, diamond

Q750CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q37worked here
Arrange the following steps (A, B, C and D) in proper sequence to determine the index correction in the given arrangement.
  1. (A) The difference between the two gives the correction to be applied to the observed distance.
  2. (B) The positions of the uprights are read on the scale. Their difference gives the observed distance between tip of the pin and the pole of the mirror.
  3. (C) A thin straight index needle OP is placed so that its one end O touches the tip of the pin and the other end P touches the pole of the mirror.
  4. (D) Length of the needle OP is measured by placing it on the scale which is the actual distance between the points in question.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  2. (A), (B), (D), (C)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (B), (C), (D), (A)
Concept to recallIndex correction = actual distance (needle length) − observed distance (difference of upright readings).
  1. Read the uprights: observed distance y (B).
  2. Fit the index needle between pin tip and mirror pole (C), then lay it on the scale for the actual distance x (D).
  3. Correction = x − y (A). The only option ending with (A) after (D) is (B), (C), (D), (A).

Answer: option (4) — (B), (C), (D), (A)

NoteWorked answer. In the lab manual the needle is fitted first and the uprights read after, i.e. C, B, D, A, which is not offered; reading the upright positions before inserting the needle does not change them, so B, C, D, A is equivalent.
Q751CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q43worked here
A planoconvex lens has the radius of curvature of its curved surface 50 cm and the refractive index of its material is 1.5. Its focal length will be
  1. 1 m
  2. 0.5 m
  3. 2 m
  4. 0.25 m
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2); plane face R = ∞.
  1. 1/f = 0.5 × 1/50 ⇒ f = 100 cm = 1 m.

Answer: option (1) — 1 m

Trapf = R is true for a biconvex lens with n = 1.5, not a planoconvex one.
Q752CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q18worked here
The physical quantity which does not change when X-rays of wavelength 10−10 m, or visible light of wavelength 400 nm, or radio waves of 500 m wavelength pass through glass is
  1. frequency
  2. wavelength
  3. speed
  4. refractive index
Concept to recallOn entering a new medium the frequency is fixed by the source; v and λ change.
  1. Each wave keeps its own frequency in glass; speed and wavelength drop, and n depends on wavelength (dispersion).

Answer: option (1) — frequency

Q753CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q32worked here
A telescope has an objective lens of focal length 150 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of the telescope is
  1. 30
  2. 36
  3. 35
  4. 42
Concept to recallNormal adjustment: m = fo/fe.
  1. m = 150/5 = 30.

Answer: option (1) — 30

NoteNormal adjustment assumed. With the final image at 25 cm, m = 30(1 + 5/25) = 36, which is option 2; the question as set gives no near-point condition, and NCERT’s stated magnifying power of a telescope is fo/fe (normal adjustment), so 30 is the intended answer.
Q754CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q48worked here
The critical angle is maximum when light travels from
  1. glass to air
  2. air to water
  3. air to glass
  4. water to air
Concept to recallsin C = nrarer/ndenser; TIR only from denser to rarer.
  1. Air → water/glass: no critical angle at all.
  2. Water → air: sin C = 1/1.33 = 0.75 (C ≈ 49°); glass → air: 1/1.5 (C ≈ 42°).
  3. Largest for water to air.

Answer: option (4) — water to air

Q755CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q12worked here
The magnifying power of a telescope is 6 in normal adjustment. The distance between its two lenses is 35 cm. The focal lengths of objective and eye-piece are, respectively:
  1. 30 cm, 5 cm
  2. 25 cm, 5 cm
  3. 5 cm, 30 cm
  4. 20 cm, 15 cm
Concept to recallNormal adjustment: m = fo/fe, L = fo + fe.
  1. fo = 6fe and 7fe = 35 ⇒ fe = 5 cm, fo = 30 cm.

Answer: option (1) — 30 cm, 5 cm

Q756CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q19worked here
A diverging lens of glass (μ = 1.5) has both surfaces of the same radius of curvature (R). On immersion in a medium of refractive index (μ = 1.8), it will behave as:
  1. diverging lens with focal length f = 3R
  2. diverging lens with focal length f = 0.3R
  3. Converging lens with focal length f = 3R
  4. Converging lens with focal length f = 6R
Concept to recall1/f = (nlens/nmedium − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2).
  1. Biconcave: R1 = −R, R2 = +R, so (1/R1 − 1/R2) = −2/R.
  2. 1/f = (1.5/1.8 − 1)(−2/R) = (−1/6)(−2/R) = 1/(3R).
  3. f = +3R: converging.

Answer: option (3) — Converging lens with focal length f = 3R

TrapA lens in a denser medium reverses its nature.
Q757CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q20worked here
To find the focal length of a convex lens, a student obtains the real, inverted and magnified image on the screen as shown in the figure below. Now the whole set up is immersed in water without disturbing the object and position of the screen. What will be student’s observation on the screen?
  1. No change in the image will be observed
  2. Size of image decreases
  3. Image disappears from the screen
  4. Size of image increases
Concept to recallfwater/fair = (ng − 1)/(ng/nw − 1).
  1. fw = 0.5/(1.5/1.33 − 1) f ≈ 0.5/0.125 f = 4f.
  2. With u unchanged the image moves to a new place (here u < 4f, so no real image at all).
  3. No sharp image forms on the fixed screen: it disappears.

Answer: option (3) — Image disappears from the screen

Q758CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q47worked here
Which of the following is not based on total internal reflection?
  1. Real and Apparent depth of a pond
  2. Prisms designed to bend light by 90° or by 180°
  3. Light pipe to facilitate visual examination of internal organs
  4. Transmission of signals over long distances through optical fibres
Concept to recallApparent depth = real depth/n is plain refraction.
  1. Totally reflecting prisms, light pipes and optical fibres all use TIR.
  2. Apparent depth is ordinary refraction.

Answer: option (1) — Real and Apparent depth of a pond

Q759CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q28 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
An object is placed at 5 cm in front of a concave mirror with a radius of curvature of 20 cm. The distance of the image from mirror and its nature are
  1. 10 cm, virtual and erect
  2. 10 cm, real and inverted
  3. 15 cm, real and inverted
  4. 3.3 cm, virtual and erect
Concept to recallMirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, f = R/2, Cartesian signs (concave: f < 0).

  2. 1/v = −1/10 + 1/5 = +1/10 ⇒ v = +10 cm (behind the mirror).
  3. Positive v: virtual and erect (m = −v/u = +2).

TrapObject inside F of a concave mirror always gives a virtual, erect, magnified image.
Q760CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q33 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q761CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q37 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
At sunrise and sunset the sun appears reddish due to
  1. scattering of light
  2. polarisation of light
  3. Reflection of light
  4. colour of the sky
Concept to recallRayleigh scattering ∝ 1/λ4: blue is scattered out of a long path through air.

  2. The light that reaches us directly is rich in red.

Answer: option (1) — scattering of light

Q762CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q41 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The magnification (m) and focal length (f) of a plane mirror are:
  1. m = +1; f = zero
  2. m = +1; f = ∞
  3. m = −1; f = zero
  4. m = −1; f = ∞

  2. Flat surface: radius of curvature infinite ⇒ f = ∞.

Q763CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q47 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Match List-I with List-II (here symbols have their usual meanings)
List-I (Physical Quantity / Law)List-II (Formula)
A. Snell’s lawt/μ
B. Apparent Shiftc/v
C. Refractive Indexμ2/μ1
D. Apparent deptht(1 − 1/μ)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)
  2. (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV)
  3. (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)
  4. (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)
Concept to recallSnell: sin i/sin r = μ2/μ1; apparent depth = t/μ; shift = t − t/μ; μ = c/v.
  1. Reading List-II in order as I–IV: t/μ (I), c/v (II), μ2/μ1 (III), t(1 − 1/μ) (IV).
  2. Snell → III, shift → IV, refractive index → II, apparent depth → I.

Answer: option (3) — (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

NoteThe re-typeset copy prints List-II without the numerals I–IV; they are taken in printed order.
Q764CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q19NTA final key
In the figure given below, APB is a curved surface of radius of curvature 10 cm separating air and a transparent material (μ = 4/3). A point object O is placed in air on the principal axis of the surface 20 cm from P. The distance of the image of O from P will be ____________.
  1. 16 cm left of P in air
  2. 16 cm right of P in water
  3. 20 cm right of P in water
  4. 20 cm left of P in air
Concept to recallRefraction at one spherical surface: n2/v − n1/u = (n2 − n1)/R, distances from P, light travelling left to right taken +.
  1. The surface is concave towards the object, so the centre C is on the air side: R = −10 cm; u = −20 cm.
  2. (4/3)/v + 1/20 = (1/3)/(−10) = −1/30.
  3. (4/3)/v = −1/30 − 1/20 = −1/12 ⇒ v = −16 cm.
  4. Negative v: a virtual image 16 cm to the left of P, in air.

Answer: option (1) — 16 cm left of P in air

TrapTaking R = +10 cm gives (4/3)/v = 1/30 − 1/20 = −1/60, v = −80 cm; the sign of R is fixed by which side C lies on.
Q765CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q20NTA final key
For fixed values of radii of curvature of lens, power of the lens will be ____________.
  1. P ∝ (μ − 1)
  2. P ∝ μ2
  3. P ∝ 1/μ
  4. P ∝ μ−2
Concept to recallLens maker: P = 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2).
  1. With R1, R2 fixed the bracket is a constant, so P ∝ (μ − 1).

Answer: option (1) — P ∝ (μ − 1)

Q766CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q21NTA final key
The graph correctly representing the variation of image distance ‘v’ for a convex lens of focal length ‘f’ versus object distance ‘u’ is ____________.
  1. Graph (1)
  2. Graph (2)
  3. Graph (3)
  4. Graph (4)
Concept to recallLens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f with real objects on the left (u < 0).
  1. For a real object u < 0, so the curve lies to the left of the v-axis.
  2. v = uf/(u + f): as u → −∞, v → f; as u → −f, v → +∞.
  3. Only graph (2) lies in the u < 0, v > 0 quadrant and shoots up as u approaches the axis.

Answer: option (2) — Graph (2)

Q767CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q32NTA final key
The refractive index of the material of an equilateral prism is √2. The angle of minimum deviation of that prism is ____________.
  1. 60°
  2. 75°
  3. 30°
  4. 90°
Concept to recallμ = sin[(A + δm)/2] / sin(A/2).
  1. sin[(60° + δm)/2] = √2 × sin 30° = 1/√2.
  2. (60° + δm)/2 = 45° ⇒ δm = 30°.

Answer: option (3) — 30°

Q768CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q45NTA final key
Lower half of a convex lens is made opaque. Which of the following statement describes the image of the object placed in front of the lens ?
(A) No change in image
(B) Image will show only half of the object
(C) Intensity of image gets reduced
  1. (A) only
  2. (B) only
  3. (C) only
  4. (B) and (C) only
Concept to recallEvery part of a lens forms the whole image; covering part of it only cuts the light gathered.
  1. Rays from every object point still pass through the upper half, so the full image forms at the same place.
  2. Half the light is blocked, so it is dimmer: (C) only.

Answer: option (3) — (C) only

Q769CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q47NTA final key
For an astronomical telescope having objective lens of focal length 10 m and eyepiece lens of focal length 10 cm, telescope’s the tube length and magnification respectively are ____________.
  1. 20 cm, 1
  2. 1000 cm, 1
  3. 1010 cm, 1
  4. 1010 cm, 100
Concept to recallNormal adjustment: L = fo + fe, m = fo/fe.
  1. L = 1000 + 10 = 1010 cm.
  2. m = 1000/10 = 100.

Answer: option (4) — 1010 cm, 100

Q770CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q654NTA final key
Light is incident on an interface between water (μ = 4/3) and glass (μ = 3/2). For total internal reflection, light should be travelling from :
  1. water to glass and ∠i > ∠iC
  2. water to glass and ∠i < ∠iC
  3. glass to water and ∠i < ∠iC
  4. glass to water and ∠i > ∠iC
Concept to recallTIR needs both: denser → rarer medium, and angle of incidence greater than the critical angle.
  1. Glass (3/2) is denser than water (4/3), so light must go glass → water.
  2. And i > iC, where sin iC = (4/3)/(3/2) = 8/9.

Answer: option (4) — glass to water and ∠i > ∠iC

Q771CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q655NTA final key
Match List-I with List-II :
List-I Optical InstrumentList-II Nature of Lens/mirror used
(A) Human eye(I) Concave mirror of large aperture and large focal length
(B) Microscope(II) Objective lens of large aperture and large focal length
(C) Reflecting telescope(III) Lens of adjustable focal length
(D) Refracting telescope(IV) Objective of small aperture and small focal length
  1. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
  2. (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
  3. (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Concept to recallEye: accommodation. Microscope: short-f objective. Telescopes: large-aperture, long-f objective (mirror or lens).
  1. Eye – adjustable lens (III); microscope – small aperture, short f objective (IV);
  2. reflecting telescope – large concave mirror (I); refracting telescope – large long-f objective lens (II).

Answer: option (4) — (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the human eye.
Q772CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q671NTA final key
Arrange the following in increasing order of focal length of convex lens.
(A) Fv focal lengths of voilet
(B) Fr focal lengths of red
(C) Fb focal lengths of blue
(D) Fy focal lengths of yellow
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  2. (A), (C), (D), (B)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (C), (B), (D), (A)
Concept to recall1/f = (μ − 1)(…) and μ is largest for violet, least for red (dispersion).
  1. Larger μ ⇒ shorter f: fviolet < fblue < fyellow < fred.
  2. (A), (C), (D), (B).

Answer: option (2) — (A), (C), (D), (B)

Q773CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q672NTA final key
Light from point source in air falls on a spherical glass surface (n = 1.5 and radius of curvature = 10 cm). The distance of the light source from the glass surface is 50 cm. The position at which the image is formed is :
  1. 100 cm in the air
  2. 150 cm in the glass surface
  3. 200 cm in the air
  4. 50 cm in the glass surface
Concept to recalln2/v − n1/u = (n2 − n1)/R; a convex surface facing the source has R > 0.
  1. u = −50 cm, R = +10 cm, n1 = 1, n2 = 1.5.
  2. 1.5/v + 1/50 = 0.5/10 = 0.05 ⇒ 1.5/v = 0.03 ⇒ v = +50 cm.
  3. Positive v: a real image 50 cm inside the glass.

Answer: option (4) — 50 cm in the glass surface

Q774CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q674NTA final key
For a light pipe as shown in the figure :(A) Optical density of core should be greater than the optical density of cladding
(B) r and θ will always be equal
(C) Optical density of cladding is sinθ.sini / sinr
(D) Optical density of cladding is sinr.sini / sinθ
  1. (A), (B) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (C) only
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallA light pipe works by total internal reflection at the core–cladding boundary, which needs ncore > nclad.
  1. Entry: sin i = ncore sin r. At the boundary (critical incidence θ): ncore sinθ = nclad.
  2. nclad = sinθ sin i / sin r: (C) true, (D) false.
  3. r and θ are complementary (r + θ = 90°), not equal: (B) false. (A) true.

Answer: option (3) — (A), (C) only

NoteStatement (C) treats θ as the critical angle at the core–cladding surface, as the figure intends.
Q775CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q679NTA final key
An equilateral prism is made of material of refractive index √3. Angle of minimum deviation through the prism is :
  1. 60°
  2. 30°
  3. 45°
  4. 0°
Concept to recallμ = sin[(A + δm)/2] / sin(A/2).
  1. sin[(60° + δm)/2] = √3 × ½ = sin 60°.
  2. (60° + δm)/2 = 60° ⇒ δm = 60°.

Answer: option (1) — 60°

Q776CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q17 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A dentist has a small mirror of focal length 1.6 cm. He observes the cavity in the tooth of a patient by holding the mirror at a distance of 8 mm from the cavity. The magnification is:
  1. 1
  2. 1.5
  3. 2
  4. 13
Concept to recallA dentist's mirror is concave, used with the object inside F: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = −v/u.
  1. f = −1.6 cm, u = −0.8 cm.
  2. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/1.6 + 1/0.8 = +1/1.6, so v = +1.6 cm (virtual, behind the mirror).
  3. m = −v/u = −1.6/(−0.8) = 2 (erect, magnified).

Answer: option (3) — 2

Q777CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q3 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A ray is incident normally on the face of an triangular prism of refracting angle of 60°. The refractive index of the prism is 2√3. The angle of deviation will be:
  1. 60°
  2. 30°
  3. 45°
  4. 90°
Concept to recallr1 + r2 = A; sin C = 1/μ; deviation δ = i + e − A.
  1. Normal incidence: i = 0, r1 = 0, so r2 = A = 60°.
  2. sin C = 1/μ = √3/2, so C = 60°: the ray meets the second face at the critical angle and emerges grazing, e = 90°.
  3. δ = i + e − A = 0 + 90° − 60° = 30°.

Answer: option (2) — 30°

Q778CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q40 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A telescope has an objective of focal length 30 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 3.0 cm. It is focused on a scale distant 2.0 m. For seeing with relaxed eye, the separation between the objective and eyepiece would be:
  1. 35.3 cm
  2. 38.3 cm
  3. 37 cm
  4. 30 cm
Concept to recallObjective images the near object at vo; relaxed eye ⇒ that image sits at the eyepiece's focus, L = vo + fe.
  1. 1/vo = 1/30 − 1/200 = 17/600 ⇒ vo = 35.3 cm.
  2. L = 35.3 + 3.0 = 38.3 cm.

Answer: option (2) — 38.3 cm

Trapfo + fe = 33 cm is for an object at infinity; 35.3 cm forgets the eyepiece.
Q779CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q46 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The bottom of a container is a 6 cm thick glass (μ = 1.5) slab. The container contains a thick layer of water (μw = 1.33), 4 cm on top of the glass. What is the apparent position of a scratch on the outer surface of the bottom of the glass slab when viewed through the container?
  1. 1 cm
  2. 2 cm
  3. 3.5 cm
  4. 3 cm
Concept to recallA slab of thickness t raises an object by t(1 − 1/μ) when viewed (near-)normally; shifts of stacked layers add.
  1. Glass: 6(1 − 1/1.5) = 2 cm. Water: 4(1 − 1/1.33) ≈ 1 cm.
  2. The scratch appears raised by 3 cm (i.e. 7 cm below the water surface instead of 10 cm).

Answer: option (4) — 3 cm

NoteThe options give the apparent shift (rise) of the scratch: 3 cm.
Q780CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q50 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Two lenses of power 3D and −1D are kept in contact. The focal length of the combined lens would be:
  1. 50 cm
  2. 200 cm
  3. 100 cm

Concept to recallLenses in contact: P = P1 + P2; f (cm) = 100/P.
  1. P = 3 − 1 = 2 D; f = 100/2 = 50 cm.

Answer: option (1) — 50 cm

Q781CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q18 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
At the time of sun set the sun appears to be at an altitude higher than its actual position. This is because of
  1. Absorption of light
  2. Reflection of light
  3. Refraction of light
  4. Dispersion of light
Concept to recallAtmospheric refraction: light bends towards the normal as it enters denser lower air.
  1. Atmospheric refraction lifts the apparent position of the sun near the horizon.

Answer: option (3) — Refraction of light

Q782CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q21 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The refractive index of air with respect to glass 23. The refractive index of diamond with respect to air is 2.4. What will be the refractive index of glass with respect to diamond?
  1. 0.28
  2. 0.625
  3. 1.60
  4. 3.60
Concept to recallaμb = μb/μa; and aμb = 1/bμa.
  1. μglass = 1/(2/3) = 1.5; μdiamond = 2.4.
  2. dμg = μg/μd = 1.5/2.4 = 0.625.

Answer: option (2) — 0.625

Q783CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q3 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In a concave mirror, an object is placed at a distance x from the focus and the image is formed at a distance y from the focus. What is the focal length of the mirror?
  1. (xy)1/2
  2. (x + y)2
  3. xy−1
  4. xy
Concept to recallNewton's form of the mirror equation, with distances measured from the focus: xy = f2.
  1. u = −(f + x), v = −(f + y). Put into 1/u + 1/v = 1/f with f → −f:
  2. 1/(f + x) + 1/(f + y) = 1/f ⇒ f(2f + x + y) = (f + x)(f + y) ⇒ f2 = xy.
  3. f = √(xy).

Answer: option (1) — (xy)1/2

Q784CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q33 · Prepp reconstructionworked here
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. Dispersion is the splitting of light into it's constituent colours.
B. The unit for power of a lens is m−1.
C. Optical fibres consist of glass fibres coated with a thin layer of material of higher refractive index.
D. Cassegrain telescope has the advantages of a large focal length in a short telescope.
E. Glass is a dispersive medium.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C and E Only
  2. A, B, D and E Only
  3. B, C, D and E Only
  4. C, D and E Only
Concept to recallAn optical fibre guides light by total internal reflection, which needs the cladding to be optically rarer than the core.
  1. A, E true. B true (dioptre = m−1). D true (the folded path gives a long focal length in a short tube).
  2. C false: the cladding has a lower refractive index; with a higher one there would be no TIR.

Answer: option (2) — A, B, D and E Only

NotePrepp's unofficial key gives option (1); the working above shows why that cannot be right. That choice includes statement C, which is false.

Q788CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q47 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  3. 7 cm to the left of third lens

Concept to recallSuccessive lenses: the image of one is the object of the next; 1/v − 1/u = 1/f with signs.

Q790CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 3 · Q8 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following change is observed when light travels from air to glass?

Q791CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q10NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. Dispersion is the splitting of light into it’s constituent colours.
B. The unit for power of a lens is m−1.
C. Optical fibres consist of glass fibres coated with a thin layer of material of higher refractive index.
D. Cassegrain telescope has the advantages of a large focal length in a short telescope.
E. Glass is a dispersive medium.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C and E Only
  2. A, B, D and E Only
  3. B, C, D and E Only
  4. C, D and E Only
Concept to recallOptical fibre: core of higher n, cladding of lower n, so light is trapped by total internal reflection.
  1. C is false: the cladding has a lower refractive index than the core.
  2. A, B (dioptre = m−1), D and E are true.

Q792CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q20NTA final key
In a concave mirror, an object is placed at a distance x from the focus and the image is formed at a distance y from the focus. What is the focal length of the mirror?

Q795CUET 2023 · 23 May, Shift 3 · Q41NTA final key
At the time of sunset the sun appears to be at an altitude higher than its actual position. This is because of

Q796CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q11 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. An equiconvex lens of f = 20 cm is cut as (along the plane of the lens): the focal length of each part is 10 cm.
B. An equiconvex lens of f = 20 cm is cut as (along the principal axis): the focal length of each part is 20 cm.
C. If an equiconvex lens of refractive index μ1 is placed in a liquid of μ2 such that (μ1 > μ2), it will not change its nature.
D. A convex lens of f = 20 cm is cut as (along the plane of the lens): the focal length of each part is 40 cm.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B only
  2. A, B, C only
  3. B, C Only
  4. B, C, D Only
Concept to recall1/f = (μrel − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2). Cutting along the axis keeps both curved faces; cutting along the lens plane leaves one curved face (R2 = ∞).
  1. Equiconvex, R1 = −R2 = R: 1/20 = (μ − 1)(2/R).
  2. Cut along the lens plane: each plano-convex half has 1/f′ = (μ − 1)/R ⇒ f′ = 40 cm. A false, D true.
  3. Cut along the axis: each half keeps both radii ⇒ f = 20 cm. B true.
  4. μ1 > μ2 ⇒ μrel > 1: still converging. C true.

Answer: option (4) — B, C, D Only

NotePrepp shows the cuts only as small lens sketches; they are redrawn and described in words here.
Q797CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q19 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The time taken by light to travel normally through a glass plate of thickness 1 mm would be: (Take refractive index of glass = 1.5)
  1. 0.1 × 10−13 s
  2. 12 × 10−5 s
  3. 5 × 10−12 s
  4. 1.5 × 10−5 s
Concept to recallSpeed in a medium v = c/μ, so t = d/v = μd/c.
  1. t = 1.5 × 10−3/(3 × 108)
  2. = 5 × 10−12 s.

Answer: option (3) — 5 × 10−12 s

Q798CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q30 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A bubble in glass slab (μ = 1.5) when viewed from one side appears at 5 cm and 2 cm from other side, then the thickness of the glass slab is:
  1. 2.5 cm
  2. 7.5 cm
  3. 10.5 cm
  4. 17.5 cm
Concept to recallApparent depth = real depth/μ.
  1. Real depths: 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 cm and 2 × 1.5 = 3 cm.
  2. Thickness = 7.5 + 3 = 10.5 cm.

Answer: option (3) — 10.5 cm

TrapAdding the apparent depths (7 cm) and stopping there forgets that each must be multiplied by μ.
Q799CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q38 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A ray of light passes through four transparent media with refractive index μ1, μ2, μ3 and μ4 shown in figure. The surfaces of all media are parallel. If BC and DE are parallel, we must have
  1. μ1 = μ4
  2. μ2 = μ3
  3. μ2 = μ4
  4. μ1 = μ2
Concept to recallAcross parallel interfaces μ sin θ is the same in every layer.
  1. μ1 sin θ1 = μ2 sin θ2 = μ3 sin θ3 = μ4 sin θ4.
  2. BC ∥ DE ⇒ θ2 = θ4 ⇒ μ2 = μ4.

Answer: option (3) — μ2 = μ4

Q800CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q5 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A convex mirror produces the magnification 1/3 and 1/4 when the object is placed at the points P and Q in front of the mirror.
  1. P is far from the mirror as compared to Q.
  2. Q is far from the mirror as compared to P
  3. P and Q both are coinciding
  4. Convex mirror produces the magnification always greater than 1.
Concept to recallFor a convex mirror the virtual image shrinks as the object moves away: m = f/(f − u) falls with distance.
  1. Smaller magnification ⇒ object farther away.
  2. 1/4 < 1/3, so Q (m = 1/4) is farther from the mirror than P.

Answer: option (2) — Q is far from the mirror as compared to P

NotePrepp prints “convex minor”; read as convex mirror.
Q801CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q10worked here
A concave mirror has radius of curvature 2 m. Light from a distant star is incident on the mirror. The distance of the image of the star from the mirror is:
  1. Infinite

Q802CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q15worked here
What is the effect on the focal length of a convex lens when it is immersed in a liquid whose refractive index is equal to refractive index of the lens?
  1. Focal length will become infinity
  2. Focal length will become zero
  3. Focal length will reduce but not become zero
  4. Focal length remains unchanged
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (nlens/nmedium − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2).

Answer: option (1) — Focal length will become infinity

Q803CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q19worked here
A glass prism of angle 60° has an angle of minimum deviation of 30° for a given colour of light. The refractive index of glass for that colour of light is:

Concept to recalln = sin[(A + δm)/2]/sin(A/2).

Q804CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q2worked here
The resolving power of a refracting type telescope can be increased by:
  1. Choosing a large diameter objective lens
  2. Choosing a small diameter objective lens
  3. Increasing wavelength of light
  4. Using an objective lens of large focal length
Concept to recallResolving power of a telescope = 1/Δθ = D/(1.22λ): grows with aperture D, falls with λ, independent of focal length.
  1. RP ∝ D/λ, so a larger objective diameter increases it.

Answer: option (1) — Choosing a large diameter objective lens

Q805CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q39worked here
If in a plano-convex lens, the radius of the convex surface is 10 cm and the focal length is 30 cm, then the refractive index of the material will be:

  3. 1.66
  4. 3.0
Concept to recallPlano-convex: 1/f = (n − 1)/R (the flat face has R = ∞).

Q806CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q1 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Resolving power of a telescope can be increased by increasing:

  2. Diameter of eye piece
  3. Focal length of eyepiece
  4. Diameter of Objective lens
Concept to recallResolving power of a telescope = D/1.22λ, D = aperture (diameter) of the objective.
  1. RP ∝ D/λ.
  2. Larger objective aperture (or shorter λ) raises it; the eyepiece does not matter.

Answer: option (4) — Diameter of Objective lens

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: resolving power.
Q807CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q16 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
What will be the time by light to travel 2 cm thickness of glass of refractive index 1.5?

Q808CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q22 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. −5 cm

  4. +5 cm
Concept to recallAstronomical telescope: m = fo/fe, both lenses converging; long objective, short eyepiece.

Q809CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q3 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
(A) Contracting of eye ball(I) Myopia
(B) Controls the shape of eye lens(II) Cornea
(C) Elongation of eye ball(III) Ciliary Muscle
(D) Control the light entering in eyes(IV) Hypermetropia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
  2. (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
  3. (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Concept to recallEyeball too short → hypermetropia; too long → myopia. Ciliary muscles change the lens shape (accommodation).
  1. (A) shortened eyeball → hypermetropia (IV); (C) elongated → myopia (I).
  2. (B) lens shape → ciliary muscle (III); (D) the front of the eye that admits light → cornea (II).

Q810CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q44 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) When light rays undergo two internal reflections inside a raindrop, a secondary rainbow is formed.
(B) The angle between the emergent ray and angle of prism is called the angle of deviation.
(C) Light undergoes successive total internal reflections as it moves through an optical fiber.
(D) A telescope provides angular magnification of distant objects.
(E) A simple magnifier is a diverging lens of small focal length.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (E) only
  2. (A), (C) and (D) only
  3. (B), (C), (D) and (E) only
  4. (A), (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallDeviation is the angle between the incident and emergent rays; a simple magnifier is a converging lens of short focal length.
  1. A true (primary: one internal reflection; secondary: two).
  2. B false: deviation is between incident and emergent rays.
  3. C true; D true.
  4. E false: a magnifying glass is converging.

Answer: option (2) — (A), (C) and (D) only

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the rainbow. Statement (A), on the rainbow, is the off-syllabus part; the other statements are in the syllabus.
Q811CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q47 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
An object is placed before a convex lens and its real image is obtained. Now if half of the surface is covered with paper. The result will be:
  1. No image will be formed
  2. Half image will be formed
  3. Image will be same as before
  4. Full image will be formed with less brightness
Concept to recallEvery part of a lens forms the whole image; covering part of it removes light, not part of the image.
  1. Rays from every object point still pass through the uncovered half.
  2. Full image, about half as bright.

Answer: option (4) — Full image will be formed with less brightness

Q812CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q34key re-derived
The least distance of distinct vision of a person is 50 cm. He wants to read a book placed at 25 cm. The focal length of the spectacles would be:
  1. +25 cm
  2. −25 cm
  3. +50 cm
  4. −50 cm
Concept to recallHypermetropia: the lens must form a virtual image at the near point (v = −50 cm) of an object at 25 cm. 1/f = 1/v − 1/u.
  1. u = −25 cm, v = −50 cm.
  2. 1/f = −1/50 + 1/25 = +1/50 ⇒ f = +50 cm (convex).

Answer: option (3) — +50 cm

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the human eye.
Q813CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q36key re-derived
When a ray of light enters a glass slab from air:
  1. its wavelength decreases
  2. its wavelength increases
  3. its frequency increases
  4. neither its wavelength nor its frequency changes
Concept to recallFrequency is fixed by the source; in a medium v = c/n, so λ = λ0/n.
  1. Frequency unchanged; speed falls by n, so wavelength falls by n.

Answer: option (1) — its wavelength decreases

Q814CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q49key re-derived
The focal length of the objective of a microscope is fo and that of the eye piece is fe. The aperture of objective is do and that of eye piece is de. Which of the following relation is correct?

  2. fo < fe, do < de
  3. fo > fe, do < de
  4. fo < fe, do > de
Concept to recallCompound microscope: objective of very short focal length and small aperture (close to a tiny object); eyepiece longer focal length, larger aperture. (A telescope is the opposite: fo > fe, do > de.)
  1. Microscope: fo < fe and do < de.

Answer: option (2) — fo < fe, do < de

TrapOption (1) describes a telescope.
Q815CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q26NTA final key
When a ray of light enters from denser medium to rarer medium, its velocity is doubled. The critical angle for total internal reflection will be :
  1. 60°
  2. 45°
  3. 30°
  4. 90°
Concept to recallsin C = 1/n21 = nrarer/ndenser = vdenser/vrarer.

  2. sin C = 1/2 ⇒ C = 30°.

Q816CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q27NTA final key
Which of the following is/are responsible for the formation of Rainbow ?
(A) Dispersion of light
(B) Interference of light
(C) Reflection of light
(D) Refraction of light

  1. (B) and (C) only
  2. (A) and (C) only
  3. (A), (C) and (D) only
  4. (A) only
Concept to recallRainbow: sunlight is refracted (and dispersed) entering a drop, internally reflected, and refracted out.
  1. Refraction with dispersion separates colours; internal reflection sends them back to the observer.
  2. Interference plays no part: (A), (C), (D).

Q817CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q28NTA final key
The shape of graph between 1/u and 1/v in case of a convex lens is :
Concept to recallLens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, i.e. 1/v = 1/u + 1/f: a straight line of slope +1.
  1. Real-object values: u < 0, so 1/u lies on the negative x-axis; 1/v > 0 for a real image.
  2. Line of slope +1 with intercepts 1/f on the 1/v axis and −1/f on the 1/u axis: graph (1), AB.

Answer: option (1) —

Q818CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q30NTA final key
Two thin lenses of power +3D and −1D are held in contact with each other. Focal length of the combination would be :
  1. 5 m
  2. 50 cm
  3. 10 m
  4. 100 cm
Concept to recallLenses in contact: P = P1 + P2; f (m) = 1/P.
  1. P = 3 − 1 = +2 D.
  2. f = 1/2 m = 50 cm.

Answer: option (2) — 50 cm

Q819CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key
Choose the correct formula for magnifying power of a simple microscope from the following
  1. m = 1 − df
  2. m = 1 + df
  3. m = 1 − fd
  4. m = 1 + fd
Concept to recallSimple microscope, image at the near point d = 25 cm: m = 1 + d/f (image at infinity: d/f).
  1. With v = −d, the lens formula gives u, and m = v/u = 1 + d/f.

Answer: option (2) — m = 1 + df

Q820CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q28NTA final key
Light from a point source in air falls on spherical glass surface (n = 1.4 and radius of curvature 20 cm). The distance of light source from the glass surface is 150 cm, At what position is the image formed?
  1. 150 cm from glass surface in the direction of incident light
  2. 105 cm from glass surface in the direction of incident light
  3. 150 cm from glass surface towards light source
  4. 105 cm from glass surface towards light source
Concept to recallRefraction at a spherical surface: n2/v − n1/u = (n2 − n1)/R.
  1. u = −150 cm, R = +20 cm, n1 = 1, n2 = 1.4.
  2. 1.4/v = 0.4/20 − 1/150 = 0.02 − 0.00667 = 0.01333, so v = +105 cm.
  3. Positive: a real image 105 cm inside the glass, in the direction of the incident light.

Answer: option (2) — 105 cm from glass surface in the direction of incident light

Q821CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q30NTA final key
For a glass prism (μ = √3), the angle of minimum deviation is equal to the angle of prism. What is the angle of prism?
  1. π6
  2. π4
  3. π3
  4. 2π3
Concept to recallμ = sin[(A + δm)/2] / sin(A/2).
  1. With δm = A: μ = sin A/sin(A/2) = 2 cos(A/2).
  2. 2 cos(A/2) = √3 ⇒ A/2 = 30°, A = 60° = π/3.

Answer: option (3) — π3

Q822CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q49NTA final key
At what distance should an object be placed from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm to obtain a real image three times the size of the object ?
  1. 10 cm
  2. 20 cm
  3. 40 cm
  4. 50 cm
Concept to recallLens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; real image: m = v/u = −3.
  1. v = −3u. With u = −x: 1/(3x) + 1/x = 1/15.
  2. 4/(3x) = 1/15 ⇒ x = 20 cm.

Answer: option (2) — 20 cm

Trap10 cm (between F and the lens) gives a virtual, upright image of magnification 3.
Q823CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q26NTA final key
Light is travelling from one medium to other medium as given in the options. In which of the following options total internal reflection will be possible?
  1. Air to water
  2. Air to glass
  3. Water to glass
  4. Glass to water
Concept to recallTIR needs light going from a denser to a rarer medium, with angle of incidence above the critical angle.

Q824CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q29NTA final key
An astronomical telescope consists of an objective of focal length 50 cm and eyepiece of focal length 2 cm is focused on the moon so that the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision (25 cm). Assuming angular diameter of moon as (1/2)° at the objective, the angular size of image is:
  1. 27°
  2. 13.5°
  3. 1°
  4. 11.2°
Concept to recallTelescope, image at near point: m = (fo/fe)(1 + fe/D); angular size of image = m × angle subtended by object.
  1. m = (50/2)(1 + 2/25) = 25 × 1.08 = 27.
  2. Angular size = 27 × 0.5° = 13.5°.

Answer: option (2) — 13.5°

Trap27° forgets to multiply by the moon’s half-degree.
Q825CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q30NTA final key
A spherical air lens of radii R1 = R2 = 10 cm is cut from a glass (μ = 1.5) cylinder as shown in figure. Its focal length is f1. If a liquid of refractive index 2 is filled in the space then the focal length of liquid lens becomes f2. Calculate f1 and f2. Choose the correct options from the following.
  1. f1 = 15 cm, f2 = 30 cm
  2. f1 = −15 cm, f2 = +30 cm
  3. f1 = −15 cm, f2 = +15 cm
  4. f1 = −30 cm, f2 = −15 cm
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (nlens/nmedium − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2).
  1. Biconvex shape: (1/R1 − 1/R2) = 1/10 + 1/10 = 1/5 cm−1.
  2. Air lens in glass: 1/f1 = (1/1.5 − 1)(1/5) = −1/15, f1 = −15 cm (diverging).
  3. Liquid (n = 2) lens in glass: 1/f2 = (2/1.5 − 1)(1/5) = +1/15, f2 = +15 cm.

Answer: option (3) — f1 = −15 cm, f2 = +15 cm

TrapA convex-shaped lens of a rarer material diverges light.
Q826CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q31NTA final key
Linear magnification produced by a mirror is + 1.5
  1. It is a concave mirror with object between F and 2F
  2. It is a concave mirror with object between F and Pole
  3. It is a convex mirror with object at infinity
  4. It is a convex mirror with object anywhere in front of the mirror.
Concept to recallPositive m = virtual, erect image; |m| > 1 = enlarged. Only a concave mirror with the object inside F does both.
  1. Erect and magnified: concave mirror, object between F and P.
  2. A convex mirror always gives |m| < 1.

Answer: option (2) — It is a concave mirror with object between F and Pole

Q827CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q49NTA final key
The graph shows the variation of the magnification (m) produced by a thin lens with image distance (v). The focal length of the lens is :
  1. b2ac
  2. b2ca
  3. ac
  4. bc
Concept to recallFor a lens m = v/u and 1/v − 1/u = 1/f give m = 1 − v/f: a straight line of slope (magnitude) 1/f.
  1. Multiply the lens formula by v: 1 − v/u = v/f, so m = 1 − v/f.
  2. |slope| = |Δm/Δv| = c/b = 1/f, so f = b/c.

Answer: option (4) — bc

Q828CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q29NTA final key
If a light ray travels from denser to rarer medium. Which of the following statement/s are correct ?
(A) Energy increases
(B) Frequency remain same
(C) Phase changes by 90°
(D) Velocity increases
(E) Wavelength decreases
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (B) only
  2. (B) and (D) only
  3. (A) and (C) only
  4. (E) only
Concept to recallOn refraction the frequency (and photon energy) is fixed by the source; v = c/n and λ = v/f change together.
  1. Frequency and energy hf stay the same: (B) true, (A) false.
  2. Rarer medium has smaller n: v increases (D true) and so does λ (E false).
  3. Refraction introduces no 90° phase change (C false).

Answer: option (2) — (B) and (D) only

Q829CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q38NTA final key
To increase magnification power of refracting type Telescope, we should increase :
  1. the focal length of the objective
  2. the focal length of the eyepiece
  3. aperture of the objective
  4. aperture of the eyepiece
Concept to recallTelescope (normal adjustment): m = fo/fe. Aperture sets resolving power and brightness.
  1. m = fo/fe grows with fo (and with a shorter fe).

Answer: option (1) — the focal length of the objective

TrapA bigger objective aperture improves resolving power, not magnification.
Q830CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q39NTA final key
The radius of curvature of the curved surface of a plano-convex lens is 20 cm. If the refractive index of the material of the lens be 1.5, then focal length of lens will be :
  1. 20 cm
  2. −20 cm
  3. −40 cm
  4. 40 cm
Concept to recallLens maker: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2); a plane face has R = ∞.
  1. 1/f = (1.5 − 1)(1/20 − 0) = 1/40.
  2. f = +40 cm (converging).

Answer: option (4) — 40 cm

Q831CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q40NTA final key
A boy of height 1 m stands infront of a convex mirror. His distance from the mirror is equal to the focal length of the mirror, the height of the image is :
  1. 0.33 m
  2. 0.25 m
  3. 0.67 m
  4. 0.50 m
Concept to recallMirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = −v/u; a convex mirror has f > 0 (real-is-negative convention).
  1. u = −f, focal length +f: 1/v = 1/f + 1/f = 2/f, v = f/2.
  2. m = −v/u = (f/2)/f = 1/2.
  3. Image height = 0.5 m (erect, virtual).

Answer: option (4) — 0.50 m

Q832CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q33 (NTA Q.No. 423)NTA final key
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II (In the context of Young’s double slit experiment)
LIST-ILIST-II
A. The width of one slit is slightly increased.I. The fringe width increases.
B. One slit is closed.II. Interference pattern becomes less sharp.
C. The width of the source slit is increased.III. Maximum intensity increases
D. Light of smaller frequency is used.IV. Interference pattern disappears

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
  2. A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
  3. A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
  4. A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
Concept to recallFringe width β = λD/d; a wider slit passes more light; a wide source slit destroys spatial coherence.
  1. A: more light through one slit → maximum intensity rises (III).
  2. B: one slit gives single-slit diffraction only → interference disappears (IV).
  3. C: wider source slit → fringes blur (II).
  4. D: lower frequency = longer λ → β increases (I).

Answer: option (3) — A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

Q833CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q34 (NTA Q.No. 424)NTA final key
In a Young’s double slit experiment, the intensity at the center of the screen is I . If one of the slits is closed, the intensity at the center of the screen now will be:
  1. 12
  2. 1
  3. 14
  4. 13
Concept to recallTwo equal coherent waves in phase: amplitudes add, I = (2a)2 = 4I0.
  1. Both open: I = 4I0. One closed: I0 = I/4.

Answer: option (3) — 14

TrapIntensities do not simply halve: in phase they add as amplitudes.
NoteThe options are printed as bare fractions; read them as multiples of I (the answer is I/4).
Q834CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q36 (NTA Q.No. 426)NTA final key
If the two slits in a Young’s double slit experiment have their widths in the ratio 4:1, then the ratio of intensities at maxima and minima in the interference pattern will be
  1. 16 : 3
  2. 16 : 1
  3. 25 : 9
  4. 9 : 1
Concept to recallIntensity ∝ slit width ∝ amplitude2; Imax/Imin = (a1 + a2)2/(a1 − a2)2.
  1. I1 : I2 = 4 : 1 ⇒ a1 : a2 = 2 : 1.
  2. Ratio = (2 + 1)2/(2 − 1)2 = 9 : 1.

Answer: option (4) — 9 : 1

TrapTreating 4 : 1 as the amplitude ratio gives 25 : 9.
Q835CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q4key re-derived
The Young’s double slit interference experiment is performed using light consisting of 480 nm and 600 nm wavelengths to form interference patterns. The least number of the bright fringes of 480 nm light that are required for the first coincidence with the bright fringes formed by 600 nm light is:
  1. 4
  2. 8
  3. 6
  4. 5
Concept to recallBright fringes coincide where n1λ1 = n2λ2 (same y = nλD/d).
  1. n1(480) = n2(600) ⇒ n1/n2 = 600/480 = 5/4.
  2. Smallest whole numbers: the 5th bright of 480 nm meets the 4th bright of 600 nm.

Answer: option (4) — 5

Trap4 is the count for the 600 nm light, not for 480 nm.
Q836CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q7key re-derived
The distance estimation for which ray optics is a good approximation for an aperture of 3 mm and wavelength 300 nm would be:
  1. 40 m
  2. 30 m
  3. 20 m
  4. 10 m
Concept to recallFresnel distance zF = a2/λ: up to about this distance, diffraction spreading is smaller than the aperture and ray optics holds.
  1. zF = (3 × 10−3)2/(3 × 10−7) = 9 × 10−6/3 × 10−7 = 30 m.

Answer: option (2) — 30 m

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: the Fresnel distance.
Q837CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1key re-derived
In Young’s double slit experiment, if the distance between the slits is increased while keeping all other parameters constant, the fringe width will:
  1. Increase
  2. Decrease
  3. Remain unchanged
  4. First increase then decrease
Concept to recallFringe width β = λD/d.
  1. β ∝ 1/d: a larger slit separation gives narrower fringes.

Answer: option (2) — Decrease

Q838CUET 2026 · 19 May, Shift 1 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q3key re-derived
Polarisation of light proves that light waves are:
  1. Longitudinal
  2. Transverse
  3. Stationary
  4. Electromagnetic only in vacuum
Concept to recallOnly a transverse wave has a direction of vibration across the ray that a polaroid can select.
  1. Longitudinal waves (e.g. sound) cannot be polarised; light can, so it is transverse.

Answer: option (2) — Transverse

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: polarisation.
Q839CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q36NTA final key
In a Young’s double-slit experiment, two slits are 1.5 mm apart while the screen is 1.2 m away. When a light of wavelength 600 nm is incident on slits, the fringe width will be
  1. 0.48 mm
  2. 4.5 mm
  3. 4.8 mm
  4. 4.2 mm
Concept to recallFringe width β = λD/d.
  1. β = 600 × 10−9 × 1.2/(1.5 × 10−3) = 4.8 × 10−4 m = 0.48 mm.

Q840CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q38NTA final key
A polaroid sheet is rotated between two crossed polarizers. The intensity of transmitted light would be maximum, when the angle between the axes of the first polarizer and the polaroid sheet is
  1. π/2
  2. π/4
  3. π
  4. π/3
Concept to recallMalus’s law I = I0 cos2θ at each sheet.
  1. After P1: I1. After the sheet at θ: I1cos2θ.
  2. The last polarizer is at 90° to P1, i.e. at (90° − θ) to the sheet: I = I1cos2θ sin2θ = (I1/4) sin22θ.
  3. Maximum when 2θ = π/2, i.e. θ = π/4.

Answer: option (2) — π/4

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus, but asked by NTA in 2025. Topic: polarisation.
Q841CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q32 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In a Young’s double-slit experiment, the slits are separated by 0.28 mm and the wavelength of light used is 6000 Å. The fringes are observed on a screen placed 1.4 m away from the slits. The distance between the central bright fringe and the fourth bright fringe will be
  1. 0.3 cm
  2. 0.6 cm
  3. 1.2 cm
  4. 2.4 cm
Concept to recalln-th bright fringe: yn = nλD/d.
  1. β = 6 × 10−7 × 1.4/(0.28 × 10−3) = 3 × 10−3 m.
  2. y4 = 4β = 1.2 × 10−2 m = 1.2 cm.

Answer: option (3) — 1.2 cm

Trap0.3 cm is one fringe width only.
Q842CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q9 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Two coherent light sources have intensities in the ratio 25: 16. The ratio of the intensities of maxima to minima, in the interference pattern due to them would be
  1. 25 : 16
  2. 9:1
  3. 4:1
  4. 81 :1
Concept to recallI ∝ a2; Imax/Imin = (a1 + a2)2/(a1 − a2)2.
  1. a1/a2 = √(25/16) = 5/4.
  2. Ratio = (5 + 4)2/(5 − 4)2 = 81 : 1.

Answer: option (4) — 81 :1

Trap9 : 1 forgets to square the amplitude ratio.
Q843CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q16worked here
In a single slit experiment, a diffraction pattern is obtained on the screen for yellow light. What will be the effect on the diffraction pattern, if yellow light is replaced by X-rays?
  1. diffraction pattern will not be observed
  2. number of fringes will decrease
  3. number of fringes will increase
  4. central maximum will become narrower
Concept to recallDiffraction is noticeable only when the aperture a is comparable to λ; angular spread ≈ λ/a.
  1. X-ray λ ≈ 10−10 m, about 10−6 of a typical slit width.
  2. The angle λ/a is then so small that the light goes straight through: no visible diffraction pattern.

Answer: option (1) — diffraction pattern will not be observed

NoteWorked answer. Strictly the pattern shrinks by a factor of about 6000, so “narrower central maximum” is the formula’s literal prediction; the intended answer is that the pattern is no longer observable.
Q844CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q19worked here
In Young’s double slit experiment, slits are illuminated by light of wavelength 650 nm. The slits are 0.13 cm apart and the screen is placed 1.2 m away. What will be the separation of the adjacent maxima?
  1. 0.0006 mm
  2. 0.006 mm
  3. 0.06 mm
  4. 0.6 mm
Concept to recallβ = λD/d.
  1. β = 650 × 10−9 × 1.2 / 1.3 × 10−3 = 6 × 10−4 m = 0.6 mm.

Answer: option (4) — 0.6 mm

Q845CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q27worked here
A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength 900 nm passes through a long slit of width 0.4 mm. The angular divergence in which most of the light is diffracted, is:
  1. 8.9 × 10−3 rad
  2. 7.2 × 10−3 rad
  3. 3.6 × 10−3 rad
  4. 4.5 × 10−3 rad
Concept to recallMost light lies in the central maximum, between the first minima at θ = ±λ/a: angular width 2λ/a.
  1. λ/a = 900 × 10−9/0.4 × 10−3 = 2.25 × 10−3 rad.
  2. Angular spread = 2λ/a = 4.5 × 10−3 rad.

Answer: option (4) — 4.5 × 10−3 rad

Trapλ/a (2.25 × 10−3 rad) is only the half-width.
Q846CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q7worked here
The fringe width in Young’s double slit experiment is 2.4 × 10−4 m, when red light of wavelength 6400 Å is used. The decrease in the fringe width, if light of wavelength 4000 Å is used instead of red light, will be:
  1. 0.9 × 10−4 m
  2. 9 × 10−4 m
  3. 1.5 × 10−4 m
  4. 2 × 10−4 m
Concept to recallβ = λD/d ∝ λ.
  1. New β = 2.4 × 10−4 × 4000/6400 = 1.5 × 10−4 m.
  2. Decrease = 2.4 − 1.5 = 0.9 × 10−4 m.

Answer: option (1) — 0.9 × 10−4 m

Q847CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q13worked here
What type of wavefront will emerge from a (i) distant light source and (ii) point source?
  1. (i) Spherical; (ii) Plane
  2. (i) Plane ; (ii) Spherical
  3. (i) Spherical ; (ii) Spherical
  4. (i) Plane; (ii) Plane
Concept to recallA point source gives spherical wavefronts; far away a small part of a sphere is effectively flat.
  1. Distant source: plane wavefront.
  2. Point source: spherical wavefront.

Answer: option (2) — (i) Plane ; (ii) Spherical

Q848CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q14worked here
In a single slit diffraction experiment, first minima for λ1 = 600 nm coincides with first maxima for wavelength λ2. The value of λ2 is
  1. 400 nm
  2. 600 nm
  3. 440 nm
  4. 300 nm
Concept to recallSingle slit: minima a sinθ = nλ; secondary maxima a sinθ ≈ (n + ½)λ.
  1. First minimum of λ1: a sinθ = 600 nm.
  2. First (secondary) maximum of λ2: a sinθ = 1.5λ2.
  3. λ2 = 600/1.5 = 400 nm.

Answer: option (1) — 400 nm

Q849CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q21worked here
Identify the INCORRECT statement(s) in the context of phenomenon of interference.
  1. (A) All bright and dark fringes have equal width.
  2. (B) All bright fringes have the same intensity.
  3. (C) Fringe width depends on the distance of screen from the slits.
  4. (D) All dark and bright fringes are not equally spaced.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (C) and (D) only
  4. (D) only
Concept to recallYDSE: β = λD/d, the same for every fringe; ideal fringes of equal intensity.
  1. (A), (B), (C) are true for Young’s double slit.
  2. (D) is false: the fringes are equally spaced.

Answer: option (4) — (D) only

NoteThe re-typeset numbers the statements 1–4; they are the (A)–(D) the options refer to.
Q850CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q28worked here
For what distance is ray optics a good approximation when the aperture is 3 mm wide and the wavelength is 500 nm?
  1. 15 m
  2. 16 m
  3. 17 m
  4. 18 m
Concept to recallFresnel distance zF = a2/λ; ray optics holds for distances up to zF.
  1. zF = (3 × 10−3)2/500 × 10−9 = 9 × 10−6/5 × 10−7 = 18 m.

Answer: option (4) — 18 m

Q851CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q7worked here
On which of the following factors angular fringe width does not depend?
  1. wavelength
  2. distance between slits
  3. ratio of wavelength and distance between slits
  4. distance between slits and screen
Concept to recallAngular fringe width θ = β/D = λ/d.
  1. θ = λ/d contains no D.
  2. So it does not depend on the slit–screen distance (the linear width β does).

Q852CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q16worked here
Read the following statements carefully and identify the correct statements.
  1. (A) Most interference and diffraction effects exist even for longitudinal waves like sound in air
  2. (B) Optical fibers work on the phenomenon of total internal reflection
  3. (C) Optical density and mass density are the same
  4. (D) Polarisation phenomena are specific to transverse waves like light waves
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (D) only
  2. (A), (B) and (C) only
  3. (A), (B) and (D) only
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallInterference and diffraction need only superposition; polarisation needs transverse oscillation.
  1. (A), (B), (D) true.
  2. (C) false: optical density is about refractive index (light speed), not mass per volume; turpentine is optically denser but lighter than water.

Answer: option (3) — (A), (B) and (D) only

Q853CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q17worked here
Visible light of wavelength 600 nm falls normally on a single slit and diffraction pattern is obtained on a screen. It is found that the second diffraction minima is at π/3. If the first minimum is obtained at θ1, then θ1 is: (Given: sin 25° = √3/4)

  2. π/4

  4. π/9

Q854CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q31worked here
Identify the correct statements among the following.
  1. (A) The wavefront for a point source of light is in a spherical shape, rays are all radial from the point source,

Q855CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q38worked here
