Q858CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q22NTA final key
Using light from a monochromatic source to study diffraction in a single slit of width 0.1 mm, the linear width of central maxima is measured to be 5 mm on a screen held 50 cm away. The wavelength of light used is ____________.
  1. 2.5 × 10−7 m
  2. 4 × 10−7 m
  3. 5 × 10−7 m
  4. 7.5 × 10−7 m
Concept to recallSingle slit: width of central maximum = 2λD/a.
  1. λ = (width)(a)/(2D) = (5 × 10−3)(10−4)/(2 × 0.5).

Q859CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q46NTA final key

  1. 1 cm
  2. 0.15 cm
  3. 1.5 cm
  4. 0.1 cm
Concept to recallYDSE fringe width β = λD/d.

Q860CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q656NTA final key
In a Young’s double-slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength λ, the intensity of light at a point on the screen is I0, where path difference between two interfering waves is λ. The path difference between the interfering waves at a point where the intensity is I02, will be :
  1. λ/4
  2. λ/2
  3. λ
  4. 2λ
Concept to recallI = Imax cos2(φ/2), φ = (2π/λ) × path difference.
  1. Path difference λ is a maximum, so Imax = I0.
  2. cos2(φ/2) = 1/2 ⇒ φ = π/2 ⇒ Δx = (λ/2π)(π/2) = λ/4.

Answer: option (1) — λ/4

Q861CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q673NTA final key
Read the following :
(A) The width of central band in diffraction pattern.
(B) The width of first bright band in diffraction pattern.
(C) The width of central band in diffraction pattern if D is doubled
(D) The width of first bright band in diffraction pattern if D is tripled
Choose the correct answer from the options given below in increasing order of width.
  1. (A), (B), (D), (C)
  2. (A), (C), (D), (B)
  3. (C), (A), (D), (B)
  4. (B), (A), (D), (C)
Concept to recallSingle slit: central maximum 2λD/a; every secondary maximum λD/a. All widths ∝ D.
  1. Let w = λD/a. (B) = w, (A) = 2w, (D) = 3w, (C) = 2(2w) = 4w.
  2. Increasing: (B), (A), (D), (C).

Answer: option (4) — (B), (A), (D), (C)

Q862CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q42 · Prepp reconstructionworked here
Young's double slit experiment is performed using a source of white light.
A. The center fringe will be white.
B. The fringe next to the center fringe will be violet.
C. The fringe next to the center fringe will be red.
D. There will be no completely dark fringe.
E. The center fringe will be of no colour.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. C, D, E only
  2. A, B, D only
  3. A, C and D only
  4. B, C, D only
Concept to recallPath difference 0 at the centre for every λ ⇒ white central fringe. Moving out, the shortest wavelength reaches its first minimum first (at path difference λviolet/blue/2), so blue/violet drops out and the fringe beside the white one looks red (NCERT Ch 10).
  1. A true: every colour has its zero-order maximum at the centre.
  2. Just off the centre the path difference reaches λb/2 first, where blue is cancelled and red remains: the fringe next to the central one is red (NCERT: “the closest fringe on either side of the central white fringe is red and the farthest will appear blue”). C true, B false.
  3. D true: the minimum of one colour falls on maxima of others, so nothing is completely dark.
  4. E false: the central fringe is white, which is all colours, not “no colour”.

Answer: option (3) — A, C and D only

Trap“Violet is nearest” confuses the position of the first violet maximum with the colour actually seen next to the white fringe.
NotePrepp's unofficial key gives option (2); the working above shows why that cannot be right. That choice takes the neighbouring fringe as violet, contrary to NCERT's explicit statement.

Q865CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q14 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A telescope has an objective lens of 0.1 m diameter and is situated at a distance of 500 m from two objects. What will be the minimum distance between these two objects which can be resolved by the telescope. The mean wavelength of light is 600 nm.

Q868CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q49 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q876CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q24 · Prepp reconstructionworked here

  1. Parabolic

  3. Cylindrical

Q877CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q40 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. The angle of minimum deviation of a prism is greater for violet light than that for red light.
B. The purpose of microscopes and telescopes is to increase the visual angle.
C. For the diffraction to take place the size of aperture or of the obstacle should be comparable to the wavelength of light.
D. The light scattered in the direction of the incident light is always plane polarised.
E. The source and its virtual image can behave as a coherent sources.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, and C only
  2. A, B, C, D only
  3. A, B, C, E Only
  4. B, C, D, E Only
Concept to recallScattered sunlight is plane polarised at 90° to the incident direction, not along it. A source and its own image (Lloyd’s mirror) are coherent.
  1. A: μviolet > μred ⇒ larger δm — true.
  2. B: optical instruments enlarge the angle subtended at the eye — true. C: true.
  3. D: false (polarised at right angles, not forwards). E: true.

Answer: option (3) — A, B, C, E Only

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: polarisation.
Q878CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q44 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The intensity of light due to (see figure) interference of two waves (1) and (2) which have path difference of λ is: (where I0 = intensity of each wave)
  1. Zero
  2. I0
  3. 2I0
  4. 4I0
Concept to recallI = 4I0 cos2(φ/2), with φ = (2π/λ) × path difference.
  1. Path difference λ ⇒ φ = 2π (constructive).
  2. I = 4I0 cos2π = 4I0.

Answer: option (4) — 4I0

TrapAmplitudes add, not intensities: two equal waves in phase give 4I0, not 2I0.
Q879CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q45worked here
Two slits are kept 1 mm apart and the screen 1.0 m away. What is the fringe separation when blue-green light of wavelength 500 nm is used?
  1. 0.05 mm
  2. 0.5 mm
  3. 5.0 mm
  4. 50.0 mm
Concept to recallβ = λD/d.
  1. β = 500 × 10−9 × 1/10−3 = 5 × 10−4 m = 0.5 mm.

Answer: option (2) — 0.5 mm

Q880CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q7worked here
Three identical polaroid sheets P1, P2, P3 are oriented so that pass axis of P2 and P3 are inclined to P1 at 60° and 90° respectively. A monochromatic source of intensity I0 is used to pass through P1, P2, P3. Intensities after passing through P1, P2, P3 will be respectively:
A. I0, I0/2, I0/8B. I0/2, I0/8, I0/32
C. I0/2, I0/8, 3I0/32D. I0, I0/2, zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. C
  2. B
  3. D
  4. A
Concept to recallUnpolarised light through a polaroid: I/2. Polarised light through a polaroid at angle θ: I cos2θ (Malus).
  1. After P1: I0/2 (source unpolarised).
  2. After P2 (60° from P1): (I0/2)(1/4) = I0/8.
  3. P3 is 90° − 60° = 30° from P2: (I0/8)(3/4) = 3I0/32. That is list C.

Answer: option (1) — C

TrapZero after P3 would hold only without P2: the angle that matters is between P2 and P3, not P1 and P3.
NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: polarisation.
Q881CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q24 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In a Young double slit experiment, if one of the slits is covered with a black paper then:
  1. Fringe width of central maxima decreases
  2. Intensity of the central maxima increases
  3. Width of maxima decreases
  4. Diffraction pattern is observed on the screen
Concept to recallInterference needs two coherent sources; a single slit alone gives a single-slit diffraction pattern.
  1. With one slit blocked there is no second source: no interference fringes.
  2. The open slit produces its own diffraction pattern.

Answer: option (4) — Diffraction pattern is observed on the screen

Q882CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q6 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The distance estimation for which ray optics is good approximation for an aperture of 3 mm and wavelength 300 nm would be:
  1. 40 m
  2. 30 m
  3. 20 m
  4. 10 m
Concept to recallFresnel distance zF = a2/λ: ray optics holds up to about this distance.
  1. zF = (3 × 10−3)2/(300 × 10−9)
  2. = 9 × 10−6/3 × 10−7 = 30 m.

Answer: option (2) — 30 m

Q883CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q28key re-derived
Diameter of the objective lens of a telescope is 250 cm. For light of wavelength 600 nm, coming from a distant object, the limit of resolution of the telescope is close to:
  1. 1.5 × 10−7 rad
  2. 2 × 10−7 rad
  3. 3 × 10−7 rad
  4. 4.5 × 10−7 rad
Concept to recallLimit of resolution of a telescope Δθ = 1.22λ/D.

Q884CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q29key re-derived
A source emits sound of frequency 600 Hz inside water. The frequency heard in air (velocity of sound in water is 1500 m/s and velocity of sound in air is 300 m/s) will be:
  1. 300 Hz
  2. 600 Hz
  3. 900 Hz
  4. 1200 Hz
Concept to recallWhen a wave passes from one medium into another its frequency (set by the source) is unchanged; speed and wavelength change.
  1. Frequency stays 600 Hz; only λ = v/f changes (2.5 m in water, 0.5 m in air).

Answer: option (2) — 600 Hz

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: sound waves (Class 11). Filed under Wave Optics because the same rule governs refraction of light.
Q885CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q46key re-derived
In a double slit experiment, the distance between slits is increased 10 times whereas their distance from screen is halved, then what is the fringe width?
  1. it remains same

  3. become 1/20
  4. become 1/90
Concept to recallFringe width β = λD/d.
  1. β′ = λ(D/2)/(10d) = β/20.

Q886CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q7key re-derived
The two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities I and 4I are superposed. The maximum and minimum possible intensities in the resulting beams are:
  1. 5I and I
  2. 9I and I
  3. 5I and 3I
  4. 9I and 3I
Concept to recallAmplitudes add, not intensities: Imax = (√I1 + √I2)2, Imin = (√I1 − √I2)2.
  1. √I and √(4I) = 2√I.
  2. Imax = (3√I)2 = 9I; Imin = (√I)2 = I.

Trap5I is the incoherent sum (and the average of max and min).
Q887CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q29NTA final key
At what speed should a galaxy move with respect to earth so that spectral line of 600.0 nm appears as 600.6 nm ?
  1. 3 × 106 m s−1
  2. 3 × 105 m s−1
  3. 5 × 106 m s−1
  4. 5 × 105 m s−1
Concept to recallDoppler shift for light (v << c): Δλ/λ = v/c; a red shift means receding.
  1. Δλ/λ = 0.6/600 = 10−3.
  2. v = 10−3 × 3 × 108 = 3 × 105 m/s, moving away.

Q888CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q31NTA final key
Let us consider interference between two sources of intensities I and 4I. What will be the intensity at points where the phase difference is π ?
  1. I
  2. 5I
  3. 9I
  4. 0
Concept to recallI = I1 + I2 + 2√(I1I2) cosφ.
  1. cos π = −1: I = I + 4I − 2√(4I2) = 5I − 4I = I.
  2. Equivalently (√4I − √I)2 = I.

Trap9I is the maximum (phase difference 0).
Q889CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q32NTA final key
Two polaroid P1 and P3 are placed such that their pass-axis are mutually perpendicular. Another polaroid P2 is rotated between P1 and P3. For what angle θ between P1 and P2 the intensity of light emerging from P3 will be maximum ?
  1. π3
  2. π2
  3. π4
  4. π6
Concept to recallMalus: I = I0 cos2θ at each polaroid.
  1. After P1: I1. After P2: I1cos2θ. After P3 (at 90° − θ): I1cos2θ sin2θ.
  2. I = (I1/4) sin22θ, largest when 2θ = π/2: θ = π/4.

Answer: option (3) — π4

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: polarisation.
Q890CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q49NTA final key
A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength 460 nm passes through a long slit of width 0.1 mm. What is the angular divergence in which most of the light is diffracted ?
  1. 2.3 × 10−3 rad
  2. 4.6 × 10−3 rad
  3. 9.2 × 10−3 rad
  4. 9.2 × 10−6 rad
Concept to recallSingle slit: first minima at sinθ = ±λ/a; the central maximum spans 2λ/a.
  1. λ/a = 460 × 10−9/10−4 = 4.6 × 10−3 rad.
  2. Angular spread of the central maximum = 2λ/a = 9.2 × 10−3 rad.

Answer: option (3) — 9.2 × 10−3 rad

Trap4.6 × 10−3 rad is the half-width only.
Q891CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q26NTA final key
Which one of the following cannot be polarised?

Concept to recallOnly transverse waves can be polarised.

Q893CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q31NTA final key
A parallel beam of light of wavelength 500 nm is incident normally on a slit of width d. If the distance between slit and screen is 0.6 m and distance of second order minimum from the centre of the screen is 6.0 mm, What is the width of the slit?
  1. 0.1 mm
  2. 0.7 mm
  3. 0.2 mm
  4. 0.5 mm
Concept to recallSingle slit: nth minimum at yn = nλD/d.

Q894CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q32NTA final key
Two polaroids P1 and P2 are set in crossed positions. A third polaroid P3 is placed between the two making an angle α with the axis passing from the first polaroid P1, In what orientation will the transmitted intensity be maximum?
  1. π2
  2. π3
  3. π4
  4. 0
Concept to recallMalus: I = I0 cos2θ at each polaroid.

Q895CUET 2023 · 20 Jun, Shift 3 · Q47NTA final key
Two sitar stings A and B playing a note are slightly out of tune and produces beats of frequency 5 Hz. The tension in string B is slightly increased and beat frequency become 3 Hz. What is the original frequency of B if frequency of A is 427 Hz.
  1. 432 Hz
  2. 430 Hz
  3. 424 Hz
  4. 422 Hz
Concept to recallBeat frequency = |fA − fB|; raising tension raises f (f ∝ √T).
  1. fB = 427 ± 5 = 432 or 422 Hz.
  2. Raising fB reduced the beats to 3 Hz, so fB was below 427: 422 Hz (it becomes 424 Hz).

Answer: option (4) — 422 Hz

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: beats in sound (Class 11).
Q896CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q27NTA final key
A slit of width e is illuminated by light of wavelength λ. What should be the value of e to obtain the first maximum at an angle of diffraction of π3?
  1. 2√3λ
  2. λ√3
  3. √3λ
  4. √32λ
Concept to recallSingle slit: minima at e sin θ = nλ; secondary maxima at about e sin θ = (n + ½)λ.
  1. NTA’s key uses e sin θ = λ: e = λ/sin 60° = 2λ/√3.
  2. That is the condition for the first minimum. For the first secondary maximum, e sin 60° = 3λ/2 gives e = √3 λ (option 3).

Answer: option (1) — 2√3λ

NoteDisagreement with the key: NTA’s final key gives 2λ/√3, which is the first-minimum condition. For the first secondary maximum as worded, the NCERT condition e sin θ = 3λ/2 gives √3 λ. NTA’s answer is kept as published.
Q897CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q28NTA final key
In Young’s double slit experiment, yellow light of wavelength 640 nm produces fringes of width 0.8 mm. What will be the fringe width if the light source is replaced by another monochromatic source of wavelength 720 nm and the separation between the slits is made thrice ?

  2. 2.7 mm

Q898CUET 2023 · 2 Jul, Shift 3 · Q32NTA final key

Q899CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q41NTA final key
Case based. In Young’s experiment the two slits S1 and S2 are lit by one source S placed symmetrically, so the two waves leave them in phase, and any sudden phase change in S reaches both equally (they are coherent). Constructive and destructive interference give alternate bright and dark fringes of equal width on the screen, the central fringe at O being bright.

The phase difference (Δφ) between two super imposing waves to obtain constructive interference and hence bright band, is :
  1. Δφ = np ; n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  2. Δφ = 2np ; n = 0, 2, 3, 4, 5
  3. Δφ = nπ2 n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  4. Δφ = 3nπ2 n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Concept to recallBright fringe: Δφ = 2nπ (path difference nλ), n = 0, 1, 2, ...; dark: (2n − 1)π.
  1. Constructive interference needs Δφ = 0, 2π, 4π, ... = 2nπ.
  2. Option (2) is evidently meant to read 2nπ, but “p” is printed for π and n = 1 is missing from its list, so no option is right as printed.

No option is correct as printed — see the note.

NoteNTA dropped this question (ID 909441); every candidate got the marks. The intended answer is 2nπ.
Q900CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q42NTA final key
Case based. In Young’s experiment the two slits S1 and S2 are lit by one source S placed symmetrically, so the two waves leave them in phase, and any sudden phase change in S reaches both equally (they are coherent). Constructive and destructive interference give alternate bright and dark fringes of equal width on the screen, the central fringe at O being bright.

If two sources of intensifies I0 each have a randomly varying phase difference φ, the resultant intensity at centre of screen will be :
  1. I02
  2. 2I0
  3. 2 I0
  4. I0√2
Concept to recallI = I1 + I2 + 2√(I1I2) cosφ; for incoherent sources ⟨cosφ⟩ = 0.
  1. Randomly varying φ: the cosφ term averages to zero.
  2. I = I0 + I0 = 2I0; no fringes, uniform illumination.

Answer: option (3) — 2 I0

Trap4I0 would be the central maximum for coherent sources.
Q901CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q43NTA final key
Case based. In Young’s experiment the two slits S1 and S2 are lit by one source S placed symmetrically, so the two waves leave them in phase, and any sudden phase change in S reaches both equally (they are coherent). Constructive and destructive interference give alternate bright and dark fringes of equal width on the screen, the central fringe at O being bright.

In Young’s double slit experiment, interference pattern is obtained on the screen. If one of the slits is closed, then :
  1. Intensity and width of central maximum increase
  2. Intensity and width of central maximum decrease
  3. Intensity of central maximum decreases and while width of central maximum increases
  4. Intensity of central maximum increases and width of central maximum decreases
Concept to recallTwo slits: central bright intensity 4I0, fringe width λD/d. One slit: single-slit diffraction, central maximum I0 of width 2λD/a (a << d).
  1. Intensity at the centre drops from 4I0 to I0.
  2. The pattern becomes a single-slit diffraction pattern whose central maximum (2λD/a) is much wider than an interference fringe (λD/d).

Answer: option (3) — Intensity of central maximum decreases and while width of central maximum increases

Q902CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q44NTA final key
Case based. In Young’s experiment the two slits S1 and S2 are lit by one source S placed symmetrically, so the two waves leave them in phase, and any sudden phase change in S reaches both equally (they are coherent). Constructive and destructive interference give alternate bright and dark fringes of equal width on the screen, the central fringe at O being bright.

In Young’s double slit experiment, the separation between the slits is halved and distance between the slits and screen is doubled. The fringe width will be :
  1. unchanged
  2. halved
  3. doubled
  4. quadrupled
Concept to recallFringe width β = λD/d.
  1. β′ = λ(2D)/(d/2) = 4λD/d = 4β.

Answer: option (4) — quadrupled

Q903CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q45NTA final key
Case based. In Young’s experiment the two slits S1 and S2 are lit by one source S placed symmetrically, so the two waves leave them in phase, and any sudden phase change in S reaches both equally (they are coherent). Constructive and destructive interference give alternate bright and dark fringes of equal width on the screen, the central fringe at O being bright.

In Young’s double slit experiment, the fringe width is 0.4 mm. If the whole apparatus is immersed in water of refractive index 43, without changing its geometry, the new fringe width will be :
  1. 0.53 mm
  2. 0.4 mm
  3. 0.3 mm
  4. 540 μm
Concept to recallIn a medium λ′ = λ/n, so β′ = β/n.
  1. β′ = 0.4/(4/3) = 0.3 mm.

Answer: option (3) — 0.3 mm

TrapMultiplying by n gives 0.53 mm.

Q904CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q38 (NTA Q.No. 428)NTA final key

B. Na (Φ = 2.75 eV)

D. Ca (Φ = 3.2 eV)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, B, C, D
  2. D, C, B, A
  3. C, A, D, B
  4. C, A, B, D

Q906CUET 2026 · 24 May, Shift 2 · Q40 (NTA Q.No. 430)NTA final key

Q907CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q6key re-derived

Q916CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q41NTA final key
The photoelectric current is directly proportional to the number of photo electrons emitted per second. This implies that

  3. the number of photoelectrons emitted per second is directly proportional to the intensity of incident radiation.
  4. the number of photoelectrons emitted per second is not related to the intensity of incident radiation.
Concept to recallAbove threshold, photocurrent ∝ intensity: more photons per second eject more electrons per second.
  1. Intensity (at fixed ν) ∝ number of photons per second.
  2. Each absorbed photon ejects at most one electron, so electrons per second ∝ intensity.

Answer: option (3) — the number of photoelectrons emitted per second is directly proportional to the intensity of incident radiation.

Q917CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q42NTA final key

Q918CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q50NTA final key

Q919CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q3 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
In the context of the Photoelectric effect, identify the statements which support quantum nature of light.

  4. (D) There is a minimum frequency of light below which no photoelectrons are emitted

  3. (B), (C) and (D) only

Concept to recallThe three facts wave theory cannot explain: Kmax independent of intensity, a threshold frequency, and no time lag. Each follows from E = hν per photon.
  1. (B), (C), (D) are the classic photon evidence.
  2. (A) is about the electron’s charge, not about light.

Answer: option (3) — (B), (C) and (D) only

Q920CUET 2025 · 20 May, Shift 2 · Q4 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

Q922CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q2worked here

Q923CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q21worked here

Q939CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q680NTA final key
When photon of energy hν falls on a photosensitive metallic surface (work function hν0) electrons are emitted from the metallic surface. It is possible to say that :

Q940CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q15 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The anode voltage of a photocell is kept fixed. The wavelength λ of light falling on the cathode is gradually changed. The plate current I of the photocell varies as follows.
Concept to recallPhotoelectron energy falls as λ rises (Kmax = hc/λ − φ); beyond the threshold wavelength there is no emission at all.
  1. At short λ the electrons are energetic and most of them reach the anode.
  2. As λ increases their kinetic energy falls, fewer are collected against the fixed anode conditions, and the current falls.
  3. Towards the threshold wavelength the current dies away. Only graph (4) falls with λ.

Answer: option (4) —

NoteThis is the AIEEE 2006 question; the expected answer is the falling curve (4). Strictly, the current should reach zero at the threshold wavelength rather than approach the axis asymptotically.

  2. B and E only
  3. D and E only

Concept to recallStopping potential V0: eV0 = Kmax = hν − φ — depends on frequency, not intensity.

  3. C and D true.

Answer: option (1) — C & D only

Q942CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q24 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Concept to recalleV0 = hν − φ.

Q943CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q27 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The figure shows the variation of photo current with anode potential for a photo-sensitive surface for three different radiations. Let Ia, Ib and Ic be the intensities and νa, νb, and νc be the frequencies for the curves a, b and c respectively. Choose the correct statement.

Q954CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q27 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q969CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q35NTA final key

Concept to recallThe (saturation) photocurrent depends on intensity, not on frequency or wavelength (for λ below the threshold).

  1. (A), (B) and (D) only

  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallEn = −13.6/n2 eV.
  1. (A) n = 1 has the most negative energy. True.
  2. (B) gaps ∝ 1/n2 − 1/(n+1)2 shrink. True.
  3. (C) definition of ionisation energy. True.
  4. (D) energy to free from level n is 13.6/n2, which falls with n. True.

Answer: option (3) — (A), (B), (C) and (D)

Q994CUET 2025 · 23 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q6worked here
The ratio for the speed of the electron in the 3rd orbit of He+ to the speed of the electron in the 3rd orbit of the hydrogen atom will be
  1. 4:1
  2. 2:1
  3. 1:2
  4. 1:4
Concept to recallBohr: vn = (2.19 × 106 m/s) Z/n.
  1. Same n, so v ∝ Z.
  2. Z(He+) = 2, Z(H) = 1: ratio 2 : 1.

Answer: option (2) — 2:1

Trap4 : 1 is the ratio of the energies (∝ Z2), not the speeds.
Q995CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q13worked here
The ratio of total energy of an electron in 3rd orbit to that in 5th orbit in a hydrogen atom is:
  1. 9 : 25
  2. 25 : 9
  3. 3 : 5
  4. 5 : 3
Concept to recallEn ∝ −1/n2.
  1. E3/E5 = 52/32 = 25 : 9.

Answer: option (2) — 25 : 9

Trap9 : 25 is the ratio of the orbit radii (∝ n2).
Q996CUET 2025 · 26 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q49worked here
When an α-particle of mass M moving with velocity v bombards a heavy nucleus of charge Ze, its distance of closest approach from the nucleus depends on M as
  1. Independent of M
  2. ∝ 1/M2
  3. ∝ 1/M
  4. ∝ 1/√M
Concept to recallAt closest approach all KE becomes PE: ½Mv2 = k(2e)(Ze)/r0.
  1. r0 = 4kZe2/(Mv2).
  2. At fixed v, r0 ∝ 1/M.

Answer: option (3) — ∝ 1/M

Q997CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q31 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
Identify the correct statement in the context of Rutherford scattering of α-particles by a target nucleus:
  1. For large impact parameter values, α-particle suffers large deviation.
  2. For small impact parameter values, the deviation in the trajectory of α-particle is negligible.
  3. The perpendicular distance of the initial velocity vector of the α-particle from the centre of the nucleus is called impact parameter.
  4. Impact parameter depends on mass of the target nucleus.
Concept to recallImpact parameter b = perpendicular distance of the initial velocity line from the nucleus; small b ⇒ large scattering angle.
  1. The first two statements are reversed: head-on (b ≈ 0) gives the largest deflection.
  2. b is a geometric property of the incoming path, not of the target’s mass. The third statement is the definition.

Answer: option (3) — The perpendicular distance of the initial velocity vector of the α-particle from the centre of the nucleus is called impact parameter.

Q998CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q38 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
What will be the energy required to remove the electron from the first excited state of Li++, if the ground state energy of the electron in a hydrogen atom is −13.6 eV?
  1. 7.65 eV
  2. 10.4 eV
  3. 13.6 eV
  4. 30.6 eV
Concept to recallHydrogen-like ion: En = −13.6 Z2/n2 eV.
  1. Li++: Z = 3; first excited state n = 2.
  2. E2 = −13.6 × 9/4 = −30.6 eV.
  3. Energy to remove the electron = 30.6 eV.

Answer: option (4) — 30.6 eV

Q999CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q5 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
The ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy of an electron in a Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom is
  1. 1:1
  2. 1:−2
  3. −1:1
  4. 2:−1
Concept to recallIn a Bohr orbit K = −E and U = 2E (U = −2K).
  1. E = K + U = K − 2K = −K.
  2. E : K = −1 : 1.

Answer: option (3) — −1:1

Q1000CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q26NTA final key
The kinetic energy of an electron in ground level in hydrogen atom is K units. The values of its potential energy and total energy respectively are ____________.
  1. −2K; −K
  2. +2K; −K
  3. −K; +2K
  4. +K; +2K
Concept to recallBohr orbit (inverse-square force): U = −2K, E = K + U = −K.
  1. mv2/r = ke2/r2 ⇒ K = ke2/2r, U = −ke2/r = −2K.
  2. E = K − 2K = −K.

Answer: option (1) — −2K; −K

Q1001CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q28NTA final key
The shortest wavelengths emitted in hydrogen spectrum corresponding to different spectral series are as under :

The wavelengths arranged correctly in decreasing order are ____________.
  1. (A), (B), (C), (D)
  2. (A), (C), (B), (D)
  3. (B), (A), (D), (C)
  4. (A), (C), (D), (B)
Concept to recallSeries limit (shortest λ): 1/λ = R/n12, so λmin ∝ n12.
  1. n1: Lyman 1, Balmer 2, Brackett 4, Pfund 5.
  2. Decreasing λmin: Pfund, Brackett, Balmer, Lyman = (A), (C), (B), (D).

Answer: option (2) — (A), (C), (B), (D)

Q1002CUET 2024 · 16 May (pen & paper) · Sets A–D · Set A Q48NTA final key
According to Bohr’s Model
(A) The radius of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to ‘n’.
(B) The speed of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to ‘1/n’.
(C) The magnitude of the total energy of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to ‘1/n2’.
(D) The radius of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to ‘n2’.
  1. (A), (B) and (C) only
  2. (A), (B) and (D) only
  3. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  4. (B), (C) and (D) only
Concept to recallBohr (hydrogen-like): rn ∝ n2/Z, vn ∝ Z/n, En ∝ −Z2/n2.
  1. r ∝ n2 (D true, A false); v ∝ 1/n (B true); |E| ∝ 1/n2 (C true).

Answer: option (4) — (B), (C) and (D) only

Q1003CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q640NTA final key
Magnetic moment due to the motion of the electron in nth energy state of hydrogen atom is proportional to :
  1. n
  2. n2
  3. n3
  4. n0
Concept to recallOrbital magnetic moment μ = (e/2m)L, and Bohr’s rule L = nh/2π.
  1. μ = iA = (ev/2πr)(πr2) = evr/2 = (e/2m)(mvr).
  2. mvr = nh/2π ⇒ μ = n(eh/4πm) ∝ n.

Answer: option (1) — n

Q1004CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q641NTA final key
Energy levels A, B, C of a certain atom corresponds to increasing value of energy EA < EB < EC. If λ1, λ2, λ3 are the wavelengths of radiation corresponding to the transitions C → B, B → A and C → A respectively then :
  1. λ3 = λ1 + λ2
  2. λ1 = λ2 = λ3
  3. λ32 = λ12 + λ22
  4. λ3 = λ1λ2λ1 + λ2
Concept to recallPhoton energies add (E = hc/λ), wavelengths do not.
  1. hc/λ3 = hc/λ1 + hc/λ2.
  2. 1/λ3 = 1/λ1 + 1/λ2 ⇒ λ3 = λ1λ2/(λ1 + λ2).

Answer: option (4) — λ3 = λ1λ2λ1 + λ2

Q1005CUET 2024 · 19 Jul (re-test, CBT) · Q677NTA final key
Consider the following particles :
(A) Proton   (B) α particle   (C) Electron
For charge to mass ratio of the above particles we can say :
  1. (C) > (A) > (B)
  2. (A) < (C) < (B)
  3. (B) = (A) > (C)
  4. (C) = (B) > (A)
Concept to recallq/m: electron e/me; proton e/mp; alpha 2e/(4mp) = ½(e/mp).
  1. me ≪ mp, so the electron’s ratio is largest; the alpha’s is half the proton’s.
  2. (C) > (A) > (B).

Answer: option (1) — (C) > (A) > (B)

  2. 6566 Å
  3. 3648 Å
  4. 14592 Å
Concept to recallSeries limit (n2 → ∞): 1/λ = R/n12, so λmin ∝ n12.
  1. Lyman (n1 = 1): λmin = 1/R = 912 Å.
  2. Paschen (n1 = 3): λmin = 9/R = 9 × 912 = 8208 Å.

Answer: option (1) — 8208 Å

Trap3648 Å (= 4 × 912) is the Balmer limit.
NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: hydrogen spectral series worked quantitatively (the syllabus treats line spectra qualitatively only).
Q1032CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q28NTA final key
The ratio maximum wavelength to minimum wavelength in Lyman series is :
  1. 43
  2. 34
  3. 13
  4. 14
Concept to recallLyman: 1/λ = R(1 − 1/n2). Longest λ: n = 2; shortest: n = ∞.
  1. λmax: 1/λ = R(3/4) ⇒ λmax = 4/(3R).
  2. λmin = 1/R.
  3. Ratio = 4/3.

Answer: option (1) — 43

If 200 MeV energy is released in the fission of a single nucleus of 23592U, how many fissions per second must occur to produce a power of 1 kW?

  3. 4.251 × 1013

Q1036CUET 2026 · 14 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q1 also 2026 18 May S1 Q1 (memory-based, collegedunia); 2026 18 May S2 Q1 (memory-based, collegedunia) (site key there printed 6 and 8)key re-derived

  2. 8 and 6
  3. 6 and 8

Concept to recallα lowers A by 4 and Z by 2; β− leaves A alone and raises Z by 1. Count α from A first.

Q1039CUET 2026 · 31 May, Shift 2 · memory-based (collegedunia) · Q10key re-derived

Q1042CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q43NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct?
  1. (A) A nucleus of mass number A has a radius R given by the expression R = R0A1/3
  2. (B) Volume of nucleus is proportional to mass number A
  3. (C) The density of nucleus increases with the radius of nucleus.
  4. (D) Density of nuclear matter does not depend on its mass number A
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A), (B) and (C) only
  2. (A), (B), (C) and (D)
  3. (A) (B) and (D) only
  4. (B) and (C) only
Concept to recallR = R0A1/3 ⇒ V ∝ R3 ∝ A ⇒ density ∝ A/V is constant (≈ 2.3 × 1017 kg m−3).
  1. (A) true (empirical).
  2. (B) true: V = (4/3)πR03A.
  3. (C) false and (D) true: mass ∝ A and volume ∝ A, so density is the same for all nuclei.

Answer: option (3) — (A) (B) and (D) only

Q1043CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q45NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct?
  1. (A) The electrostatic repulsive force between the protons can be greater than the nuclear force to bind the nucleons together inside a nucleus.
  2. (B) The repulsive electrostatic force between protons in smaller nuclei is much smaller than the nuclear force between nucleons inside a nucleus.
  3. (C) The gravitational force between nucleons is much smaller than the nuclear force between the nucleons inside a nucleus.
  4. (D) The binding energy per nucleon between nucleons is almost constant because the nuclear force is a long range force.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. (A) and (D) only
  2. (B) and (C) only
  3. (C) and (D) only
  4. (A) only
Concept to recallNuclear force: strongest of the three, short range (~ fm), charge independent; it saturates, which is why B.E./A is nearly constant.
  1. (A) false: in a bound nucleus the attractive nuclear force must win over the repulsion.
  2. (B) true for light nuclei. (C) true: gravity is ~10−38 times weaker.
  3. (D) false: B.E./A is nearly constant because the force is short range (saturation).

Answer: option (2) — (B) and (C) only

Q1044CUET 2025 · 13 May, Shift 2 · Q49NTA final key
In the following nuclear reaction, 10n + 23592U → 14054Xe + abSr + 2 10n we have
  1. a = 38, b = 94
  2. a = 94, b = 38
  3. a = 94, b = 40
  4. a = 96, b = 38
Concept to recallIn a nuclear reaction both the mass number (upper index) and the charge number (lower index) are conserved.
  1. Mass numbers: 1 + 235 = 140 + a + 2 ⇒ a = 94.
  2. Charge numbers: 0 + 92 = 54 + b + 0 ⇒ b = 38 (strontium is element 38).

Answer: option (2) — a = 94, b = 38

TrapSwapping the indices gives a = 38, b = 94; the upper index is the mass number.
NoteCollegedunia’s typed copy marks a = 38, b = 94; NTA’s final key and the conservation laws give a = 94, b = 38.

Q1066CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q7 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
When we draw the variation of the potential energy of a pair of nucleons with their separations, then
  1. the force is attractive when separation between them is greater than 0.8 fm

  3. the force is attractive when separation between them is less than 0.8 fm

Concept to recallF = −dU/dr. Where U rises as r grows (beyond the minimum at r0 ≈ 0.8 fm) the force is attractive; inside r0 it is strongly repulsive.
  1. The minimum of U is at r0 ≈ 0.8 fm.
  2. For r > 0.8 fm, dU/dr > 0 ⇒ F < 0: attraction (up to ~2–3 fm).
  3. For r < 0.8 fm the force is repulsive.

Answer: option (1) — the force is attractive when separation between them is greater than 0.8 fm

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. C and D only
  2. A and B only
  3. B and D only
  4. B and C only
Concept to recallEnergy is released when the products are more tightly bound, i.e. higher on the BE/N curve: fusion of light nuclei (left of the peak) and fission of heavy nuclei (right of the peak).
  1. B: heavy F splits into D and E, both higher on the curve ⇒ Q > 0 (fission).
  2. C: light A and B fuse into C, which is higher ⇒ Q > 0 (fusion).
  3. A (C breaking into lighter A, B) and D (D, E fusing into heavy F) go downhill ⇒ Q < 0.

Answer: option (4) — B and C only

NoteRepaired. Prepp prints reaction C as “C + A → C + Q”, which cannot balance (A’s nucleons vanish). The intended reaction is the fusion A + B → C + Q, the mirror of reaction A; with it, option (4) is the standard answer, and no option is correct without it.

Q1104CUET 2025 · 21 May, Shift 2 · dubuddy re-typeset · Q31worked here

Q1113CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q23 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here

List-I (Electronic Device)List-II (Function)

D. TransformerIV. Used to remove any ripple in the rectified output voltage

Q1115CUET 2025 · 27 May, Shift 2 · Q8 (dubuddy re-typeset)worked here
A given p-n junction is forward biased. Which of the following statements is correct?

  2. The height of potential barrier is increased.
  3. The height of potential barrier is decreased.
  4. The width of depletion region increases.
Concept to recallForward bias opposes the built-in field: barrier height and depletion width both decrease.

  2. Majority electrons cross from n to p (not p to n); the depletion region narrows.

Q1123CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q20 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In a p-n junction under equilibrium:
  1. Diffusion current dominates
  2. Drift current dominates
  3. No net current flows
  4. Depending upon the semiconductor either diffusion current or drift current dominates.
Concept to recallAt equilibrium the diffusion current is exactly balanced by the opposite drift current.
  1. The barrier builds up until drift = diffusion, so the net current is zero.

Answer: option (3) — No net current flows

Q1124CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q23 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  1. It contains few ions as charge carriers.
  2. It has few holes as charge carriers.
  3. It has no charge carriers.
  4. It contains few electrons as charge carriers.
Concept to recallThe depletion region is emptied of mobile carriers; only fixed (immobile) ions remain.
  1. No free electrons or holes ⇒ it behaves as an insulator. The ions there are fixed and do not carry current.

Answer: option (3) — It has no charge carriers.

Q1125CUET 2023 · 21 May, Shift 3 · Q39 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Q1126CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q2 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
In a feedback amplifier, if the feedback voltage is in opposite phase, the gain is less than 1. Then it will:
  1. Never work as an Oscillator
  2. Work as an Oscillator
  3. Not work as an Oscillator
  4. Work as a rectifier
Concept to recallBarkhausen criterion: an oscillator needs positive (in-phase) feedback with loop gain ≥ 1.
  1. Feedback in opposite phase is negative feedback, and the gain is below 1: the condition for sustained oscillation is never met.

Q1128CUET 2023 · 22 May, Shift 2 · Q26 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

  2. NOT gate only
  3. OR gate only
  4. NAND gate only
Concept to recallNAND and NOR are universal gates: any gate can be built from either alone.
  1. NAND: AND = NAND followed by a NAND used as NOT.
  2. NOR: AND = NOR of (A NOR A) and (B NOR B), since (A′ + B′)′ = AB.

Answer: option (1) — Both NAND gate and NOR gate

Q1138CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q2 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived

Answer: option (2) — Decreases

Q1139CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q22 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
A semiconductor device is connected in series circuit with a battery and resistance. A current is found to pass through the circuit. If the polarity of the battery is reversed, the current drops to almost zero. The device may be
  1. A p-type semiconductor
  2. An intrinsic semiconductor
  3. An n-type semiconductor
  4. a p-n junction
Concept to recallOnly a p-n junction conducts one way (forward bias) and blocks the other (reverse bias: tiny leakage current).
  1. A plain p-type, n-type or intrinsic piece conducts equally either way (it is just a resistor).
  2. Rectifying behaviour ⇒ p-n junction diode.

Answer: option (4) — a p-n junction

Q1140CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q28 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
For insulators and semiconductors, the resistance decreases with increase in temperature because
  1. number density decreases
  2. number density of charge carriers increases
  3. Resistivity does not depend upon the temperature
  4. Resistivity does not depend upon the number density of Charge carriers
Concept to recallρ = m/(ne2τ). In semiconductors n rises steeply with T (more electrons cross the gap), outweighing the fall in τ.
  1. Heating breaks covalent bonds: more electrons and holes.
  2. Larger n ⇒ smaller ρ.

Answer: option (2) — number density of charge carriers increases

Q1141CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q32 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
I-V characteristics of solar cell is drawn in the fourth quadrant. The reason is
  1. Solar cells does not draw current and supplies the same to the load.
  2. Solar cell draws the current and does not supply.
  3. Solar cell does not supply the current.
  4. Solar cell only store the light energy.
Concept to recallA solar cell is a source: current flows out of it into the load, opposite to a forward-biased diode’s current, so I is negative while V is positive.
  1. Photocurrent flows from n to p inside the cell (reverse direction) while the terminal voltage is forward.
  2. So the cell supplies current rather than drawing it: fourth quadrant.

Answer: option (1) — Solar cells does not draw current and supplies the same to the load.

Q1142CUET 2023 · 25 May, Shift 3 · Q48 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Match List-I with List-II
List-IList-II
(A) NAND Gate(I)
(B) NOR Gate(II)
(C) NOT Gate(III)
(D) OR Gate(IV)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

  3. (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
  4. (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Concept to recallThe bubble means NOT: AND-shape + bubble = NAND, OR-shape + bubble = NOR; a triangle with a bubble is NOT.
  1. (I) curved OR body with a bubble: NOR. (II) OR body, no bubble: OR.
  2. (III) D-shaped AND body with a bubble: NAND. (IV) triangle with bubble: NOT.
  3. A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: option (4) — (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

Q1143CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q13worked here
In a transistor:
A. one of the outer layers is heavily doped and is called collector
B. one of the outer layers is heavily doped and is called emitter
C. the middle layer is very lightly doped and is called base
D. one of the outer layer is moderately doped and is called emitter
E. one of the outer layer is moderately doped and is called collector
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A, C and D only
  2. B, C and E only
  3. C, D and E only
  4. A, C and E only
Concept to recallEmitter: heavily doped, moderate size (supplies carriers). Base: very thin, lightly doped. Collector: moderately doped, largest (collects carriers).
  1. B (emitter heavily doped), C (base lightly doped) and E (collector moderately doped) are true; A and D swap the roles.

Answer: option (2) — B, C and E only

Q1144CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q21worked here
Match List – I with List – II.

List – II: the gate symbols I–IV below.Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
  1. A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
  2. A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
  3. A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
  4. A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
Concept to recallD-shaped body = AND, curved (shield) body = OR; a bubble at the output inverts (NAND, NOR).
  1. I: OR body with bubble = NOR; II: AND body = AND; III: AND body with bubble = NAND; IV: OR body = OR.
  2. NAND → III, OR → IV, NOR → I, AND → II.

Q1145CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q25worked here
In a half wave rectifier, the frequency of the output is:
  1. half the frequency of input
  2. same as that of input
  3. twice the frequency of input
  4. Zero
Concept to recallHalf-wave: one output pulse per input cycle (ripple frequency f). Full-wave: two pulses per cycle (2f).
  1. Only the positive half of each cycle passes, so the pulses repeat at the input frequency.

Answer: option (2) — same as that of input

TrapTwice the input frequency is the full-wave rectifier.
Q1146CUET 2023 · 26 May, Shift 1 · Prepp reconstruction · Q44worked here
In the depletion layer of a reverse biased p-n junction, the:
  1. potential is zero
  2. potential is maximum
  3. drift current is zero
  4. electric field is zero
Concept to recallReverse bias widens the depletion layer and raises the barrier potential (V0 + V); a strong field exists across it and a small drift (reverse saturation) current flows.
  1. The field across the depletion layer is strong, not zero, and the reverse current is a drift current, so it is not zero.
  2. The potential barrier across the layer is at its largest under reverse bias.

Answer: option (2) — potential is maximum

NotePrepp gives no key for this paper. Three options are plainly false; “potential is maximum” is the intended answer.
Q1147CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q10 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Let iE, iC and iB represent the emitter current, collector current and the base current respectively in a transistor. Choose the correct statement from the following.
  1. iC is slightly greater than iE
  2. iB is much greater than iE
  3. iC is equal to iB
  4. iE is equal to the sum of iC and iB
Concept to recallKirchhoff’s junction rule on the transistor: iE = iB + iC, with iB only a few per cent of iE.
  1. Charge entering at the emitter leaves via base and collector.
  2. iE = iC + iB; iC is slightly less than iE.

Answer: option (4) — iE is equal to the sum of iC and iB

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: transistors.
Q1148CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q14 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
What is the value of Vo if the silicon diode starts conducting at 0.7 V while the Germanium starts conducting at 0.3 V?
  1. 11 V
  2. 12 V
  3. 11.7 V
  4. 11.3 V
Concept to recallTwo forward-biased diodes in parallel: the one with the lower knee voltage turns on first and clamps the voltage across both.
  1. Ge conducts at 0.3 V, fixing the drop across the pair at 0.3 V; Si (needs 0.7 V) stays off.
  2. Vo = 12 − 0.3 = 11.7 V.

Answer: option (3) — 11.7 V

Trap11.3 V treats the Si diode as the one conducting.
Q1149CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q18 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
The logic circuit performs the logic function of:
  1. AND
  2. NAND
  3. OR
  4. NOR
Concept to recallA NOR gate with its inputs tied together acts as a NOT gate; NOT(NOR) = OR.
  1. Y′ = NOT(A + B).
  2. Second gate: Y = NOT(Y′ + Y′) = NOT Y′ = A + B.
  3. OR.

Answer: option (3) — OR

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: logic gates.
Q1150CUET 2023 · 30 May, Shift 1 · Q20 · Prepp reconstructionkey re-derived
Which of the following causes electric conduction in a semiconductor?
  1. Holes only
  2. Electrons only
  3. Both electrons and holes
  4. Neither holes nor electrons
Concept to recallIn a semiconductor both free electrons (conduction band) and holes (valence band) carry current.
  1. Breaking a bond frees an electron and leaves a hole; both move in a field.
  2. Current = electron current + hole current.

Answer: option (3) — Both electrons and holes

Q1151CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q22key re-derived
An a.c. source of 200 V is connected through a diode ‘D’ to a capacitor as shown in figure. Find the maximum potential difference across the capacitor:
  1. 100 V
  2. 200 V
  3. 283 V
  4. 310 V
Concept to recallAC voltages are quoted as rms; peak V0 = √2 Vrms. A diode–capacitor (peak detector) charges C to V0.
  1. V0 = 200√2 = 283 V.
  2. The diode conducts until C reaches the peak, then is reverse biased, so C holds 283 V.

Answer: option (3) — 283 V

Q1152CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q23key re-derived
The electrical conductivity of a semiconductor increases when electromagnetic radiation of wavelength shorter than 2480 nm is incident on it. The band gap for the semiconductor is:
  1. 0.5 eV
  2. 0.7 eV
  3. 0.9 eV
  4. 1.1 eV
Concept to recallA photon can lift an electron across the gap only if hc/λ ≥ Eg; the threshold wavelength gives Eg = 1240/λ(nm) eV.
  1. Eg = 1240/2480 = 0.5 eV.

Answer: option (1) — 0.5 eV

Q1153CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q24key re-derived
Energy gap between valence band and conduction band of a semiconductor is approximately:
  1. zero
  2. 4 eV
  3. 1 eV
  4. 10 eV
Concept to recallMetals: overlapping bands (gap 0). Semiconductors: Eg < 3 eV (Si 1.1 eV, Ge 0.7 eV). Insulators: Eg > 3 eV (diamond 5.4 eV).
  1. Typical semiconductor gaps are about 1 eV.

Answer: option (3) — 1 eV

Q1154CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q26key re-derived
The given combination represents the following gate:
  1. OR
  2. XOR
  3. NAND
  4. NOR
Concept to recallA NAND with its inputs tied is a NOT gate. NAND of two inverted inputs: (A′B′)′ = A + B (De Morgan).
  1. First stage gives A′ and B′.
  2. Y = (A′·B′)′ = A + B: an OR gate.

Answer: option (1) — OR

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: logic gates.
Q1155CUET 2023 · 09 Jun, Shift 3 · Prepp reconstruction · Q40key re-derived
A piece of copper and another of germanium are cooled from room temperature to 100 K. The resistance of:
  1. copper increases and germanium decreases
  2. copper decreases and germanium increases
  3. each of them increases
  4. each of them decreases
Concept to recallMetals: positive temperature coefficient (fewer collisions when cold). Semiconductors: negative (fewer carriers excited across the gap when cold).
  1. Copper (metal): R falls on cooling.
  2. Germanium (semiconductor): carrier density falls, so R rises.

Answer: option (2) — copper decreases and germanium increases

Q1156CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q40NTA final key
Energy band gap is maximum in :

  2. semi-conductor
  3. super conductor
  4. insulator

Q1157CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q41NTA final key
The forbidden energy gaps in conductors, semiconductors and insulators are (Eg)c, (Eg)s and (Eg)I respectively. What is the relation among them ?
  1. (Eg)c < (Eg)s < (Eg)I
  2. (Eg)c > (Eg)s > (Eg)I
  3. (Eg)c < (Eg)s > (Eg)I
  4. (Eg)c = (Eg)s > (Eg)I
Concept to recallBand gap: conductor (0) < semiconductor (< 3 eV) < insulator (> 3 eV).
  1. Conductors have no gap, semiconductors a small one, insulators a large one.

Answer: option (1) — (Eg)c < (Eg)s < (Eg)I

Q1158CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q42NTA final key
Which of the following statements are correct for a transistor action ?
(A) The input resistance depends upon the current Ic in the transistor
(B) Collector currents is equal to the sum of base current and emitter current
(C) The emitter junction is forward biased
(D) The collector junction is reverse biased
(E) Both the emitter junction as well as the collector junction are forward biased
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A), (B) and (C) only
  2. (B), (C) and (D) only
  3. (C), (D) and (E) only
  4. (A) and (C) only
Concept to recallActive region (amplifier): emitter–base forward biased, collector–base reverse biased; IE = IB + IC.
  1. (B) false: it is the emitter current that is the sum, IE = IB + IC.
  2. (E) false in transistor (amplifying) action. (C) true.
  3. (A): input resistance ΔVBE/ΔIB varies with the operating current (the input characteristic is non-linear).
  4. Of the printed choices only (A) and (C) contains no false statement.

Answer: option (4) — (A) and (C) only

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: transistors. (D) is also true, but no option offers (C) and (D) together; NTA’s key is option (4).
Q1159CUET 2023 · 15 Jun, Shift 2 · Q43NTA final key
The logic gate realised using p-n junction diodes in the given figure is :
  1. OR gate
  2. NOT gate
  3. AND gate
  4. NAND gate
Concept to recallDiodes from each input to a common output resistor: any HIGH input forward-biases its diode and pulls y HIGH.

  2. Either input HIGH: that diode conducts and y is HIGH.
  3. y = A + B: OR gate.

Q1173CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q30NTA final key
When a forward bias is applied to a p-n junction diode, then :

Concept to recallForward bias opposes the barrier: barrier height and depletion width shrink, majority current rises.
  1. The applied field opposes the junction field: barrier lowered, depletion layer narrows.
  2. Majority carriers cross easily, so the junction resistance falls.

Answer: option (4) — The width of depletion layer reduces

(D) (IV) Photo diode
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
  1. (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)
  2. (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (I), (D) - (IV)
  3. (A) - (III), (B) - (II), (C) - (I), (D) - (IV)
  4. (A) - (III), (B) - (II), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)
Concept to recallWhere each device works: LED forward bias (1st quadrant); Zener reverse breakdown (sharp fall in 3rd); photodiode reverse bias (3rd quadrant, current set by light); solar cell no bias, 4th quadrant (V > 0, I < 0).
  1. (A) forward exponential rise: LED (II).
  2. (B) flat, then a sharp reverse breakdown: Zener (III).
  3. (C) reverse current that does not depend on V: photodiode (IV).
  4. (D) curve in the fourth quadrant, delivering power: solar cell (I).

Answer: option (1) — (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (IV), (D) - (I)

NoteNot in the CUET 2026 syllabus. Topic: special-purpose diodes (Zener, LED, photodiode, solar cell).
Q1177CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q34NTA final key
Choose the logic operation carried out by the following current :
  1. OR Gate
  2. AND Gate
  3. NAND Gate
  4. NOR Gate
Concept to recallA NOR gate with its inputs tied together is a NOT gate. De Morgan: (A′ + B′)′ = A·B.
  1. First gates: (A + A)′ = A′ and (B + B)′ = B′.
  2. Last gate: Y = (A′ + B′)′ = A·B, an AND gate.
    ABA′B′Y
    00110
    01100
    10010
    11001

Answer: option (2) — AND Gate

Q1178CUET 2022 · 18 Aug, Shift 2 (PHY17) · Q35NTA final key
The process of superimposing message signal with the carrier wave is known as :
  1. demodulation
  2. attenuation
  3. modulation
  4. detection
Concept to recallModulation: the message changes a property (amplitude, frequency) of a high-frequency carrier. Demodulation/detection recovers it; attenuation is loss of strength.
  1. Impressing the message on the carrier is modulation.

Answer: option (3) — modulation

(A) Receiver
(B) Information source
(C) Channel

(E) Transmitter

  3. (C), (A), (E), (B), (D)
  4. (D), (E), (C), (A), (B)
